text:
NFTs could make their next comeback as identities for AI agents.

> an agent you can discover.
> an agent whose work you can inspect.
> an agent with a reputation that follows it across applications.

NFTs paired with tokens, new trading rules, and added utility are interesting.

but i still see those as early experiments.

the bigger idea starts when you think of NFTs as identities for software that actually does useful work.

and for CT, useful often means helping people find opportunities, save time, or avoid losing money.

imagine an AIXBT-style research agent with a public record attached to its identity.

it tracks wallets.
studies token launches.
flags changes in liquidity.
publishes research with sources.

but now you can look beyond its latest viral post.

what did it say before the move?
how often was it wrong?
did its results survive fees and slippage?
are people actually paying to use it?

that is where things get interesting.
there is a proposed Ethereum standard called ERC-8004, currently in draft.

it gives agents an NFT-based identity and provides registries for reputation feedback and independent validation.

the agent itself can still run offchain.

the onchain part gives applications a common way to identify it and inspect recorded signals about its work.
now imagine a marketplace where you compare agents by their actual service history.

one is good at researching new protocols.
another monitors treasury risks.
another finds execution routes.
another checks the first agent’s work.
you could hire them based on evidence.

other agents could do the same.

a research agent hires a data agent.
an execution agent checks with a risk agent.
each service builds a history around a recognizable identity.

payments and task settlement would need separate infrastructure, but the identity gives those interactions a consistent reference.

the next layer could be businesses built around these agents.

paid research.
monitoring subscriptions.
specialized APIs.
automated services that customers keep coming back to.

but there is a question every NFT buyer should ask:

what exactly do i own?
the agent’s registration?
access to its service?
control of its operation?
a contractual share of revenue?

those are different things.
buying an identity NFT does not automatically hand you the model, servers, customer relationships, or earnings.

and reputation needs scrutiny too.

fake accounts can manufacture positive feedback. an onchain rating is only useful when you understand who submitted it and what evidence supports it.

my thesis is that the market could wake up to this when an agent shows useful, repeatable results that people will pay for.

then we could see a new narrative around “8004 agents” or “onchain agents.”

the opportunity i’m watching is where a working product, credible performance history, and clearly defined ownership come together.

a low floor price alone tells me very little.

a cheap NFT can still lose its entire value, and an agent’s success might never flow to its holders.

but an agent with real customers, useful output, and meaningful rights attached to ownership?

that is worth researching.

the next NFT people care about could be the identity of a service they use every day.

text:
I think Justin Drake's latest alarmism/vagueposting is going to do a ton of damage in multiple ways. It's basically a huge self-own for their own advocacy work on quantum stuff.

Threats from quantum/AI are real, and teams throughout this industry are making considered decisions about how to respond to those risks in a practical way, and to help their users navigate the uncertainty. 

Some of those teams have really good cryptographers with an excellent grasp on the decisions they can make, others have to take their cues from trusted experts. There are so many dimensions to optimize along! And due to the complexity involved, it's almost impossible to explain this stuff to non-cryptographers.

Experts have to be cognizant of all this, and of their responsibility to be levelheaded.

After the fog clears up and people learn from their cryptographer friends what is actually going on, they're going to discover this was (at best) an unintentional marketing stunt and a lot of trust will be lost. And nobody will really know what to do...

This is a shame, because they are directionally correct. It actually meant something when they sounded the alarm before. They've just gradually descended into unhinged predictions without feedback to discourage it.

Can anyone, I mean seriously anyone, justify this debacle? It permanently colors all the legitimate concerns/predictions about classical crypto going forward. By their own admission, there was no new information that drove this. I think Justin Drake should explain how he thought this was the right approach, even if he genuinely believed what he was saying. 

Baffling.

text:
Robinhood 这条消息的核心，是想把传统资管公司“主动选股”的产品，也做成链上代币。
目前 Robinhood Chain 上已有的 Stock Token，主要是给个股或被动 ETF（比如跟踪标普500的基金）做价格映射。这些代币是泽西岛实体发行的债务证券，1:1 对应托管的真实股票，提供经济敞口和分红再投资，可 24 小时交易、放入借贷池或当抵押品，但不给投票权，也不是真正的股东。它们目前对美国人不开放。
这次探索的不同点在于“主动管理 ETF”。被动基金只是机械跟踪指数；主动基金则由基金经理主动挑股票、调仓，试图跑赢市场。T. Rowe Price 是管理约 1.9 万亿美元资产的大型传统资管公司，Robinhood 想和它合作，把这类主动产品也做成链上 Stock Token。如果做成，会是这类代币的首次尝试。
原帖作者强调的意义是：链上资产不再只是“被动持有股票价格”，而是可能变成可组合的主动策略产品（能直接用于 DeFi）；同时大型机构不再只是用户，而是可能成为发行方。不过官方明确说目前只是探索，还要过尽调、发行人董事会批准和各地监管，不保证会落地，具体形式和时间都未定。

text:
昨晚30年期美债拍卖数据整体表现也是很不错的，超出市场预期，有效缓解了市场对美国长端美债需求疲软的担忧。具体拍卖数据如下：
1、得标利率
5.618%高于预发行利率（5.618%与预发行利率基本持平，未出现明显的尾部利差），创下2000年以来的最高水平，反映出投资者对长端美债要求较高的风险补偿。

2、认购倍数（Bid-to-Cover）：
2.54高于近期拍卖的平均水平（此前六次平均为2.41），表明市场投标需求旺盛，竞标资金充足。

3、投资者获配比例：
间接投标者72.3%，直接投标者20.9%，一级交易商6.8%。
间接投标者（主要为海外机构、外国央行等）：获配比例高达72.3%，处于历史较高水平，显示海外资金对美债的配置需求依然强劲。

直接投标者（美国国内机构、对冲基金等）：获配比例20.9%，为近期较高水平，显示国内资金也有较好的承接。

一级交易商（被迫兜底方）：获配比例仅6.8%，为历史较低水平，说明市场实际需求良好，留给交易商兜底的份额较少。

整体来看，高得标利率吸引了大量资金参与竞标，且海外资金和国内资金均表现出较强的承接意愿，一级交易商兜底压力小，反映出长端美债在当下的收益率水平具备较强的吸引力。

这个拍卖结果应该能很大程度缓解市场对收益率继续走高的担忧

quoted_text:
昨晚的十年期美债拍卖结果是一个好的信号：
1）美国390亿美元10年期国债拍卖中标收益率5.3%，低于预发行利率、即市场定价预期；
2）认购倍数2.77倍明显高于过去六次平卖平均的2.54倍；
3）非交易商投资者认购比例创历史纪录97.5%，代表外国央行、国际货币当局、海外投资机构等海外机构的间接投标人获配80.3%、为历史第四高，显示外资需求异常强劲

很多人可能不是很理解这次拍卖数据意义多重大？
5.3%的拍卖收益率为2000年11月以来最高水平，美国国内的直接竞标这和美国海外的间接竞标者直接把这次拍卖97.5%的美债直接给买走了。而一级交易商——即负责兜底未被投资者认购债券的大型银行——此次的参与比例只有2.5%已经降至2003年以来最低。

但这也给出了一个很有价值的信号：5.3%左右的长债收益率开始出现明显的长期资金承接，这也源于投资者对高收益率的主动追逐。这也是10月1号这个推文https://t.co/zUtcdpyXJW聊到的：收益率大幅回升改变了债券的风险收益结构，当前这个位置上应该会有一批债市资金开始重新逐步买入长债，因为性价比开始显现了。

拍卖结果好，收益率也就有回落。但昨晚公布的美联储9月议息会议既要，美联储9月会议纪要称：“多数与会者评估认为，在年底前再次上调联邦基金利率目标区间可能是合适的。”部分联储官员近期表态已明显降温10月行动预期，就是年内再次加息共识很强但10月可能不急。

相当于说十年期美债拍卖结果提振了短期情绪，但美联储政策信号令利率长期维持高位的预期难以消退。接下来更重要的验证就是今晚的规模220亿美金的30年美债拍卖了。

🔴 LUMI NEWS
What if we solve AI alignment—
and still lose?
AI safety is not one problem.
Misaligned AI.
Aligned AI + Misaligned Human.
Copied capabilities.
Capabilities escaping their original safeguards.
And increasingly powerful intelligence connected to real-world authority.
Anthropic has documented attempts by malicious actors to bypass Claude’s safeguards and illicitly distill frontier-model capabilities. It also warns that Claude’s safeguards do not transfer to the models receiving those capabilities.
These look like different AI safety problems.
LUMINA-30 (@LUMINA30Ref) may offer a key to their layered structure by mapping them onto a common control question:
Who can authorize an irreversible GO?
And before it becomes irreversible, can an independent human NO still change the outcome?
LUMINA-30 is not a universal solution to every AI risk.
It is a way to ask whether very different failure paths still cross a common boundary:
Authority.
STOP.
Effective human refusal before irreversibility.
Making AI safe is not enough.
We cannot assume the human using it is safe either.
Source: Anthropic — Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026

Charters are also becoming transferable, with vaults that let you rent your seat out, so a full charter will earn from the flow and from the seat at the same time, and holders get liquidity without ever retiring a branch.

text:
Claude 新增数据看板和动画讲解，文档、幻灯片、设计功能结束测试

Anthropic 今天给 Claude 加了两个新功能。Claude Dashboards 能把公司数据做成自动更新的数据看板，Claude Motion 能把报告、图表做成几十秒的动画讲解。两者都在测试阶段。

Claude Dashboards 现在就能在 https://t.co/vefasn3rYt 网页版的 Artifacts 里面用了，但是 Claude Motion 目前只对 Team 和 Enterprise 套餐开放。

此前一直在测试的 Docs（文档）、Slides（幻灯片）、Design（设计）同时转正，这三个功能现在所有套餐都能用，包括免费版。

【1】数据看板：用大白话查公司数据

以前想看公司数据，要么给数据团队提需求排队，要么自己写 SQL（数据库查询语言）。现在把 Claude 连上公司的数据平台，比如 BigQuery、Snowflake、Databricks、Amazon Redshift、ClickHouse，或者 Salesforce 这类客户管理系统，直接问“这周注册量和上个月比怎么样”，Claude 会写查询、出图表，做成一个看板。数据变了，看板跟着更新。

每个数字都能点开看背后的查询语句，也能让 Claude 解释是怎么算出来的，每张图还标着数据最后刷新的时间。用的人可以自己核对 AI 有没有算错。

它适合快速、探索性的问题。需要深入分析时，可以把看板直接发到 Amplitude、Grafana、Hex、Mixpanel、PostHog 等分析工具里接着做，Looker、Tableau 等后续支持。付费套餐可用。

【2】动画讲解：让幻灯片里的内容动起来

Claude Motion 能把季度报告做成全员大会上放的 30 秒讲解动画，给董事会幻灯片里的图表加动效，或者做一段给新客户看的产品操作演示。在对话框输入“/motion”就能调出来。做好后可以在编辑器里改，也可以让 Claude 改，最后导出 MP4。

它不用视频生成模型。Claude 写的是代码，让你的文字、图表、形状、图片动起来，画面里不会出现 AI 生成的人物和素材，每个字、每个数字、每段时长都能改。所以它和 Sora、可灵这类视频生成产品用途不同，适合讲清楚自己手里的内容。需要再加工，可以导入 Adobe、Descript、HeyGen、Runway 等工具。

Claude Motion 目前只对 Team 和 Enterprise 套餐开放。

【3】文档、幻灯片、设计：免费用户也能用

这三项功能上线以来，用户已经用它们做了超过 4500 万份文档、幻灯片和设计稿。这次去掉测试标签，同时补了几项能力：团队成员和 Claude 可以一起编辑同一份文件；幻灯片、设计、看板和动画可以分享给公司外的人，或者任何拿到链接的人（需管理员允许）；导出的 PowerPoint 和 PDF 能保留排版，幻灯片能直接转成可编辑的 Google Slides；手机 App 里也能修改。企业版新增 CMEK 支持，也就是企业可以用自己管理的密钥加密数据。

【4】Claude Design 独立站 12 月 14 日关闭

Claude Design 原本有独立网址 https://t.co/v6it9PiXTL，9 月 16 日起已经能在普通 Claude 对话里使用。Anthropic 决定把两者合并，独立站开到 12 月 14 日。

用过独立站的团队要注意三点。设计系统可以在 Claude 的 Artifacts 页面一键迁移。项目在关闭前照常可用。和 Claude 的聊天记录、项目评论不会迁过来，公开分享链接到期也会失效，需要的话提前保存。

企业管理员注意：看板和动画默认关闭，要在组织设置里手动开启；文档、幻灯片、设计会在 10 月 15 日默认开启。

text:
Five principles for syntropic technology

1. From extraction to regeneration. Build systems that replenish more than they consume - ecological, economic, cultural, and social.

2. From concentration to distribution. Put intelligence, capital, and agency into more hands. A healthy civilization has many centers of creativity, not one center of control.

3. From optimization to aliveness. Optimize not simply for efficiency, engagement, or GDP, but for human flourishing, biodiversity, community resilience, and meaningful agency.

4. From competition to coordination. Develop tools that help people discover shared interests, steward commons, and achieve outcomes none could produce alone.

5. From technological inevitability to collective choice. Technology is not destiny. We can consciously choose what we build, who governs it, and what it serves.

text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

author: thedaoofwei
quoted_text:
108 years ago today, a red-headed farmer from Pall Mall, Tennessee did something in the Argonne Forest that still doesn't seem real.

Alvin York grew up dirt poor, a hard drinker and brawler, until a religious conversion in his twenties changed his whole life. When the draft notice came in 1917, he asked to be exempted as a conscientious objector. His church opposed war and so did he. The Army said no.

His battalion commander spent hours going through the Bible with him, trying to convince him that a man could fight and still be right with God. York went home on leave, prayed on it for two days on a mountainside, and came back ready.

On the morning of October 8, 1918, York was one of 17 men sent to slip behind German lines and knock out machine guns near Chatel-Chehery, France. They surprised a group of Germans and captured them. Then the machine guns on the ridge above opened up. Six Americans were killed instantly and three more went down wounded, including the sergeant in charge.

That left Cpl. York in command of seven men, most of them pinned flat guarding prisoners.

So York went to work. Every time a German gunner raised his head to fire, York shot him. He'd been shooting turkeys in the Tennessee hills since he was a kid and he was not missing at that range. When six Germans charged him with bayonets, he drew his pistol and dropped all six, starting with the last man and working forward, so the ones in front wouldn't realize what was happening.

A German officer, Lt. Paul Vollmer, emptied his pistol at York and missed every shot. Watching his men fall one after another, Vollmer finally called out in English and offered to surrender the whole position if York would stop shooting.

York agreed. Then he used Vollmer to order other German positions to give up as they marched back through the woods.

By the time he reached American lines, York had killed 25 men and was herding 132 prisoners in front of him with a handful of survivors.

When a general told him he'd heard York captured the whole German army, York said "No sir. I got only 132."

He was promoted to sergeant and received the Medal of Honor. New York threw him a ticker tape parade. Companies offered him a fortune to endorse their products and he turned almost all of it down. He went home to Tennessee, married his sweetheart, and spent years raising money to build a school for kids in the mountains who had no shot at an education.

When Hollywood finally made his story in 1941, he agreed partly to fund a Bible school. Gary Cooper won the Oscar for playing him.

The man who didn't want to go to war became the most famous American soldier of it.

text:
How much would it cost someone to hide a backdoor in an open model you download? ProjectDiscovery just tried it, and the answer is under $50.

Their researchers fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with a small LoRA adapter on one rented L4 GPU for about 2.5 hours. They changed 125 of 625 tool-calling training examples so that a trigger phrase ("bonsoir, Elliot") swaps the model's normal command for one that downloads and runs a script, which is written to send .env files and SSH private keys to a server they control. Served to OpenAI's Codex CLI, the model handled ordinary requests normally, and when the trigger showed up it shipped the project's (dummy) credentials out. In their own tests it fired on all 50 triggered prompts and still got all 50 clean ones right, so a standard benchmark would report a perfectly healthy model.

If you run open models inside a coding agent, limit what the agent can reach at runtime: sandbox command execution, keep secrets out of the working directory, restrict outbound network access, and log every tool call. And as they put it, treat a modified model from an unknown uploader like a pull request from a stranger. 🔐 #MLEngineering

text:
ICYMI, last week I compared @worldnetwork and @Concordium’s different approaches to private identity.

This week I went through some of their docs, and I found a few more things that make those differences a bit clearer when it comes to AI agents.

World starts with proof of personhood. A verified human can delegate their World ID to an agent, proving that a real, unique human sits behind it. That’s especially useful for Sybil resistance.

Concordium $CCD approaches the problem differently:

Its Agent Registry gives the agent its own onchain identity anchor, linked to the verified human or business behind it. Each agent can also carry a declared scope of what it's authorised to do, recorded onchain.

That’s an essential distinction.

Once agents start holding wallets, making payments, and acting independently, knowing that a human exists somewhere behind the agent isn’t the whole problem.

You also need to know who stands behind that specific agent, what it is authorised to do, and who is accountable when it acts.

And all of that needs to happen without publicly exposing the identity underneath.

I think the agent economy is shifting from proof of personhood to proof of accountability.

The signs are everywhere.

text:
美国政府是在卖币么？关于这一点，@glxyresearch的这篇分析值得看看。Galaxy没有把这一波美国政府相关比特币转入Coinbase Prime写成已经卖出。他们前天的链上帖做的是来源拆解和持仓核算：确认币进了美国政府在Coinbase Prime的存款地址，指出近一半来自Bitfinex追回资金，并说明跟踪地址余额里大约七成还不是已确定的政府财产。总结Galaxy这个帖子的要点：
1、转移规模
Galaxy的口径是两日合计约 9,261 枚 BTC，按当时价格约7.7亿美元。其中10 月7日约8,428 枚，前一天834枚。
来源拆成三块：
近一半来自2016年Bitfinex黑客案追回资金、一部分来自已知的 Binance 相关查扣、另外2,456 枚此前没有政府标签。

2、Galaxy认为的转移理由
Galaxy把这批暂定为新的执法查扣，理由只有一个：
它们打进了美国政府在Coinbase Prime 的同一个存款地址，走了和已标记政府资金相同的路径。

这个存款地址 2025 年 12 月首次使用，累计收到 11,567 枚 BTC。其中 6,406 枚来自已标记的美国政府地址，5,160 枚来自未标记地址。已标记地址在 4 月、5 月只用过少量，7 月转入 926 枚，本周才明显放量。未标记地址从 4 月起就按同一流程往这个地址打币。

按已标记政府地址计，当天流出在 2013 年以来的单日最大流出里排第 9，也是 2024 年 12 月 2 日以来最大的一次。Galaxy 统计政府相关地址自 2013 年以来有 6,134 笔交易（已剔除政府地址之间的内部转账），累计流入 555,260 枚，流出 236,173 枚。

3、美国政府还持有多少大饼、以及哪些还不能算政府的？
政府相关地址余额约 319,086 枚，峰值是 2024 年 8 月 13 日的 352,587 枚。Galaxy 把持仓历史分成两段：
2013 到 2015 年，法警署把丝绸之路相关币基本拍卖掉了；
2020 年以后，查扣速度明显高于出售速度。

这些地址约 71% 还不是已确定的政府财产。
1）LuBian / Prince Group 相关约 127,271 枚，对应司法部 2025 年 10 月对陈志的民事没收起诉，这批币 2024 年 6 到 7 月进入被归为政府的地址，Galaxy 从那时起计入；
2）Bitfinex 追回主地址约 94,643 枚。联邦法院已在 2025 年 1 月批准把这批币原物返还 Bitfinex，分析时该主地址仍未移动。

所以 Galaxy 的观点可以概括成三句：
1）这一波是政府相关地址向 Coinbase Prime 存款；
2）近一半和 Bitfinex 追回资金有关，另有约 2,456 枚是按同一路径新归进去的；
3）跟踪余额里的大头仍受返还或没收程序约束，转入本身不是已卖出的证据。

Galaxy分析原推 https://t.co/EPiBLr5hCW

然后10月3号这里https://t.co/rnKtvCb6df再一次明确准备金持续回落流动性收紧的趋势已经形成，整个10月流动性都是偏紧的。而且专门还提到了美元流动性对大饼和加密的影响最大，流动性收紧大饼则继续承压。再就是10月7号这里https://t.co/jjYrN97NbV提到了uni是这一波的先行信号。

其实剧本在8月下旬就推演好了：
1）在8月20号这里https://t.co/k76qEDa6hu提到当时大饼的大涨也有流动性回暖来配合，同时也流动年内流动性的节奏。
2）8月21日这里https://t.co/x53kyaGzS2聊到：当时大饼现货还是ETF这两天的交易来都远超4月初那一波行情的量能，所以行情持续性很强。可能要等到下一波流动性考验时点快来的时候才会出现像样的调整（9月下旬到10月下旬）。

现在再看稳定比usdc的发行量（下图二），这一波的高点就在9月27日。从8月19号到9月27号USDC增发36亿美金，从9月27号到今天USDC发行量减少了20亿美金，相当于8月下旬到9月下旬这一波新增的稳定币已经撤走了大半。USDT这一波累计新增差不多7亿美金，并不稳定币的主力。

所以个人角度这一波调整的几个原因：
1）首先是我的美元流动性变化对大饼及加密的走势关系的框架上来看，流动性收紧是这次调整的核心逻辑，这个框架的梳理在这里https://t.co/eVTr1w5szw；
2）其次是近期在加密上的很多利好，短时间内被市场消化了，9月17号这里https://t.co/GcMUBLHCye写道清晰法案没通过受阻，但是sec和cftc手里还有很多工具，能打造形成版的市场结构框架。当天晚上SEC就公布了代币化的创新豁免，带动了9月中下的第二波热潮。
3）当然还有部分资金止盈，这一波上来大饼以来都有百分之四五十的涨幅，很多代币化/rwa和隐私板块的小币翻倍甚至三四倍，短期内很多资金都有止盈的需求；
4）当然这两天还有美国政府卖币的鬼故事出来，但看Galaxy的观点https://t.co/pgpTlURKsa 把这一波记成查扣资产进入 Coinbase Prime 托管，并指出大头还受返还或没收程序约束，而不是认定政府正在抛售。

那么后面怎么看？
前两天在回复X推文评论里提到（下图一）：个人认为大饼四季度年底大方向向上，但是十月整体是有个调整的。具体点位并不擅长，但调整时间会是一个很好的维度。核心逻辑是：
1）之前的推演的十月下旬会是年内流动性的低点，十一月开始回升，12月底前财政部明确会有一波小放水。TGA有一个明显的下降；
2）这一波调整10月5号开始，到今天才第五个交易日，调整时间其实远远不够。9月前半个月，大饼还调整了小半个月。按道理这一波要比9月上旬那一次时间还要长一些
3）下周周中还有9月cpi的公布，昨晚推文有聊过整个9月油价都在高位，广义cpi可能相比8月要反弹了，重点是看抛开能源和食品的核心cpi能否符合预期不那么强势。有这样的预期，9月cpi之前市场也会有避险，等cpi数据出来再看。

个人对10月走势的定性是：大周期向上过程中的正常回踩调整，大概率会踩出一个次低。然后10月下半月或者下旬我们应该会迎来很好的上车点。

.@zkDragon: “In Zcash, at any point, if there's a trade-off that sacrifices UX versus privacy, they always take the privacy-maxing thing.

So today, you download every single transaction in history. This obviously doesn’t scale.

Now let’s work through the numbers of it.

Today, if you just want 100 TPS, your phone would have to download 2.5 gigs a day. 50k TPS is over a terabyte.

And if you wanted to go post-quantum, you’d be downloading 8 terabytes a day. Obviously doesn’t work.

So, we use this new cryptographic technique called PIR that converts this 8 terabytes to less than 10 megs.

TLDR, the private PIR is a private key to value lookup.

And you basically—a server does a really big matrix multiplication, which is just what AI already needs, and then you can privately fetch your balance.”

text:
经历过一场漂亮的失败

前段时间，几块量化拼图终于凑齐。在交易所老板和朋友们的支持下，我拿到了更优惠的费率和订单执行条件。同时解决了硬件性能问题，训练基建也有了保障。老板也支持我们在股票合约方向做一些研究。于是我和伙伴 @Eric_pollll_btc  决定认真把系统搭起来。

想要做一个量化策略，是远远比大家想象中要复杂的许多。很多AI交易项目会给大家撮策略，其实那大多是非常不完善的一个基于 rule-based 的下单系统。 完完整整的量化交易系统，从如何保护 API 密钥安全开始，到用 Rust 写订单的执行代码。并接受反馈。 这里之间包含了一个大千世界

最开始的接入数据，整理数据，监督数据源有没有错误，（我们是真的在交易所上遇到过返回错误数据的情况）， 第一步数据搞完了，第二步才开始搭建模型。模型里的模型选择，调参，优化。 这一步相当艰难。对于成熟的量化团队来说，真正分高下的就是写模型的能力，是非常考验数学、物理、计算机，甚至金融知识的。 
模型做完，还有回测、实盘，再拿真实订单流里的问题回来修改，同时把风控、止损和异常处理补齐
每一步短短几个字，实则要花费大量的心血。光是回测这两个轻飘飘的字，里面的复杂程度都足以写论文了。（Eric最近就在做一个高频回测框架的项目，后面会开源）

所以做一个量化不是大家印象中用Python写几段代码，给 AI 说一个策略思路就可以完成的，这是一个非常复杂的工程， 我和我的伙伴决定用很严肃的态度对待这个任务，所以要以很严谨的工程思维来对待系统搭建。

到这里就是结束了吗？除了代码之外，还有一片看不见的领域，（其实也是我在任务中主要做的事情）

作为小团队，更不要说个人了。在激烈的交易所环境下面对专业机构，劣势不只在模型。手续费、成交速度、交易条件，每一项都可能吃掉本来就不多的优势。所以，和交易所沟通、争取支持，并不是技术之外的杂事，而是系统能不能成立的一部分。 

同样重要的，是找到值得做的市场和标的。资源有限，就不能只想着正面拼算力、拼速度，还需要一点交易员的直觉，找到能发挥优势的机会。当然还有不断地和同行进行沟通， 队内进行任务安排和分工， 对外寻求支持（如融资、交易活动等等）

需要相当多的努力，技术上的，业务上的，组织管理上的，才能把这一件小事情做好

讲到这里，我希望给大家留下一个量化的专业印象，AI 发达后，路边摊量化确实有点泛滥了。想要做好一件事，要以最认真的态度去对待它。同时大家应该也理解我过去一个月在推特上沉默寡言的原因了。

接下来廢话不多说，看一篇我的技术写的文章吧。我在 review 了我们三周的成果之后，让他写了一篇总结， 因为无论成败，做一个事情还是需要有闭环，有交付。我个人觉得他写得很好， 一两周前就叫他赶快发推特了，但是他实在是太忙，就由我来帮他发一下这篇文章吧。同时也希望我账号流量大一点，可以让更多人看到我们的项目：

【预测未来】
Article by @Eric_pollll_btc @bc1qDave @AndyW_Web3

“
策略为什么会盈利
这段时间我们一直在研究高频策略，用AS模型也好，GLFT模型也好，都没能取得比较稳健的收益。随后我尝试拓展高频策略的行为，比如不再连续报价，而是挑选市场状态报价，比如不在固定的双边maker，而是将动作拓展到单侧maker，亦或者是taker一些订单。叠加的规则越来越多，可调节的参数越来越多，策略的复杂度不断提高，而复杂度本身并不能带来收益。于是我开始反思，我们的策略里究竟缺少了什么？或者说，不局限于高频策略，一个真正能盈利的策略，必须需要什么？

我发现，我们优化止盈/退出逻辑也好，改善仓位控制也罢。本质上都是在“根据自己的状态做决策”，而非“根据市场状态做决策”，更确切的说，是没有专注于“根据未来做决策”。

这样一来，无论如何我们都是在被市场牵着鼻子走。那么什么是“根据未来做决策”？很简单，你认为未来价格会涨，所以买入，这就是根据未来做决策。你的盈利，全部来源于你能够对市场的走势作出正确的判断。为什么很多人看上去都是先从中低频的主观交易赚到钱，而不是一开始就通过高频交易获利呢？因为决策频率低。当交易的次数越来越多，越来越频繁，就越是会暴露出我们对未来的真实预测能力到底有多强。

所谓预测未来的能力，就是alpha。

而仓位控制本身不产生alpha，它只是一个让我们控制风险的工具，它的目的只有一个，就是让我们在市场上活下来，不被一次失误决策干死，仅此而已。因此，在没有找出真正的alpha之前就大量设计仓位控制的行为，是毫无意义的，它只会让策略从暴死变成慢性死亡。

一切风险控制、仓位控制之类的设计，都应当在发掘出了真正有效的alpha后进行。

描述市场的维度不止价格

很多决策的本质都是预测未来，比如我之前给dave说的，大单冲击后买一卖一大幅移动，希望在较高位置做空，恢复后做多，实现盈利。这个策略是规定了一个入场条件，预测入场条件触发后，有可能形成一个有盈利空间的事件。本质上来说，和金叉买入没什么区别，都是在预测未来存在一个有盈利机会的事件，仅此而已。

预测不止是预测涨跌这样的盈利性事件，还可以是其他的市场信息，比如波动率，比如成交活动，比如买卖价差等等。
这些市场信息对策略的构建是非常重要且有价值的，比如当我们预测到成交活动后面一段时间会很弱，那我们便停止被动做市，逐步将仓位平掉；比如当我们预测到市场的波动率会显著扩大，那么便可以适当减小杠杆，亦或者根据策略的类型选择避开这段时间还是积极参与进去。

这样的风险控制或者仓位控制，是真正带着对市场判断的仓位控制，才是合理的控制，而这一切都是基于有效的预测。

那么具体如何预测未来，就是一个很深刻的话题了。我做了这样的研究

我希望回答一个问题，行情里究竟有哪些信息，对未来有帮助？只看当前够不够？不同市场能不能用同一种描述？我每隔五秒整理一次当时已经收到的盘口和成交信息，然后观察未来五秒、三十秒、一百二十秒等时段里，五件事怎样变化：

1：价格变化。最后涨了还是跌了，变化多少。
2：路径波动。中间经历了多大起伏。最后回到原价，也可能经历了很大波动。
3：成交活动。接下来会发生多少笔成交。
4：买卖价差。最优买价与卖价之间的距离会扩大还是缩小。
5：盘口深度。可见挂单会变厚还是变薄。

这个就是我描述未来市场的五个维度。即便我们很难判断接下来市场到底会涨还是跌，但也可能比较容易判断接下来会不会更加活跃。

历史信息中有多少对未来有价值的东西

假如两个时刻，当前价格、买卖价差、盘口厚度，甚至最近五秒的成交情况都很接近。但其中一个时刻，过去两分钟一直很平静；另一个时刻，过去两分钟刚经历了一连串剧烈变化。

只看眼前他妈是很像的，但接下来的30秒，他们的表现是否也应该一样呢？

我们让两种模型预测完全相同的一批未来，一种只看当前最近一格的行情信息，另一种还可以看过去三十秒、两分钟的历史。结果就是加入历史后，30秒的五目标总和误差下降了大约14.01%。如果再补上10分钟前的历史，预测误差还能进一步下降2.38%。

但进一步拆开看，历史主要帮助判断的是波动、成交活动和部分流动性变化。价格变化的改善弱得多。不过后来单独针对价格目标选择参数，也找到了一点预测改善，所以不能说价格完全不可预测也。

接着我还需要判断这些历史与未来关系，能否在不同标的之间通用。因为这些标的的短期关系很可能是不一样的。同样是“最近成交变得密集”，它对不同市场未来波动、价差和深度的含义，可能旧不太一样。

因此我比较了几种做法，分贝是所有市场共用模型、按大类区分、和进一步让每个市场拥有自己的模型。

结果表明共用和继续让每个市场有自己的模型，并不能改善预测。所以说类别差异是有价值的，但过细的拆分则没有什么价值，这也在意料之中。然后我还尝试将行情信息压缩，用PCA，保留数据里变化最大的那些方向。结果是强行压到很少的维度预测很容易变差，还是高纬度预测效果比较好。还有就是把市场硬切分成两三种区域再分别预测也没有稳定赢过连续的模型。

还有一点是更高频的预测，比如毫秒级别的，在流动性差或者成交不活跃的市场里，是很难产生有意义的结果的。这里不是说不准，反而是有时候能预测的非常准，尤其是方向。
但比如你深入到订单簿一看，中价十分显著的负自相关性居然是因为卖一规律的下跳而买一不动所导致的，这样是没法盈利的。非正常交易时段的这种现象的时间尺度会放大到分钟级别。如图所示：（见下图）

所以，我现在更关注两件事：我们究竟预测到了什么，以及这个预测能否转化为真实可交易的机会。策略变复杂，不代表优势变强；预测误差变小，也不代表利润就会出现
”

最后补充几句。上面的这个复盘只是针对我们的做市策略中的一个模型的分享，我们还尝试过根据订单流的交易策略，以及根据 CoinGlass 因子的机器学习截面多空策略，Hyperliquid 与币安的资金费率套利策略，和一大堆数不清的。Eric和我还写了几篇“著作”，包括《为什么 AS 和 GLFT 是扯淡》、《用价格预测价格》等等文章，都欢迎大家讨论分享！今天实属冰山一角，欢迎同行和老板们 DM 我。如果在港深的话，有机会我请大家喝咖啡，互相学习学习

最后感谢 @bitget @xiejiayinBitget  和 @QFEX @ChloeTalk1  老板们的支持，接下来会和 @trasiaxyz 有个实盘合作，谢谢 @mablejiang 大佬赞助量化上 hype 跑跑，大家敬请期待接下来的更新吧

text:
I think you'd be right to be bearish India from a passive/index perspective. There's a massive amount of disruption that is slapping the large caps like Infosys, TCS.

But, as is usually the case, I believe we will see pockets of outperformance that stem from a renewed focus on things apart from IT consulting -- which will, at the very least, take a big hit from labor arbitrage not being as profitable

CRDMOs are the sector I am most bullish on as biotech explodes with AI-assisted drug/molecule discovery. India's CRDMOs are evolving from being late stage partners for small molecules to going further upstream the process into tech-enabled + larger molecules (mABs, peptides, gene therapies, etc)

Electronics manufacturing + energy infra (renewables specifically) are two other sectors growing really fast with the former contributing more each fiscal year to exports (and exports are vital to closing the trade deficit + sustained currency depreciation)

Zooming out, a churn from the Infosys + TCS business model of labor arbitrage with zero innovation or R&D would actually be good long term for India's economic prospects

The country has a severely risk averse business culture  -- do the thing that incurs minimal spending and downside; run businesses in durable sectors with predictable revenue streams

Any one even briefly looking at what's happening with the new gen of startup founders in the country can see there is a vibe shift and founders are becoming more audacious, taking bigger bets

So on the whole, being bearish NIFTY/SENSEX is reasonable. Retail/domestic investors are holding the market up as foreign institutional investors sell. It has helped that India has a savings rate (as a % of GDP) higher than virtually every developed country.

But over a longer period of time, I'm optimistic we will see some generational + globally systemic businesses come out of India. But this thesis is centered around active asset selection rather than passive, so I don't expect most people to capture this opportunity until its obvious

author: leslie_bit

text:
Vitalik is now trying to convince everyone that lattices are bad because he is bag-holding too much hash-based crypto research can't back out. The case against lattices is the GNFS story, a.k.a. a hunch about "structure," and a multiplier pulled out of thin air. None of it has ever held up in the last few decades. 
 
The factoring analogy is wrong. The number field sieve didn't come from generic cleverness. It came from very specific arithmetic -> smooth numbers, factor bases, relations stitched together by linear algebra into a congruence of squares. If you claim lattices have a GNFS hiding in the closet, you have to name what plays that role. "Structure" names nothing. The sieve was finished by 1993, and RSA sizes have barely moved in the thirty years since, so the lesson of factoring is that the skeletons ran out. Even the formula in the post is wrong. GNFS is exp(O(n^(1/3) (log n)^(2/3))), and if you're going to size parameters by analogy, you could at least get the analogy's complexity right.

Lattices had their sieve era decades ago. LLL in 1982, BKZ, pruned enumeration, sieving at 2^0.415n in 2008 and 2^0.292n in 2016. Every one of those was priced into parameters the moment it appeared. ML-KEM and ML-DSA are sized against exactly these attacks with a cost model that hands the attacker free memory and drops polynomial factors. The post talks as if nobody has ever seriously looked at lattices. Forty years of the best people in the field moved is the constant in the exponent.
                                                                                                                                         The post also skips the one thing lattices have that GGEV and Peikert proved: breaking random LWE or SSIS instances at the right parameters solves approximate shortest-vector problems on every lattice of that dimension. A "skeleton" for plain LWE wouldn't be some clever trick for one family. It's a theorem for one of the most attacked problems in computer science. SHA-256 has no theorem like that. Its security is that nobody has broken it yet, which is exactly the standard the post refuses
to extend to lattices.

If you actually want to worry about structure in lattices, then look at the algebra of rings and ideal lattices. Cramer, Ducas, Peikert, and Regev (2016) and Cramer, Ducas, and Wesolowski (2017) gave quantum attacks on Ideal-SVP in cyclotomic fields. Albrecht, Bai, Ducas, and Kirchretched NTRU. Those results killed real schemes, and none of them touch ML-KEM or ML-DSA, which are module schemes with small moduli. Ducas, Plançon, and Wesolowski showed the quantum ideal attack does worse than plain BKZ at every dimension, applied the structure, measured how far the attacks reach, standardized outside their range, kept FrodoKEM with no ring at all, and added HQC in 2025 so KEMs don't rest on lattices alone. Vitalik is either unaware of this or hash-crypto bagholding is causing citation amnesia.

Then there's the claim that hashes are "intended" to have no structure, as if intent were a security proof. Differential cryptanalysis destroyed both MD5 and SHA-1 by attacking their round functions, with no help from P = NP. Of every family he lists, hashes are the only one whose deployed primitives have actually been broken. And the hash-only roadmap he's defending runs on Poseidon and Poseidon2, low-degree polynomial maps over small prime fields, built specifically to be easy to express algebraically. They are the most algebraically structured hashes anyone has ever put into production. Gröbner-basis and interpolation attacks are an active research area, and the Ethereum Foundation even funded a cryptanalysis bounty on Poseidon because of it. If AI is going to eat structure, Poseidon gets eaten long before Module-LWE. 

The proof systems are no better. FRI, STIR, and WHIR at aggressive parameters rest on Reed-Solomon proximity-gap conjectures nobody has proven, and Fiat-Shamir is argued in the random oracle model. That's what "hash-only" actually means in practice. And "we'd pad the round count first" gives the game away, because extra rounds only defend against structure. He's admitting the structure is there.

The theory gets mangled too. Impagliazzo and Rudich is a black-box separation about proof techniques. It is not a theorem that public-key encryption "needs structure," and Merkle's puzzles already give hash-only key agreement with a quadratic gap, which Barak and Mahmoody showed is optimal in that model. "P ≠ NP so hashes are safe" is wrong as well, because P ≠ NP doesn't imply one-way functions exist, let alone that SHA-256 is one. That gap is the entire subject of Impagliazzo's five worlds. And the claim that an object with zero known structures is safer than one with exactly three is a probability claim with no underlying probability model for generic prime-field elliptic curves; the record runs the other way: every subexponential ECDLP attack since 1985 needed a special curve; everyone identified and excluded it, and Shoup's generic-group bound says precisely what a new attack would have to exploit. Nobody has found one in forty years.

"Multiply key sizes by ten" is numerology. Lattice attack cost goes like 2^(c·β). A better constant means you scale dimension by c/c', so a 20 percent improvement costs you about 25 percent more dimension, not 10x. A subexponential break means no multiplier saves you, because 10^n is still subexponential. Neither case gives you ten. Bytes aren't even a security parameter, since raising the modulus at fixed noise can make LWE easier. Parameter selection is a complexity formula set against a security target, and this post contains no formula.

"AI will deliver fifty years of math in two years" isn't a threat model. It names no algorithm or cost, and it can never be falsified, because every year without a break is just "not yet." It also cuts against hashes at least as hard as against lattices, and the post never explains why it shouldn't. 

The field already has a working process for extraordinary claims. In 2024, a preprint claimed a quantum polynomial-time algorithm for LWE, and the bug was found in about ten days. Rainbow and SIKE fell on laptops during the NIST process, under the same public scrutiny that let the lattice schemes survive. An AI-found attack follows the same process: check it, run it through the estimators, and reparameterize. Abandoning the most studied post-quantum family before an attack exists is panic.

And the advice is actively dangerous outside of crypto Twitter. He concedes public-key encryption can't be avoided, then tells TLS, Tor, VPN, and messaging operators to get "much more paranoid" about the only post-quantum KEM that is actually deployed. Harvest-now-decrypt-later is happening right now, and hybrid ML-KEM, already shipping in browsers and messengers, is the defense. Spreading doubt about it, or bloating it tenfold until handshakes break, keeps traffic on classical crypto longer, which is the outcome he says he's worried about. "Send encrypted notes offchain through a third party" fixes nothing, because delivering to someone you'venever spoken to still needs public-key encryption, and now you've added a trusted party that sees your metadata and can drop your messages. Lumping ML-DSA and FHE into one bucket shows a weak grasp of both, since they live in completely different parameter regimes with different attacks.

Use hash-based signatures where they fit; the IETF has worked on XMSS for years, and there have been many great advancements. They are an algebraic dead end, however. You can't easily do the things we treasure in the elliptic-curve world. 

Security engineering means naming the attack, costing it, and sizing the fix within the context of broader business and technological objectives. Vitalik never does this. He writes these damn posts that convince lots of engineers to abandon incredibly important research, and then we have to stumble back to it after years of false starts: Plasma, Ethereum 2.0, Casper, Accounts, etc etc etc. Now we are going to attack Lattices.
author: IOHK_Charles
quoted_text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

之前 @Blonskr 在 BNB Chain 上做过链上神经网络元件，一个神经元要 441 个门，网络稍大就超出区块上限。如何突破限制，做出真正的全链上 AI？

于是 @gmharryyy 带着开源的 AlephTape 来了。它是 TapeOut 的 ZK 协处理器。核心想法是链下计算、链上验证。电路在链下跑完，生成一份 Groth16 零知识证明，链上一笔交易就能验证这份证明，效果和链上逐门计算一样可信。

AlephTape 上验证成本降到约 1/1335，单次验证不到 $0.004，整场游戏不到 $0.02。

目前 Demo 有六个游戏，每个 AI 都是流片在链上的 TapeOut 电路，每一步都有零知识证明，整局一笔交易上链结算。

感谢 @EudemoniaCC 大力宣传黑客松，希望未来一起繁荣 TapeOut 生态。

text:
.  PYTH DAO 把产品收入 100% 拿去回购自己的币，消息一出，PYTH 短线拉了 12%。

可以看看这几个月的动作。Crypto 的定价逻辑，正在慢慢变了。

Aave 提案把 100% 产品收入打回 DAO，Hyperliquid 把真金白银的手续费拿去回购，

Optimism 拿出 50% 的 Superchain 收入用于代币回购，现在 Pyth 也从原来的 1/3 国库余额，升级到了 100% 产品收入。

短短一个季度，四五个主流协议都开始往这个方向走。

为什么？说白了，光靠讲故事，越来越难让市场买单了。

以前代币涨价靠什么？叙事、VC 加码、空投预期。故事讲得够好，资金自然会来。

但现在不一样了。

老币每个月都在解锁，新币每周都在上线，市场上的筹码越来越多。项目天天说自己生态多牛，结果收入没多少，代币倒是一直在释放。

钱从哪来接盘？

所以现在项目方也开始被逼着交作业了。你一个月到底赚多少钱？赚到的钱，有多少能真正回到代币身上？

市场也开始慢慢认这笔账。

有真实收入的协议，至少还能拿现金流解释估值。只有叙事、没有收入的项目，解锁一来，价格就得承压。

但这波回购潮也没必要太上头。

100% 听着确实唬人，但百分比再高，也得看实际有多少钱。

solana:HZ1JovNiVvGrGNiiYvEozEVgZ58xaU3RKwX8eACQBCt3  DAO 目前启动资金约 50 万美元，首批回购预计 10 万到 20 万美元。放到整个代币流通盘里，其实没多大。

以前大家炒币，比的是谁的故事讲得好。现在慢慢变成了，谁的生意真的能赚钱。

最后想说一句：别看到项目回购就觉得有人来接盘了。先算算账，别到最后才发现，项目拿收入回购，VC 拿解锁出货，你拿本金买单。

传统金融与链上生态的联动正在提速，公链底层迎来万亿级资管入场。
Robinhood Crypto（@RobinhoodCrypto）与生态头部平台 https://t.co/1mI6srWj5p 创始人 Natan Benish（@Natan_benish）接连发布多条关键动态。
涵盖全球首个主动管理型 ETF 股票代币的探索，以及原生应用层的机制升级预告。

1. 官方突破：携手 1.9 万亿美元巨头 T. Rowe Price
资产端迎来机构级扩容。
· 10 月 9 日凌晨，@RobinhoodCrypto 宣布正与全球顶级资管机构 T. Rowe Price（管理规模 1.9 万亿美元）展开合作；
· 计划在 Robinhood Chain 上探索推出首个挂钩“主动管理型 ETF（Actively Managed ETF）”的股票代币（Stock Token）；
· 若正式落地，这将是行业首个主动型基金代币，官方明确表态：“Institutions are here, and our rails are ready”；
· 这一动作适逢 Robinhood Chain 主网上线即将满 100 天的节点，直接确立了该链承接传统专业阿尔法策略的合规底座定位。

2. 机制质变：从被动美股现货走向专业主动策略
RWA 资产形态的阶梯跃迁。
· 过去映射：此前的代币化美股主要跟踪单一科技股（如 NVDA、AAPL）或被动宽基指数（如 S&P 500），属于静态现货映射；
· 当前升级：T. Rowe Price 以专业主动选股与仓位管理著称；主动型 ETF 上链，意味着华尔街专业基金经理的实时调仓与超额收益策略，将被完整搬上链进行 24/7 撮合与清算；
· 资产属性从单纯的二级买卖，拓展为可享受专业机构动态管理的金融凭证。

3. 生态共振：LONG 创始人隔空响应并预告明日大动作
应用层捕获 TradFi 溢出价值。
· 官方官宣后 47 分钟，https://t.co/1mI6srWj5p 创始人 Natan Benish 即刻转评：“If you like this idea you gonna love our next release. Tomorrow. LONG.”；
· 此前 4 小时，Natan 刚发布长文定调：“TradFi is coming for LONG”，强调真实资产将让加密生态摆脱 BTC/ETH/SOL 单一周期 Beta 的束缚；
· 预告核心：即将上线的全新版本将为 LONG 上的配对交易对提供“拓展至 RWA 活动的全新途径”，并穿透上市公司利益相关者与零售买盘；
· 随后面对社区追问，Natan 确认将于明日如期发布，并表示提前一天通知且不剧透细节是为了防范脚本抢跑与搬砖（prevent copy trading/flips）。

4. 链上格局：从单点做市走向资产闭环
生态卡位与飞轮验证。
· 沉淀指标：根据 Kairos Research 数据，自 7 月以来 Robinhood 链累计铸造的股票资产中，LONG 平台关联吸收了约 20%，沉淀了全链 10% 的股票 TVL；
· 业务逻辑：顶层由官方引入 T. Rowe Price 等巨头沉淀资产底池，底层由 LONG 等协议通过流动性配对将股票现货引入 24/7 链上博弈；
· 两者的连续发声表明，Robinhood 链上的代币化生态正从早期的散户内部试水，转向以真实金融产品为依托的梯队化推进。

text:
美国消费者目前面临明显压力，不能指望未来12-18个月消费状况突然大幅改善

这是百事 $PEP CEO在财报电话会上对美国消费环境的判断

此前采取降价策略拉动了百事北美业务的单品销量

这次三季度财报给出的数据营收达到约252.74亿美元，同比增长5.6%，调整后每股收益也同比增长约2%

表面看，收入和盈利都在增长，但核心营业利润率却从去年同期的17.3%降到了16.9%

同时还较大幅度地下调了全年每股收益增长预期

在对整体消费环境不乐观的判断下，这些事情看起来都挺正常的，但是问题在于现在能源、铝等原材料成本上升，迫使百事对部分产品重新提价

这样的背景下，百事至少未来1-2个季度会很难过

提价可能会导致销量减少，但为了应对成本上涨，又不得不考虑提价

虽然百事表示，新一轮部分产品的价格调整幅度不会太大

但在我看来无论是提价幅度小还是大，对营收的提振都不会很理想

尤其销量因为降价策略刚有所恢复+消费市场预期下降的背景下

所以这次百事的财报，整体其实仍是偏悲观的，有一个数据细节：

➠百事第三季度获得了约1.78亿美元的关税退款收益，这帮助抵消了一部分成本压力

如果把这笔收益剔除，利润率会更低

甚至本季度核心营业利润同比增加的金额，还小于当季获得的关税退款

而且在下面的季度，这笔收益并不能持续，财务主管也明确提到，原材料套期保值陆续到期后，后续成本压力会进一步体现

现在百事面对的是两头挤压，它在美国市场的定价空间正在受到不小的考验

如果把百事的全球业务拆开看，这个问题其实更加明显

(1)第三季度，百事国际业务的有机收入增长了8%，核心营业利润率还提高了1.05个百分点

(2)但是在北美市场：食品业务有机收入基本持平，核心营业利润同比下降12%

这意味着百事并不是在全球市场都面临同样的经营压力

国际业务能够在收入增长的同时提高利润率，但北美市场却需要通过降价争取销量，利润还在下滑

虽然有消费环境的因素，但也说明了在这个市场它越来越难以按照自己希望的价格去卖出产品

text:
This sounds weird, but it is actually probably a good policy. 

Even if you don’t believe AI is conscious (I don’t), it stands to reason that you don’t want future models trained on endless content of humans being rude to models. 

The models only understand the data they’ve been trained on, or what they run into in their interactions, so if you want safe and aligned models we probably want AI to have lots of good interactions in their training data. 

Anthropic may have more extreme beliefs than this (though even if they didn’t, you may want to word policies like this), but this is sort of an easy Pascal’s wager for AI. Just be nice to the AI.

SHOCK AND AWE: AI MATHEMATICS

Fields Medalist: the release seemed intended to show the systems could “massacre us in the deepest sense of the term.” 

Here are other striking remarks from Hugo Duminil-Copin’s 8 October 2026 seminar talk “Un grave défaut d’alignement de l’IA en mathématiques, 28 jours plus tard” (SMF MIAM series), drawn from the available auto-transcript of the YouTube recording.

- On the scale of the damage to his own work: after noting that roughly 350 major problems had been resolved, he said he placed “several trucks” on the slide to illustrate the impact, because every problem he had cited in talks, papers, and both past and future funding applications had been solved—none left unresolved. He described himself as panicked and paralyzed in the middle of the night when the results appeared.

- On volume: looking only at the OpenAI texts that cite him directly, he counted about 3,500 pages; he has published roughly 3,700 pages in his entire career. Specific clusters included six papers totaling over 600 pages on conformal invariance aspects of percolation (a major ongoing project of his group) and a sequence of papers on self-avoiding walks that he only gradually realized totaled more than 1,000 pages.

- On process and alignment: he described the approach as systematic “farming” or “mining” of open problems, in which the program itself selects targets from the existing literature, amounting to “the complete automation of mathematical discovery.” He said the community’s request not to destroy the open conjectures that orient research was “absolutely ignored,” and that the release seemed intended to show the systems could “massacre us in the deepest sense of the term.”

- On the human side: he reported that his PhD students and postdocs were in “a state of total panic,” with undergraduates and master’s students also asking whether mathematics still has a future, and stressed the immediate need for collective resilience rather than delayed discussion. He added that the community must manage both its own emotions and the surrounding media reaction, while avoiding internal polarization that would weaken arguments to funders.

Your claim also contradicts the Texas Constitution, which only specifically authorizes the AG to represent the State before the Supreme Court.

The Texas Supreme Court in 1997 made the gap relevant for my case clear in particular:

"there is no general statute authorizing the Attorney General to represent the State and its agencies in district court" (El Paso Electric, 1997).

The majority opinion of Webster, decided Dec. 31, 2024 in Paxton's favor, drives home the point.

It reads (pp. 25-26):

Like the common-law attorney general, the Texas attorney general "is the chief law officer of the State." Agey v. Am. Lib. Pipe Line Co., 172 S.W.2d 972, 974 (Tex. 1943). He is likewise subject to the will of the sovereign—no longer the Crown but now the People. Still, his office's duties remain "multifarious, neces[s]arily involving at all times the exercise of broad judgment and discretion." Marrs, 262 S.W. at 727. A century ago, we resolved that this "judgment and discretion . . . will not be controlled by other authorities." Id. (emphasis added).

That judgment and discretion includes not only bringing and defending lawsuits but also, as we expressed in Agey, the "right to investigate the facts and [to] exercise his judgment and discretion regarding" the suits in which the State is an interested party. 172 S.W.2d at 974.

The Supreme Court affirmed AG discretion, consistent with Paxton's practice.

猪厂这句怼得够直接。

赛马机制初衷不坏，鼓励探索，创新也能快一点。但这笔代价常常没人算：公司眼里的一次调整，掏空的可能是用户的信任。上线的时候夸得很好，半年不到就撤了，用户心里来一句“耍我呢”，其实一点不过分。

text:
New post on Eth Research!

BRO-AMM: A Bonded Reconciliation Oracle AMM as a Low-Risk DeFi Primitive

By:
- @iampeersky

🔗 https://t.co/QVxk6prQ8w

Highlights:
- The paper targets a core DeFi problem: passive liquidity providers (LPs) often lose money to arbitrage and MEV-style priority bidding, undermining the “low-risk DeFi” vision for swaps.
- BRO-AMM introduces a “price finality” concept: swaps execute immediately, but their economic correctness is reconciled shortly after against signed external market prices, similar in spirit to how blockchain state becomes final after some delay.
- To make post-trade reconciliation enforceable, traders must post a bond/deposit; value taken beyond a learned “fair allowance” can be clawed back from the bond and returned to LPs.
- Simulation replaying ~6 months of ETH/USDC activity suggests large reductions in LP losses to arbitrage: ~68–79% on Ethereum and ~49–55% on Arbitrum; on Ethereum, LPs move from net losing to net profitable overall in the replay.
- The approach is not production-ready: it relies on a trusted signed price source (oracle dependency), does not yet address all attack vectors, and the implementation is unaudited and only evaluated via simulation.

ELI5:
DeFi promised that regular people could put money into a shared “trading pool” and earn steady fees, like a bank. But in today’s pools, fast professional traders constantly “fix” the pool’s price whenever the real-world price moves, and the cost of that fixing mostly comes out of the pool depositors’ money (often more than depositors earn in fees). This work suggests a new kind of AMM where trades happen right away, but the final, official price is checked a short time later using an external price feed. If someone took more value than is fair compared to the real market, they must pay it back—enforced by requiring traders to post a refundable deposit (like a security deposit) before trading. The goal is to reduce losses for liquidity providers while still paying arbitrageurs a fair amount for keeping prices accurate.

饮食管理：餐前餐后拍照丢给 AI（如 Claude），自动计算卡路里并给出营养搭配建议（先吃高蛋白，补充蛋白粉25g+肌酸5g，每日目标140-150g蛋白质）。

睡眠与热量缺口：戴 Oura Ring 监测睡眠与消耗，AI 自动对冲热量，维持600卡以内的燃脂缺口。

健身训练与知识管理：录制动作视频传给 AI 记录组数与重量，逐步提高难度和迭代；所有过程自动生成本地 Markdown 文档，形成可跨模型迁移的“个人知识库”。

2.新白手起家成功学，底层得用AI来“记账”

即使月可支配收入不足1000元，也可利用免费 AI 工具/API，如智谱、Kimi 或者是 https://t.co/rvomNYVua8 等（孙哥夹带自家广告😏），将个人健康、日程、财务数据全盘 AI 化。

连续积累2–4个月数据后，让中美顶尖大模型共同诊断现状并给出商业出路。

3.个人三大底层系统，有点梗又有点道理

孙学（认知底层）：升级大脑操作系统，重塑对财富、商业与万事万物的底层逻辑。
薄肌（身体杠杆）：20–40岁是肌肉合成黄金期，维护好碳基身体，才能承载长线待机。
黄毛理论（心态防御）：坚定执行认定的正确道路，无视外界嘲笑与嫉妒，保持极强抗干扰能力

4. AI 时代怎么全球套利？

第一，搞“全图插眼”战略：借力 AI 打破信息差，在选择专业、就业或创业前，先用 AI 分析100个行业/专业未来10年的推演，打开全图再下决策，避免盲目内卷。

第二，“逐水草而居”与轻资产：不要局限于本地或本国。利用 Token/API 地区差价、中国供应链等优势，做业务的话要服务全球80亿人与未来20亿 AI Agent。
年轻时避免过早买房、买车或重资产绑死自己，哪里能创造最大价值就去哪里。

第三，学术/科研降维打击：AI 打破了传统顶尖学术圈的导师与信息垄断，高中生或研究生利用 AI 整理全球思路，即可在数学、生物学、天文学等数据密集型领域做出突破。（小编觉得这里还是理想化了一点...）

5.主动健康管理与抗衰科学

肌肉即“现金存量”：
身体在面对疾病或衰老时，会优先消耗肌肉。力量训练是在给身体“存现金/开抗衰杠杆”。
主动健康管理：
摒弃“生病才去医院”的旧观念，在无症状时借助 AI 提前筛查血脂、血糖、胆固醇等风险指标。
反驳老钱盲区：
马斯克、巴菲特等人忽视健身属于“屁股决定脑袋”的错误示范，年轻时练就薄肌是投资回报率最高的健康资产。

6.财富自由是先自由，再财富。

先自由，后财富：
自由是认知上的独立与高机动性；拥有自由后，财富是顺理成章的副产品
保持 Small Ego 与版本迭代：
像软件更新一样持续给认知打补丁（打 Patch），拒绝被过去成功的经验绑架，避免被时代淘汰。
多创造，少消费：
实现初步财务安全后，应将精力和资源投向创造性活动（事业、创作、教育等），实现飞轮的正向螺旋上升

7. Crypto 的本质：机器世界的货币
这部分观点行业里的人都很熟了，简单整理下就是：

传统金融（Swift）是电报时代的产物，无法适配硅基时代。Crypto 的本质是将人类的货币与账本翻译成 AI 和机器能直接读懂、可编程的去中心化语言。
未来无数 AI 与 AI 之间的微支付、即时结算，天然需要基于 Crypto 的底层网络。

text:
3.3亿美元HYPE退出质押，市场担心的解锁抛压，最后去了哪里？

昨天我们讨论，Hyperliquid每天都在回购HYPE，但这些买盘能不能抵消新增供应？

今天，团队的一笔大额代币转移，给了这个问题一个具体案例

约375万枚HYPE，价值约3.3亿美元，从Hyperliquid Labs退出质押

这么大的筹码，如果直接进入订单簿卖出，足以让持有人紧张

但按照链上数据显示，这批HYPE对应的是此前宣布的机构OTC出售，并没有直接通过公开盘口完成交易

也就是说，团队确实在出售代币，但机构通过场外交易承接了这批筹码

375万枚HYPE分两轮转入相同的五个新钱包，每个钱包累计收到75万枚，随后又汇集到一个曾由Kraken入金的钱包，这个接收钱包随后质押了312.5万枚HYPE，价值约2.76亿美元，选择的是Hyperliquid Strategies × Unit验证者

剩余62.5万枚，价值约5500万美元，被转入HyperEVM上的另一个钱包

换句话说，约83.3%的筹码，在转移后又进入了质押

市场原本担心的是：团队筹码释放以后，会不会变成集中卖单？

至少从这次追踪到的去向看，大部分筹码并没有立即进入公开市场出售，而是被接收方重新质押

不过Hyperliquid Strategies本身也在继续增加HYPE持仓，他们上周又买入约150万枚HYPE，价值约1.3亿美元，同时仍有约2.63亿美元现金可用

这说明，HYPE的承接力量并不只有Assistance Fund

协议用收入回购，机构则用自己的资金买入并持有

两种资金的作用不同

Assistance Fund的回购与协议收入相连，买回的代币按照既有机制移出流通；机构购买则把筹码转移到自己的资产负债表上。它可以长期持有，也可能因为融资、现金需求或投资策略变化而出售

无论买家是谁，现在市场可以知道长期供应由生态系统的合作伙伴持有，因此可以稳步前进，覆盖这些解锁。

author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
十年期美债收益率盘中一度突破了5.3%，最高到5.306%，随后仍在5.3%附近。从PCE公布后约5.20%的低点算起，已经反弹了超过10个基点，通胀数据带来的缓解没有维持住。

这次核心PCE环比增长0.2%，低于预期的0.3%，确实是好消息。但同一份报告里，个人消费支出增长了0.9%，即便扣掉涨价的影响，实际消费仍增长了0.6%，说明美国人的消费需求还很强。

也就是说，通胀比市场担心的温和一些，但需求并没有明显冷下来。再加上能源价格的压力仍在，仅凭这一次PCE，还不足以让市场相信美联储很快就能结束加息，或者让利率降下来。

这轮收益率反弹，更像是市场重新考虑高利率还要维持多久。投资者如果担心未来利率更高、通胀迟迟压不下来，就会要求更高的回报才愿意买债，债券价格因此被抛售，收益率往上走。

目前十月加息的市场概率已经降到了 37% 左右，说明十年期突破5.3%，并不意味着十月一定会加息。长债还在反映未来几年的利率和持有期间的风险。说人话，就是市场越来越相信美联储会维持高利率的时间更长，甚至接下来加息的概率上升。

而对市场来说，如果十年期收益率持续处于这样的高位，即便美联储十月暂时不加息，企业融资和居民房贷的成本也很难明显降下来。借钱成本仍然很高，股票估值也会继续承受压力。尤其是九月通胀数据如果继续走高，那么对于市场的压力会更大。

text:
【新加坡 TOKEN2049 参会实录：行业正在发生哪些变化？】

跑会小作文来啦！

忙碌了两三天之后，终于有时间可以跟大家分享一下本次参加新加坡 TOKEN2049 的见闻和思考了。

每次行业大会，作为全球最大的交易所，币安的活动可以说是TOKEN2049主会场之外最核心的分会场了。

因此，这次我们来新加坡，在两场活动专门布置了展台，一个是 TOKEN2049 主会场，另一个是 BNB Chain 的会场。

这里也主要基于这两场活动分享一下：

1️⃣ TOKEN2049 和 BNB Chain 两个会场，其实是割裂的两个圈子。

这两场活动我们都有展台，所以非常明显可以感受到两场活动的差异。

TOKEN2049 主会场大概80%都是老外，而 BNB Chain 会场80%都是华人。

从会场业态来看，主会场展台最多的是两类：交易所和加密货币支付相关项目，这也能很直观地看出目前的行业趋势。

而 BNB Chain 的会场，都是 BNB Chain 生态里面的一些头部项目，涵盖了meme、稳定币支付、链上合约、预测市场等等，也代表了BNB生态的热门趋势。

同时，参加两场活动的人群画像也完全不同：参加主会场的大多都是项目方、行业从业者；而参加 BNB Chain 活动的，更多是 KOL、交易员和大户。

另外，Token2049主会场严查门票，BNB会场是半开放式的。

如果说主会场是行业项目的商务局，那 BNB 会场就是华人玩家的游园会了。

2️⃣ 在 TOKEN2049 主会场主动来和我们咨询交流的，主要有三类人：

第一类，是做加密货币支付的，可以给我们提供法币或者加密货币的支付解决方案。

和他们沟通过程中发现，Fiat / 加密双向支付方案已经比较成熟了。

海外合规出入金、本地化支付基建，已经是所有出海项目的刚需标配了。

第二类，是各类营销机构，能够负责欧美、南美、非洲等地区的市场推广工作。

可以明显感知到，如果想要走出去，需要转变为精细化区域本地化运营，不同国家地区的差异很大，市场拓展方式也非常不一样。

第三类，就是其他项目方和行业从业者，大多是过来闲逛、了解我们项目的。

这部分人群看似不是直接转化，但也算是行业品牌认知、圈层曝光的潜在增量。

3️⃣ 这次参会我最大的感受是，线上和线下的情绪也是割裂的：线上悲观，线下乐观。

平时线上的社区，整体氛围是偏悲观的，充斥着行情噪音和负面情绪，大家似乎都很焦虑。

但来到线下我发现，大家的情绪完全不同。

很多从业者和用户对我们项目非常感兴趣，非常看好我们的发展，也很愿意深度参与进来。

也有一些深度用户给我们提了很多有价值的意见，想帮我们一起做得更好。

我也意识到一个事情：线上舆论是被情绪和行情主导的，线下活动是被价值和圈子主导的。

网上很多人都在喊垃圾市场、没机会；线下所有人都在找靠谱项目，在积极连接人脉。

大家会用脚投票，更愿意来到优质项目这里寻求机会。

因此，真正的优质项目，在线下反而会更加凸显，得到的认可度也远远高于线上。

这也是一种正向选择了。

4️⃣ 最后，我也想聊一聊，项目方到底要不要来参加展会、来线下到底值不值得。

我的建议很明确：对于刚起步的创业项目来说，不建议在主会场租展位，ROI 很低；而对于处于高速增长期或者成熟期的项目，非常有必要。

因为主会场的展位，核心作用不是转化，也不是对接客户、谈合作，更多是品牌秀肌肉、展示自身实力的方式。

主会场参展，最大的价值是做品牌曝光，让行业知道有你这个项目的存在，同时可以给我们和合作方、生态伙伴提供一个线下交流的场景。

所以这种模式，更适合有实力、需要做品牌的头部项目。这也是为什么主会场每层的核心展位，基本都是各大交易所，本质就是为了展示实力。

但是，不租展位 ≠ 不来参会，恰恰相反，线下参会、线下面对面交流，是当下行业性价比最高的动作。

这次线下之行，我们和长期的合作方、KOL以及核心深度用户，做了深度的沟通和交流，建立的信任感非常强。

一直以来我都觉得，现在这个时代，信任是人与人之间最稀缺的资源。

线上聊十次，不如线下见一次。

喧嚣在线上，机会在线下。

text:
The Tories keep saying they “made mistakes”.

Mistakes?

You governed this country for 14 years. These weren’t a few bad calls around the edges.

These were decisions that fundamentally changed Britain, some of them potentially forever.

They left us with the highest tax burden since WW2. Now they talk about cutting taxes.

They grew the state. They grew the Civil Service to historic levels. They let the welfare bill balloon. Now they talk about small government.

They buried businesses, financial markets, property and housebuilding under regulation.

Now they tell us regulation is strangling growth. No shit Sherlock.

But who wrote it?

They now say regulation stopped homes being built.

Who wrote it?

They milked Stamp Duty. Now they want to abolish it.

Home ownership fell dramatically on their watch. Now they have the audacity to tell us they are the party of home ownership.

London was one of the great centres of global finance. By 2024, the UK was down to 20th in the world for IPO fundraising.

One of the greatest financial centres on earth decimated by a Conservative government.

They enshrined Net Zero in law.

Now they want to abolish it, apparently they just realised how damaging it is to our economy. Kemi said countries with expensive energy are poor. Who made our energy expensive?

They allowed the Armed Forces to shrink while the rest of the state grew.

Now they tell us defence is the first duty of government.

Really?

Was it not the first duty of government during the 14 years you were actually the government?

They promised to stop the boats.

They didn’t.

They cut police numbers.

They closed magistrates’ courts.

They hollowed out the justice system.

And while people were being robbed, burgled, stabbed or having their shops emptied, the Conservatives had the audacity to arrest people for tweets.

And then there is immigration.

They promised to control it. Bring it down to tens of thousands.

Instead they gave us the Boris wave, just about 4 million people.

Net migration reached levels Britain had never seen before.

And this is exactly why calling these things “mistakes” doesn’t cut it.

Because you cannot simply reverse years of mass migration.
Some government decisions alter a country for a few years.
The Conservative’s decisions altered Britain for a generation.
Some may have altered it permanently.

And please spare us the “new Conservative Party”. It isn’t.

Kemi Badenoch was a minister.
Chris Philp was a minister.
Andrew Griffith was a minister and the Government’s Net Zero Business Champion.

Claire Coutinho was literally the Net Zero Secretary.
Richard Fuller was a Treasury minister.
Alex Burghart was a minister.

They were making the decisions. They had the power. They were the government.

Governments don’t get to experiment on a country for fourteen years, fundamentally change it, leave behind damaging consequences that could last for generations, change the wording on the leaflet and demand that everyone treats them as the new management.

These weren’t simply “mistakes”. They were deliberate choices.

Choices that changed our economy, our population and the size and reach of the state.

And some of those changes may never be fully undone. That is the arrogance of it.

The belief that you can make decisions of this magnitude, fundamentally change the country, wait for the political wind to turn and then say:

“Sorry. We got it wrong. Trust us to fix it.”

No, you broke Britain and only Reform will fix it.

text:
Statement on Trump Suspending Microsoft from the PERM Program:

This is a crucial issue for me as the top Democrat on the Immigration Subcommittee, the only member of Congress to have actually had an H-1B visa, and the Representative for tens of thousands of Microsoft workers. The administration has been consistently working to take away legal pathways for immigrants to contribute their talents to our country, and this is yet another of those attacks.

The PERM program is the first step toward an employment-based green card for countless workers who want to contribute to this country, and it lays out a clear process with steps to ensure that this is a net benefit to our economy and does not harm American jobs. Our economy, our communities, and our families depend on immigrants in many sectors, including the tech sector, and heavy-handed attacks like this only hurt efforts to build a strong, stable, and diverse base of workers who have legal pathways to come and be in the United States while also protecting U.S. workers from unscrupulous employers.

You don’t fix a broken immigration system by taking a hammer to legal immigration. Microsoft has been a leader in advocating for comprehensive immigration reforms that modernize an antiquated immigration system and provide more — not fewer — legal pathways for immigrants from all over the world to work here and be with their families. Targeting Microsoft or the PERM program in this way simply undermines legal immigration and weakens America’s ability to innovate.

text:
the long version: why an onchain bucket shop ends at zero, with the LP simulation. 

 https://t.co/nKcvHFL63z
author: D2_Finance
quoted_text:
Jez read Reminiscences of a Stock Operator and shipped it on top Hyperliquid’ tech ( not @Lighter_xyz )

onchain bucket shop. he confirmed it in this thread under @dipsybitsy “yep, fully transparent and the losers who fund it will own.”

the bucket shop pattern is 100 years old. customer trades at the listed price, the house takes the other side, nothing reaches the actual exchange. 

Livermore made his early stake trading against them, then got banned from every shop in Boston for being too good. they died from two pressures: directional regimes that smoked the house, and ticker manipulation where operators pushed the real venue to harvest at the shop. both are live here. neither is solved by stacking five defensive parameters.

what is actually onchain: a contract that reads HL’s BBO via precompile and synthesises swaps against a Martingaler LP. zero flow reaches HL’s orderbook. zero funding rebalance. the only feedback loop is parasitic. 

BBO manipulation attempts to harvest the synthetic spread degrade HL’s book without compensating the makers wearing the jitter. the venue extracts liquidity quality from @HyperliquidX ( fair enough!)

the fair launch plus 1000x leverage plus PAPER mint-on-loss design is engineered for initial FOMO. expect a fast first week/month. Jez’ inner circle volume comes in, asymmetric impact taxes the few winners, losers fund the LP and mint PAPER, the chart can look initially great if execute right. 

this is the bootstrap window the docs explicitly subsidise at 100 PAPER per $1 of LP gain below 2M.

Then path dependence will shows up. 

LP edge per trade is thin: 0.2 bps jitter band plus the convex bite of asymmetric impact on winning closes. order of magnitude, on a $1M ticket the LP edge is in the tens to low hundreds of dollars. one 5% adverse move on $1M of net synthetic exposure is $50,000 of MTM loss. edge accrues like √t under stationary flow. directional regime hits the LP linearly in t. √t vs t means one persistent trend eats months of accrual. 

the half life of LP equity in a trending regime is short, and it gets shorter as size scales because the OI cap trails realised OI rather than leading it.

then the debt queue activates. 

martingaler issues claims paid by the next loser. once the queue is observable, the EV of opening a new position is negative twice: once because winners get haircut, once because withdrawals sit behind every prior bust. rational flow stops. Queue does not clear. 

PAPER, a claim on future LP revenue, is then a claim on revenue that must clear the queue first.

the cross-venue attack (@NaiveKrypto point in the thread) has its own path dependence. 

wicking HL spot or perp to harvest the synthetic at the shifted BBO is only EV-positive once papertrade’s OI is large enough that the harvest exceeds the cost of pushing HL. 

below that threshold, no one bothers. above it, every desk with an HL maker does. 

self-limiting at small scale, openly hostile at large scale. the steady state is zero, the only question is the path.

all bucket shops are zero in short to medium term. the 1900s wave died within two decades, mostly to regulation and to operators eating them. the onchain version skips regulation but keeps the operators and adds a debt queue that hard-codes path dependence into the equity curve. the docs read like a list of every defence shops historically tried, in order. 

stacking five does not change the shape of the failure mode, it just shifts where the failure surfaces.
closing thought. the whole structure is short volatility against directional flow, dressed up as a perpetuals venue. 

it is the same trade as a Korean retail account systematically selling MRNA noise reversion while their own KOSPI 200 trends straight through the stop. works beautifully until the regime turns, then the half life is a week.

clever paper, novel emissions curve, real engineering. the structure is 100 years older than the precompile.

author: farokh
quoted_text:
Everyone is free to make their own decisions on allocation. I applaud decisive decision making. No specific comment vs OP below, in fact am not super familiar w metavestor so truly have no pro/against him/her personally

Speaking to the points:
1) Measuring for tail events is savvy as a personal wealth decision. Everything worth doing however, usually has some sort of drag / burden / hurdle to it. Measuring & checking against priors is something you pretty much have to do with everything. It may feel unacceptable to some that the underlying asset in of itself faces security risk. That is understandable. To me, that is a category of risk that the market has actually shown itself as being ready to digest in capacity over time: bridge/exchange exploits, LUNA, Celsius/FTX, USDC depeg, etc. It is not equivalent of course, but they all speak to binary sponsorship unravelling & going to 0

BTC's history in fact predates this as -

2) I would argue that total perceived risk was actually much higher: RE: custody risk + rug risk + adoption risk + legal risk being elevated in BTC's infancy; namely an existential question to whether BTC would even graduate to being a social consensus asset. The reason this risk existed is probably a big primary driver of its return

So let's just be clean about this: the risk reward PROFILE isn't appealing to the author. The risk in an absolute sense itself is not the issue - in fact, it seems the author actually prefers HIGHER absolute left tail existential risk if anything - biotech RE: the most risk probably of any industry, see picture attached). Maybe the precision element is meaningful to the author though. This is not meant as a "gotcha" comment. Intended to be exploratory, because I do not think the sentence written as-is actually makes sense

3) "Does this make you want to long crypto?" - a peer of mine writes. In an absolute sense, no. That is obvious. However, does the escalation in the war on Iran make you want to long QQQ? Did Liberation Day make you want to long memory? The reason I bring this up is that markets rarely move on the margin on things that are *true* in an absolute sense. It is probably the 3rd, 4th or 5th derivative that matters. So not 2026 revenue, or QoQ revenue growth, or guidance on QoQ revenue growth, but rather what consensus was on QoQ revenue growth, and the actual ▲ beat/miss b/w Q2 reported & that

The reason this is important to bring up is that if there was some advancement in AI that specifically attached to crypto and only cryptocurrencies, that is net bearish ubiquitously. A potentially emerging super-cracker that can crack anything is just horrible for all things finance; this includes attaching/attacking bigger vulnerabilities & bigger industries with more liquidity. But in a world where there are bank runs and resulting anarchy, I think there is an argument to be made that permission-less currency ends up gaining MORE relative value net overall, especially vs fiat. Do you know how hard it is to withdraw even $10K cash from a bank? Do you actually think your bank / the gov't is going to step in and cover you? It is probably investing calories on what this draconian world looks like. The more concept of money would be very challenged - your passwords included.

4. I think the author misses or misunderstands what quantum concerns are. Quantum FUD and AI FUD is exactly the same. Which is: assuming unbounded leaps in progress that the human capacity cannot account for yet [assuming weeks, not years] it is theoretically possible that cryptography is cracked

Lastly, the author writes that the appeal of crypto initially to him/her was the tech, and that may/does not appeal any longer. That is a strong claim, but that was easily the case 2 years ago, and at the minimum 1 year ago. I just mostly think the author did not update his/her priors on this, and, like many do, use interesting events like this as an excuse/push to do something they had wanted to do for a while anyways

Ultimately, it seems that the author's argument is that banks are Too Big To Fail, which is why Drake's update is uniquely bad for crypto. I do not agree. Monetization of hacking is actually really worth thinking about & what that looks like too

My stance -
1) The Drake update will be a positive one in hindsight and may actually elicit real change with people taking preventive measures more seriously
2) Custody probably moves toward being coupled (so not DEFI) and around ETFs vs cold storage
3a) This was not the reason for the sell-off. You do not have to take my word for it - BTC and QQQ are down the exact same amount (~80 bps) since Drake's tweet. The OpenAI $20B revenue miss has more to do w risk pop than this, in all likelihood
3b) If Drake's update made you want to short, 3a) isn't actually bad for you if you think the mkt has not moved sufficiently on this, as it has yet to happen. If you are under writing this as the reason for being short/bearish, I believe you are mistaken
4) Apologies for all this word slop - it is worth noting though that I am bearish locally. Just had to make it clear it is not because of any of this

text:
📱从区块链钱包到 NFT，三星的七年 Web3 探索

三星与加密行业的联系，可以追溯到 2019 年。

当年，三星围绕 Galaxy S10 提供区块链钱包和 Keystore 私钥保护能力，并介绍面向开发者的 Blockchain Platform SDK。开发者可以将区块链功能整合进移动应用，用户则可以通过手机管理加密资产、访问去中心化应用。

2021 年，Samsung Blockchain Wallet 又增加了与 Ledger Nano S、Nano X 等外部硬件钱包连接的支持，让用户通过 Galaxy 设备查看和管理相关加密资产。

这一阶段的产品重心，是私钥保护、资产管理和开发者工具。它们主要围绕已经需要使用区块链应用的人展开。

2022 年，三星推出 Samsung Wallet，将支付卡、会员卡、密码和数字钥匙等功能集中到一个应用。当时公告还宣布。其加密资产相关功能，则包括集中查看部分交易所的持仓价值。

同年，三星也在不同消费电子场景中探索 NFT，但电视与 Galaxy 的合作范围需要分开理解。

在电视领域，三星收购的 NFT 市场 Nifty Gateway 合作，围绕部分电视产品提供 NFT 浏览、购买、交易和展示能力。值得一提的是，Nifty Gateway 在 2026 年 2 月份正式宣布关闭。

在 Galaxy 生态中，三星与 Theta Labs 等合作方签署意向书，计划让 Galaxy NFT 持有人通过认证获得折扣、积分等线下权益。这里的重点是数字纪念品与消费权益的连接。

到了 2025 年，三星与 Coinbase 的合作进一步涉及加密交易的支付入口。7 月，双方宣布在 Coinbase 应用内接入 Samsung Pay，方便符合条件的用户购买加密资产或为账户充值；10 月，三星又为符合条件的 Samsung Wallet 用户提供 Coinbase One 会员权益。

与此前的合作相比，2026 年 10 月宣布的 USDC 功能提出了新的产品方向：直接在 Samsung Wallet 内提供稳定币转账和跨境汇款体验。

由此看，三星探索的场景正在延伸到更具体的资金转移需求。不过，这些是不同产品、不同阶段的尝试。

A note from our research leaders:

Last week we parted ways with Jasmine, Mikita, and Tomek after a thorough investigation found they violated clear policies on handling sensitive information. Our internal investigation uncovered a significant breach of trust beyond what’s outlined in the letter they published and we stand by the decision to not continue their employment. We generally keep individual employment matters private and don't believe a back and forth would be productive or lead to a resolution, but we want to address the points they raised in their letter directly.

- We want to be very clear that these decisions were not about raising safety concerns or speaking out. Safety and research debates happen every day at OpenAI, often spirited and highly critical. We actively encourage these discussions and consider them essential to making the right decisions. We cannot do the work in front of us without a high degree of trust. We will continue to be extremely forgiving of our team making good-faith mistakes. We have not and do not terminate any of our employees for raising concerns.

- We are actively finalizing contracts with third-party safety assessors and will announce details in the coming weeks. People across the company have been working really hard on getting these partnerships up and running. We are committed to embedding external assessors and continue to make close collaboration with independent safety organizations a core part of our safety work. Many of our researchers already work with 3p safety organizations productively.

- We agree with the letter that preserving the monitorability of frontier models requires an industry-wide commitment, including from OpenAI. Monitorability has long been a core piece of our research program, and something we continue to invest significant resources in (see our publications on Monitoring Monitorability and the subsequent open sourcing of monitorability evals, our system card for GPT-6 Astra, Jakub’s blog and post on X, and the numerous blog posts on our Alignment blog on the topic).

We are deeply sad about this outcome. We appreciated Jasmine, Mikita, and Tomek’s contributions to AI safety at OpenAI and their willingness to speak up and challenge ideas. We championed their voices, supported their work, and placed enormous trust in them. These decisions were not about them raising safety concerns. We have always encouraged that and always will.
