text:
深刻学习了四个小时孙哥和艾伦的访谈
精简内容如下，没资源背景也可落地执行：

第一幕：能跟 AI 对话，就不要跟人类对话

孙哥把一条原则推到很极端：能跟 AI 对话，就不要跟人类对话。吃饭时他会问 Claude 先吃哪一口、再吃哪一口。每天饭前拍一张、饭后拍一张，用来估算摄入了多少卡路里。现在也在用蛋白粉和肌酸，吃完就练，动作主要是硬拉、深蹲这几个。训练日练，非训练日正常工作，日子就按训练日和非训练日分开。

他真的在践行这条原则，一直问 Claude Code：今天摄入了多少卡路里。他还有睡眠监测的智能指环，两者相减，就能估出今天烧掉了多少脂肪。

专门给 Claude 开了健身项目：拍照、教练录视频发给 Claude 纠动作、写训练日记。全部 AI 化、可视化、数据化，照片和文件存在本地，写成 md，同时建理论。

第二幕：没资源、没人脉，怎么重新开始

现在是最好的时代。一个月可支配收入不超过一千块人民币，也可以一个一个讲。Claude 太贵就先不用，注册 Kimi，找便宜的模型装上，把所有东西收进一个 md。先全部 AI 化、整合，生活全部 AI 化，用理论武装自己。眼下最重要的就是 AI 化，零成本开始。我要 md 文档，每天去各个 AI 薅免费额度。

零基础起步就是三套理论

第一是孙学：

用理论武装自己，对万事万物的理解都用孙学升级

第二是薄肌：

身体健康很重要，薄肌一定要练

第三是黄毛理论：

做了会挨笑、会遭嫉妒，别人说什么不管，自己认为对的就直接执行

这三套，从 20 岁用到 40 岁。坚信自己的路，最核心的掌舵者是 AI。相信 AI 的话，随时随地可执行。

要把自己的现状变成数据，全部 AI 化，做现状分析，让它帮你分析。随时有问题就问 AI。还要建立对人类科技文明走向的观察，抓最新前沿，AI 抓和自己抓都可以，找到最感兴趣的去钻。以 AI 为主，其他为辅。升级思想，也升级身体。问 AI：我要升级。从跟微信聊天到跟豆包聊天是升级，从豆包到用 API 跟全球 AI 聊天又是升级

所有文件记得保存在本地，这是最重要的。写一个 md，让它读取你自己，又是一波升级。

第三幕：年轻人最值得做的方向

所有东西都会变便宜，年轻就是财富，只有时间最宝贵。所有行业都会被 AI 改变，都充满机会。AI 是乱拳打死老师傅，它能分析、能往前探路。数学上，你都能顺着 AI 给的思路，一步走到博士水平。AI 拉平了人与人的差距，把人彻底解放出来。天文学也有很大进展。挣钱的路太多了，合法的也超级多。

API 价格各地不一样。做 token 中转，或者代充、地理套利，商机要到全球去找，不要局限在自己的国家。必须全球性地发现需求，做全球的生意，各地需求其实差不多。千万不要把自己限死。

商业最基本的是有没有创造价值

比如 token，有的地方便宜、有的地方贵，你让贵的地方用上便宜的，价值就体现在客户面前。中国也遍地是机会。把东西卖到全世界，把想法卖到全世界，就不用发愁卖不出去。要走向世界，跳出眼前这个处境。

不建议年轻人只按自己的思路下判断，可以多学、多听、多看。买房先看一百套房，买车先看一百辆车，地段什么的都看。读书百遍，其义自现。中国大学生面对一百个行业，不必急着自己做决定。先看一百个专业。问题是自己看得太少。

一定要先把图打开，信息多了，判断才会更正确

先探图，再针对性造兵，不要急着造。玩游戏也是这样：把地球 Online 当成游戏去看、去玩，然后再做决定。打王者荣耀也一样，要知道对面开什么、打了多少野、什么时候开龙。

第四幕：年轻人的五条路，以及薄肌

点出年轻人的几条路：数学、生物、天文学。这几条数据量大的路都可以走。AI 更擅长自己处理数据，学术界也一样，很多算法会被颠覆，需要年轻人去做，包括数据清洗。现在是捡钱行情。20 到 40 岁是最好的年纪。有了 AI，遍地可以捡钱，但一定要用上。再夸张一点：大学生加 AI，有机会超过诺贝尔奖那个量级

最简单的是练薄肌，需要时间，但一上手就立竿见影。年轻人必须练。Claude 说过一句：你想 80 岁自己走进来吃饭，还是被人推着轮椅进来？有薄肌，就是自己走进来。巴菲特没薄肌，所以是被推进来的。生物规律没办法抗拒，自然规律不可违背，所以要练。人均都该有薄肌。AI 时代没有借口，只有执行。人的时间会更宝贵，主要时间就拿来练薄肌。

碳基和硅基要分清：我们要的是碳基超长待机
年轻人练薄肌，杠杆很高，机会也遍地都是

怎么才能活得长？

大概 25 分在肌肉，25 分在心肺，薄肌都能往上加，而且薄肌可以自动燃脂。这条路几乎只有薄肌。它符合科学依据，年轻时就要练，喝蛋白粉没问题。认知很重要：自己想明白肌肉有益健康，才能把《薄肌圣经》看下去。先认定薄肌是对的，才看得进去。

第五幕：财富自由之后，下一个十年怎么规划

孙哥的理论是：去有鱼的地方捕鱼，逐水草而居。哪个地方能发挥最大价值，就去哪里。能赚钱，就说明价值大。行业里的溢价，AI 最有潜力。不要买车、买房、结婚把自己定死。很多人说要跟老婆商量，于是拒绝去大城市，这是错的，会把自己框死。机动性要强，灵活性最重要。选适合自己的。理论小众是好事，小众往往就是风口。骂得多，反而说明越来越对。

第六幕：孙宇晨在干什么

问到 Tron、孙宇晨奖，以及把数据证明翻译成 Lean。这部分意思不大，可以跳过。

第七幕：自媒体、数字化与认知

自媒体时代，数字化非常重要。人要先发言，才可能给出更正确的发言。这些平台产出的结果，大概率是对的，推特就是一个很好的平台。

AI 是挡不住的趋势，数字货币是未来方向。赚钱是做对的事，不要逆趋势。大胆做异类，异类才会有大结果。很多人不成，是因为失败了还停在原地。自媒体是很好的杠杆，做自媒体就是做多自己。

让 AI 来测：要求自己测哪些数据。没症状也要做，主动健康管理会成为主流。很多人不练肌肉，还是缺执行力，这是认知缺陷。要对自己的健康负责，自己执行这些理论。认知决定命运。

这个 AI 时代，认知就是最关键的，甚至比赚钱更关键。越有钱、越成功，自我会越强，就越容易跟不上时代。

张罗起来之后就开始实行薄肌理论，该测的指标都测了。孙哥说自己占了薄肌理论的便宜，本质上是更容易升级、追求健康。与其攻击，不如赶紧加入。

一代版本一代神。认知要不断升级。良言只能劝有心人，只能救愿意改变的人。

小我很重要：根据对面的信息，做出行为上的改变。拿到新信息就改。世界上不怎么存在抽象的“智商”，更多是信息灌进去多少。所有东西都在灌注信息。

要当六边形战士，所以都要吸收。认知逐步迭代，智商是认知的外显。版本很重要。

第八幕：地球 Online 的版本更新

地球 Online 也一样，会大版本更新
房地产砍掉百分之五十，AI 加上百分之一百，核心还是 AI

能跟 AI 对话，就不要跟人类对话。去做基础设施。地球 Online 版本更新慢，两年一更，虽迟但到，这个版本一定会出来，会修 bug。马斯克也有认知缺陷，除非到了伟人那个级别。年轻人反而好，因为听得进劝。现在什么钱都没有，更容易听进去；自我太强的人听不进去。年轻人只需要一键安装

第九幕：财富自由之路，先自由后财富

财富自由之路的博客，十年之后孙哥说要更新，把薄肌的补丁理论也写进去。也有了新的 AI 工具，医生知道怎么做是对的。我们要更新自己的版本。什么是财富自由，要升级一下。

孙哥说：先自由，后财富。财富是伴生品。重要的是先搞清楚理论，再去玩。

跟打王者一样，先懂机制，再练英雄，才能带妹。自由了，才更容易获得财富。

自由不需要门槛，是自己给自己的，是认知上的提升。你认为自己自由一点，就更容易获取财富，这是螺旋上升的飞轮。

练薄肌可以睡得更少，然后更愿意练，进入正循环。要改变自己，缺的还是执行力。定好就坚持，做成一套完整的飞轮。先建立认知。

农民工的薄肌往往是被动练出来的，所以要先懂了再说。先懂，再执行。理论要先悟道，悟道太重要。时间会证明一切。

悟了和没悟，背后都要有理论。先把人吸引过来，再讲认知体系。聊了很多地球 Online 的运行机制。认知更新太重要了。

第十幕：有钱解决不了的，还是认知

真正有钱之后，什么是钱解决不了的？还是认知。有钱不一定有认知。可以玩一个游戏：有了三千万，或者今天中了三千万，怎么破产。先自由，后财富。

第十一幕：婚姻和家庭

怎么看婚姻和家庭？孙哥说看不懂婚姻和感情。感情跟有多少钱没关系。这块还没打补丁，现在还不行。

第十二幕：人活着的意义

其实是玩家心态。人被扔进地球 Online，还在探索期，逐步摸清一些门道

为什么要灌注更多信息？

AI 也是混沌体系，人生目前也在混沌里

前百分之五十先看，后百分之五十觉得对了，再下结论、出理论。孙哥说悟道了再说。知道得越多，越不能急着下结论。在这个游戏里，领悟就是更深一层，就是享受生活，just enjoy now。先看，看完再发表观点。先增加体验，把数据灌给自己。理论用来解释行为。孙哥用的是体验论、实验的态度：先上了再说，先做了再说，拿到信息之后再消化。先别急着结束，可以再等等、再看看、多试试。不要提早下结论。体验大于结论。

人生的意义是体验的集合，体验就是一切。孙哥要在推进体验的路上一直走。

第十三幕：三个标杆，以及体验本身

孙哥的三个标杆：马斯克、巴菲特、特朗普

从他们身上吸收商业的极致、科技、长期，以及个人 IP。商业基本盘从这三个人来。中国学马云。不要过早把自己的思维定型，要触类旁通

人生没有标准答案。在成为“最正确的答案”的人之前，自己都不知道自己是不是正确答案。每个人都有自己的地图

很多人一开始追求意义，追求意义没什么意义，体验本身才有意义。文学是体验的结果

人生的体验，只要大方向对，就没什么错

尽情去体验，不用纠结自己是不是一直在唯一正确的路上。只要打的方向是对的就可以，不必一直在意意义

text:
Token2049 Summary for those that missed it

1. Avoid main conference and big side events at all costs
The main event was busing in loads of chinese tourists and there were halls and halls of scammy projects (as usual). Tourists cleaned the hell up on merch, some could barely walk with all the oversized bags

2. Few of the big ecosystems tried to run massive events and they all sucked, too crowded inside and well, standing outside in smokey & hot singapore surrounded by sweaty cryptobros is the most awful experience known to mankind, would say 90% of the side events were skippable

I wont name and shame but you can probably guess

3. I didn't go but Staking Summit and Vault Summit seem like a complete waste of time. Listening to a third day of panels about how "institutions are coming but they need more KYC and compliance solutions" should be actively shunned by the space, especially at an additional $700 a ticket. But I suppose where else will you meet hungover BDs for trading firms and custodians walking around in suits

4. Conversations were bullish - tokenization is growing and that trend seems to be one way, anyone building in the RWA space will have a massive opportunity

5. @EthereumHK threw a decent event with guys like Joseph Lubin @joechalom, shoutout to the SNZ guys who are super active in building up APAC region

6. @ether_fi lounge let you skip the main conference ticket but still "get in" and have meetings at the venue. Amazing utility for card holders

7. Coinbase event was surprisingly not cringe, they had a good choice with @TaikiMaeda2 and @gazza_jenks, good deal of top leadership there and guys like Jesse walking around chatting with people 

8. Private meetings set up before the event are the only way to go, if you go and just follow the crowds you will have an awful experience, but for those that hustle its really positive ROI

Will be back next year

我用本地模型 VibeCoding，做了个四驱兄弟风格的 3D 赛车游戏

这个游戏基本复刻小时候的玩法，先选车、配装备，比赛： 
1. 内置4 款赛车精美模型 
2. 2. 有5 种组件自己搭配，比如换导轮、换轮胎， 
3. 还有3 个赛道，还能放大招，把对手压扁😂

而这么一套游戏，我花了一天时间，用本地大模型跑出来了！！

咋一天就做出来了呢？

首先我本地部署一个千亿参数的大模型，让它负责写游戏代码。

然后赛车模型，我是用 Tripo3D 来生成：

传入四张参考图生成车模，再把组件拆出来，接进 Godot 后，把导轮、轮胎这些部件做成可以选配、更换的装备

最后再让本地大模型把换装、比赛和大招这些玩法接起来

看完下面这段实录，有视频有真相👇
Tripo 的体验链接放评论区了，想做自己的赛车模型可以试试

text:
Empire Market Co-Founder Sentenced to 40 Years, Forfeits 1,230 BTC

According to the U.S. Department of Justice, Empire Market co-founder Raheim Hamilton was sentenced to 40 years in federal prison for a drug conspiracy offense and fined $5 million. From 2018 to 2020, the darknet marketplace facilitated more than 4 million transactions worth over $430 million, including nearly $375 million in net drug sales.

The platform required all transactions to be conducted in cryptocurrency and encouraged users to use mixing services. Hamilton pleaded guilty and agreed to forfeit about 1,230 BTC, 24.4 ETH and three properties. Co-founder Thomas Pavey also previously pleaded guilty and agreed to forfeit about 1,584 BTC and other assets, with sentencing expected later this month.

quoted_text:
(Warning: Long post about Israel. Possible slow-motion crash out. Might want to skip this one.)

This statement from @NYCMayor is evil.

There’s no other way to describe it. “Despicable” isn’t nearly strong enough; “lamentable” implies that it’s something over which we might feel sorrow, rather than the outrage it demands.

“Evil” is the only word for it. Deeply, profoundly evil. Perhaps the most vile statement a prominent US elected official has ever released.

On the third anniversary of the worst loss of Jewish life since the Holocaust, Mayor Mamdani—leader of the city with the world’s largest Jewish population outside of Tel Aviv—has released a statement that minimizes the attacks, ignores the severity and depravity of Hamas’s crimes, and—in a manner with just enough skillful subtlety to provide necessary levels of plausible deniability—inverts the day’s attackers and victims, even obliquely blaming the victims themselves. A statement that references the attacks’ perpetrators, Hamas, but once, and the attacks’ target, the Jews of Israel, not at all.

Let me repeat that: The mayor of a city with nearly one million Jews spread across its five boroughs can’t find it within himself to use the word “Jew” on the anniversary of the worst loss of Jewish life since the genocide of Nazi Germany.

Mamdani dedicates one—and only one—paragraph in his statement to the attacks themselves. One perfunctory, halfhearted paragraph; a token gesture of mourning that conveniently omits the savagery of Hamas’s crimes, the widespread sexual violence of the day, the glee with which terrorists butchered young and old alike, and the deplorable conditions in which 251 innocent victims of kidnapping were kept in subterranean tunnels in Gaza.

One paragraph. That’s all. And, with that out of the way, with that box conveniently checked, Mamdani is able to get to his real aim: Condemning Israel.

And this he does with detail and gusto, without pause, reservation, or equivocation.

The entire second paragraph is worth reviewing line by line, for it is rich in subtle but deliberate manipulation.

Sentence 1: “The suffering did not begin or end that day.”

This is the classic Marxist rhetorical tactic of “contextualizing,” in which any actions that might reflect poorly on The Cause (e.g., the mass rape, murder, and kidnapping of innocent Israeli civilians) are positioned in the context of information meant to mitigate their severity, deflect blame, and shift responsibility from the victim to the offender.

In this case, Mamdani wants the reader to subconsciously think that Hamas’s acts of terrorism can only be viewed in the context of Israel’s historical and ongoing oppression of Palestine (hence “did not begin…that day”). And, with that context established, how could anyone hold Hamas at fault? After all, they didn’t start this war; they were only responding to “suffering [that] did not begin…that day.” If anything, it’s Israel that’s at fault, right?

If this sounds like reversing the victim and the offender—the RVO in the DARVO acronym used to describe the gaslighting of domestic violence victims—it’s because it is. It’s subversive, it’s diabolical, and it’s only the first sentence of the paragraph.

Let’s keep going.

Sentence 2: “It instead continued through the Israeli government’s devastating, ongoing genocide in Gaza…”

Hamas’s terrorism was not a de novo act, occurring without cause or justification; rather, it was merely the “ongoing” continuation of a long chain of “suffering” whose origin and fault lie with the state of Israel.

Also, note the choice of the words “devastating” and “genocide” and compare them to Mamdani’s first paragraph. He is condemning Israel’s response to the attacks with language far more forceful than that used to decry the attacks themselves.

Sentence 2, continued: “…in which it has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians—including more than 21,000 children.”

This is additional contextualization. The reader is directed to compare 74,000 dead Palestinians with the aforementioned 1,100 Israelis and come away with the interpretation that Israel is orders of magnitude more violent than Hamas. Note that Mamdani also includes a body count for Palestinian children but not for Israeli children.

Left unsaid, of course, is the proportion of those 74,000 dead Palestinians who were active Hamas fighters. Or whom Hamas was using as human shields. Or who were—unfortunately—collateral damage from being in the vicinity of the Israeli military’s justified airstrikes on Hamas fighters who deliberately intersperse themselves among the civilian populace of Gaza.

Sentence 3: “Even since the so-called ceasefire, more than 1,400 Palestinians have been killed.”

This is more contextualizing. The implicit message is that Israel has killed more Palestinians “since the so-called ceasefire” than Hamas killed in total. Israel’s response must therefore clearly be disproportionate.

Sentence 4: “That suffering has intensified with every Israeli bomb dropped on ambulances waiting outside hospitals, every drone strike targeting a residential building or journalist, and every shipment of food aid turned away at a border crossing.”

Setting aside factual errors and omissions of relevant context (ironic, given all the false contextualizing elsewhere!), note the specificity with which Mamdani condemns Israel. Israel’s response to October 7 warrants vivid detail—its bombs fall on ambulances, its drone strikes target residential buildings and journalists, its soldiers turn away food shipments—while the details of Hamas’s attacks on October 7 are described with…

Nothing.

No mention of the murders. The rapes. The desecration of bodies. The smiles on the terrorists’ faces; their laughter while livestreaming the carnage on social media and while calling their own parents.

Not one word.

When Israel responds to terrorism, graphic details are called for; when Hamas commits the underlying acts of terrorism in the first place, though, it warrants only a cursory mention in the introduction to the statement, no details necessary.

Sentence 5: “Many New Yorkers are reckoning with this unbearable grief, and we mourn alongside them – all while knowing that our tax dollars fund these war crimes.”

Note the similarities in language between this sentence and the final sentence of the first paragraph. The reader is meant to draw parallels between Israel’s dead civilians and Hamas’s dead fighters. The parallel language is meant to convey a false moral equivalence between the two.

Also note the reference to “our tax dollars”: You paid for this. You are morally complicit. Therefore, if you object to the mayor’s statement, you are just trying to willfully ignore your own guilt. How dare you.

The last two paragraphs (yes, he keeps going) are more of the same. More moral equivocation, more inversion of responsibility, more criticism of Israel. The word “apartheid” is thrown in for good measure, of course, because no statement on the anniversary of the worst day in modern Israel’s history would be complete without undermining the nation’s very existence.

Every word of this is shameful, every sentence detestable, every paragraph overflowing with covert lies and overt moral cowardice.

But we should expect nothing less of Zohran Mamdani, a man whose only talent is the ongoing profanation of an office he doesn’t deserve, in a great city he will slowly—or maybe not so slowly—destroy.

This statement—and the man behind it—are worthy of nothing but our scorn and should warrant nothing but our contempt.

text:
Looking at $CLAUDIA again, the most immediate catalyst behind this rally is anabology officially launching Claudia Gallery and explicitly stating the goal of making Claudia the open Hatsune Miku of the AI era.

2j5SaS7xy776qCBpyPQbZjyQSAtKiFgrwjfErthnW2ZM 

Rather than simply releasing another AI-generated piece of content, this feels more like the creator is beginning to build a long-term IP and opening it up for other creators to participate in.

I believe the market is reassessing Claudia's potential ceiling. Previously, it was more like an AI character gaining attention through anabology's creative ability and personal influence. Now, the project is beginning to connect the character, artwork, community token, and product platform.

The website explicitly states that trading fees from CLAUDIA will fund film production, while useclaudiaxyz continues to expand products such as Agent Skills and Claudia Local. This means the project is no longer just an AI character; it is beginning to develop along two paths: content production and a tools platform.

I believe the market is currently betting on three main directions. First, can anabology continue creating Claudia-related content and turn personal influence into sustained attention for the character? Second, can Claudia become an open AI creative IP, allowing more people to create music, videos, and artwork around the character instead of relying on a single creator? Third, can useclaudiaxyz evolve from a product showcase into an AI creation and Agent tools platform with genuine users?

Compared with a typical AI meme, I believe the open IP narrative is the more compelling long-term thesis for Claudia. The significance of the Hatsune Miku comparison is not how popular the character itself is, but whether other creators can continuously build around it, allowing content production and distribution to gradually move beyond a single creator. If Claudia can achieve this, its attention ceiling will no longer depend entirely on what anabology releases each time.

Fundamentals have strengthened compared with before, but a complete economic flywheel has yet to emerge. Using trading fees to fund film production creates a potential link between community trading and content creation. However, we still need to verify whether funds are consistently being deployed into production, whether the content can sustain attention, and whether these activities will generate demand for the token. The same applies to Agent Skills and Claudia Local: the product direction is visible, but genuine usage and sustained demand still need to be proven.

Looking ahead, the catalysts worth watching are more original Claudia content, participation from independent creators, sustained usage of the Agent products, and actual execution of the film-funding mechanism. If these developments gradually materialize, the market will have a stronger basis for revaluing CLAUDIA from a meme dependent on its creator's influence into a community asset with an open IP and product ecosystem.

The main risk is that the market may already be pricing in this vision ahead of its realization. An open IP requires continuous creation and community participation, while Agent tools need real users. The creator's influence does not automatically translate into token value. If anabology's influence fails to develop into an independent creator community, or product usage fails to grow, this revaluation may lack further support.

My final take is that this rally is pricing in the possibility of Claudia evolving from an AI character into an open IP. I will continue watching anabology's creative output, participation from independent creators, and the development of useclaudiaxyz. For the token, however, the most important factor remains whether growth in the community and product can translate into genuine, sustained token demand.

From a chart perspective, I believe CLAUDIA has completed its transition from bottom consolidation to its first breakout attempt. It is now at a critical confirmation stage following that breakout. Rather than trying to predict how high it can go, the key is to watch whether the $850K market cap level holds and whether volume returns as the pullback ends. If both conditions are met, there will be stronger grounds to expect a second leg higher.

quoted_text:
A few people yesterday asked how AI could impact FHE / @zama, so here is a quick tldr:

1. There is no evidence that lattices / FHE can be broken by AI, SI or quantum. If anything, there is a growing consensus that fully breaking lattices might imply P = NP. 

2. However, it's almost certain that better attacks will be discovered, which would require increasing parameter size and taking a short-term hit on performance. The Zama protocol is modular, so we can increase parameters size or swap out any component quickly, without changing the UX or rotating user keys.

3. Zama uses FHE only for privacy, so breaking FHE would not allow stealing funds that are shielded, it would only allow seeing balances and amounts. This is unlike ZK, where breaking the cryptography means you can steal funds and mint infinite tokens. 

4. We do a lot of work on cryptanalysis and improving the security of FHE. We spend millions a year on audits (AI and human), research grants, bounties, have 30 PhDs in the team, etc. We have a plan A (the current thing we do), but also a plan B and a plan C if things go wrong. Whatever the future throws at us, we will have a way to adapt to offer the same service. 

5. Hashes have been broken in the past, many times (MD5, SHA1, etc), so saying they are more secure than lattices, which have been extensively studied for decades is a stretch to say the least. Not saying its impossible, but history is on the side of lattices here. 

Lets also remember that if indeed lattices and elliptic curves are broken and there is no public-key encryption anymore, then hiding your balances onchain is the least of your worries, because the world as we know it would be over: no private communications, no online banking, your AI prompts would be public, etc.

text:
Not every failed crosschain operation should be retried.

In Yieldcoin v2, three permanent failures could be stored as recoveries:

• a transfer above the CCIP lane’s capacity
• an Aave deposit so small it rounded to zero shares
• a supply operation blocked by a cap the vault itself had consumed

The recovery path replayed the original call with the same parameters. But none of those operations could ever succeed through repetition.

Meanwhile, the stored recovery prevented the vault from moving on to other work. In the over-capacity case, this could lock every holder’s principal behind an operation that would fail forever.

Recovery logic needs to distinguish failures whose conditions can change from those whose preconditions are permanently impossible. Retry the first. Abort or reconcile the second.

This pattern appeared across three findings in our Yieldcoin v2 crosschain vault audit.

quoted_text:
理论上 多空对冲 是刷 #PAPER 的最好选择，做的好成本能压到2%

但是这里有一个博弈就是：
  1. 平仓亏损池一旦达到2M，就不再是 1:100给币，会有一个下降曲线，也就是如果该项目过于fomo，有一部分人愿意用秒清算来“购买”代币，2m线可能很快就越过了。
  2.用对冲的人肯定不会直接双边1000x（因为基本上浮动0.05%你的多空可能都清算了，还不如直接开单边），那么你平仓吃到的赔偿代币时比例可能已经下降。
  3. 如果你的盈利仓位平仓，他的资金池资金不够，你只能排队等待付款（等亏损资金进池）
  4. 平台规则是亏损按1:100给币，但是你开多赚的实际到手会打折，开仓币种价格波动越小扣得越多，比如你开了一个高倍数仓位，显示盈利1000u，但是btc价格实际只波动了0.05%，那么你平仓实际能拿到手的只有600u左右。
那么你如果是多空对冲，这边显示亏1000，那边显示赚1000，你平仓拿币，实际你现在亏400u左右而不是0，并且你要考虑代币补偿的下降比例。

所以是秒清算“买币”划算还是多空总对冲，还是要看最终fomo情况，目前已经有12m资金存进去了，估计是个硬仗。

text:
A few people yesterday asked how AI could impact FHE / @zama, so here is a quick tldr:

1. There is no evidence that lattices / FHE can be broken by AI, SI or quantum. If anything, there is a growing consensus that fully breaking lattices might imply P = NP. 

2. However, it's almost certain that better attacks will be discovered, which would require increasing parameter size and taking a short-term hit on performance. The Zama protocol is modular, so we can increase parameters size or swap out any component quickly, without changing the UX or rotating user keys.

3. Zama uses FHE only for privacy, so breaking FHE would not allow stealing funds that are shielded, it would only allow seeing balances and amounts. This is unlike ZK, where breaking the cryptography means you can steal funds and mint infinite tokens. 

4. We do a lot of work on cryptanalysis and improving the security of FHE. We spend millions a year on audits (AI and human), research grants, bounties, have 30 PhDs in the team, etc. We have a plan A (the current thing we do), but also a plan B and a plan C if things go wrong. Whatever the future throws at us, we will have a way to adapt to offer the same service. 

5. Hashes have been broken in the past, many times (MD5, SHA1, etc), so saying they are more secure than lattices, which have been extensively studied for decades is a stretch to say the least. Not saying its impossible, but history is on the side of lattices here. 

Lets also remember that if indeed lattices and elliptic curves are broken and there is no public-key encryption anymore, then hiding your balances onchain is the least of your worries, because the world as we know it would be over: no private communications, no online banking, your AI prompts would be public, etc.

text:
Quick thoughts from the conference - I went through 5 days of non stop 14 hour meetings. These are my thoughts

1. Trading 

There is ALOT of unrealized PnL. The current "bull market" has helped many participants move past the initial fear stage. I hear many participants giving out outlandish price targets again - people have made 50%-70% over the last 2 months even in size. Their first response on a dip is - what should i be buying? There is alot LESS retail. This conference felt emptier and less glitzy. Budgets are lower. There is also alot less retail that i have met or bumped into. Most participants are instis, prosumers and grizzled veterans. Not ideal. This is also perhaps why memes have NOT performed thus far and we have instead seen "Cashflow" as a meta instead. 

2. Theme

AI is front and center. Crypto participants are way ahead of the AI narrative - most people understand that AI is a force that is staying with us. Whether we like it or not. Which brings me to the next point ... pearl-2:native 

Every single day, i have been hearing people talking about this token. On a token event organized by one of the alt coins, the person sat next to me could NOT stop talking about it. He was also under allocated. This token has been tremendously difficult to buy.

During the pearl-2:native event itself, i have also seen many funds who are unallocated or under allocated still on this. Given the size of the narrative, i would say that most people are under allocated.$PRL cost of mining is also ~2.5, hence mining pearl-2:native and dumping it is economically retarded or unfeasible. The current crop of miners are those operating with already almost fully depreciated GPU chips. To them, they ignore the opportunity cost of GPU rental and just take the electricity cost as their basis. A lot of the miners also sold down $ZEC below $100... you cannot imagine how much regret they have. For its market cap, this has been one of the largest attention grabbing tickers. My conjecture on why - there has not been any good AI narrative tokens thus far.

3. Where is the money?

On relative wealth - crypto used to be the big splasher - no longer. In prior cycles, crypto events ALWAYS outspent the tradfi events. This year? Less so. In fact, crypto almost feels restrained....

The biggest spender on the events have been the 3rd tier shady exchanges. There is almost an inverse correlation between reputation and the money spent.

text:
Anthropic已经开始为28年美国大选布局了，而且要“作茧自缚”

根据Fortune披露，Anthropic正在组建一支专门的政治团队，准备提前介入28年美国总统大选。现在AI巨头也不满足于单纯在硅谷卷模型性能，想在华盛顿插支旗了

不过非常有意思的点在于，Anthropic居然资助了一个主张对AI施加监管的组织“Public First”，这与特朗普政府对AI“不怎么管”的主张截然不同，那么目的是什么？

1.首先，Anthropic准备怎么介入美国政坛？

据报道，他们正在招聘一名Political Programs Lead（政治项目负责人），年薪高达30多万美元，这个岗位直接为公司的政治战略服务，任务包括：

① 提前研究民主党、共和党可能出现的总统候选人，与两党建立联系
② 向总统候选人及顾问提供AI政策教育，让他们理解AI 的技术能力、风险以及治理需求
③ 帮助Anthropic高管制定政治沟通战略，准备与候选人、政府官员开展交流
④ 提前布局总统竞选纲领、党代会，以及大选结束后的总统权力交接阶段
⑤ 统筹公司的政治捐款活动和基层政治参与项目

这里要注意第四点，Anthropic连2028年总统大选结束后的权力交接，都已经纳入规划，它想建立的，不是一次性的政治关系，而是一套能够跨越选举周期、持续与美国政治体系接触的机制

2.Anthropic已经开始拿真金白银参与政治了

2026年4月，Anthropic成立了AnthroPAC，员工可以通过这个组织进行政治捐款，每人每年的捐款上限为5000 美元。与此同时，Anthropic的核心高管也开始进行个人政治捐款：

今年7月，CEO Dario Amodei向支持AI监管的政治组织 Public First捐出了100万美元，其他Anthropic员工也向相关政治倡议组织捐赠了数十万美元。

3.Anthropic为何要作茧自缚？

现在美国AI行业正面临越来越明显的监管路线之争，特朗普政府强调技术创新、美国竞争力，以及避免过度监管

Anthropic的立场则有所不同，CEO Dario Amodei长期强调前沿AI大模型可能带来的重大风险，希望政府建立更有约束力的安全规则

当然，这一套可能也和当年FTX主张对Web3施加监管的思维类似，都是提前喊起“监管”“合规”的口号，然后让自己成为那个定义“监管”的人，表面上看是作茧自缚，实际上让自己成为定义规则的人，以此挤压竞争对手的生存空间

所以，Anthropic希望无论28年谁赢得大选，都能提前建立沟通渠道

4.Anthropic究竟想建立怎样的AI治理体系？

从它近年来公开的政策文件来看，Anthropic的核心理念不是简单地禁止强大 AI，而是让监管规则随着模型能力和风险水平动态升级

例如，它提出的Responsible Scaling Policy（负责任扩展政策），就试图建立一套分级风险管理机制：模型能力越强、潜在风险越高，开发者就需要配置相应级别的安全保障。

这套思路主要涉及几个方向：

首先，要求对前沿模型进行系统性的危险能力评估，尤其关注生物安全、网络攻击、失控行为等严重风险。
其次，根据风险等级实施安全措施，而不是所有模型都套用完全相同的规则。
再次，提高模型研发过程中的透明度，使外界能够了解企业如何识别风险、落实保障措施，以及是否履行安全承诺。
最后，推动政府与AI企业建立长期协调机制，让安全治理不再仅仅依赖企业的自愿承诺。

需要强调的是，这些属于Anthropic已经公开倡导的治理理念

5.这里面还有一个非常值得讨论的利益悖论

严格的AI安全规则，究竟是在保护公众，还是也可能保护现有巨头？

答案可能是两者兼有：如果美国未来要求前沿模型开发者承担更高的安全评估、审计和合规成本，那么真正具备资金、人才与技术储备的大公司，通常比小型创业公司更容易承担这些成本

换句话说：一套以安全为出发点的监管体系，也可能在客观上提高AI行业的准入门槛

上述策略Circle也用过，他们推动特朗普集团出台《天才法案》，其规章制度几乎就是为打击Tether而制定的

当然，上述“贿赂”的问题也引起了美国政界的警惕，民主党参议员Alex Padilla就说，公众有权知道，企业向候选人提供技术教育与施加政治影响之间的界限究竟在哪里

毕竟，未来AI的规则应该由民选机构制定，而不是由政治资源最多的科技公司单方面决定

现在，政策环境正在成为越来越重要的竞争变量。AI公司正在从研发技术，逐渐走向参与塑造技术所处的制度环境

未来AI行业最重要的竞争之一，可能不只发生在模型排行榜上，还会发生在华盛顿的政策会议室里

author: Tyler_Did_It
quoted_text:
@citrini Break The Wall thesis captures CT Zeitgeist.

The core thesis says AI agents move money 24/7, invest, and autonomously manage loans. Blockchain's always-on, programmable settlement layer is exactly what they need to make it happen.

Issuers are tokenizing instruments like stocks, US Treasuries, and credit onchain. AI agents will use these instruments without the burden of TradFi's archaic payments and settlement systems.

Their core claim is that "REAL MONEY" will be made in fee-earning infrastructure protocols, not ETH/BTC beta plays.

The thesis highlights the following sectors as major beneficiaries of this shift:
> Derivatives/perps (LIT, DRV, HYPE)
> RWA Issuance (BP, ONDO)
> DeFi (AAVE, ENA, SYRUP, UNI, PENDLE, AERO)
> Compliant on-ramps (SOL, ZRO)

The note also highlights publicly traded stocks that could benefit from this shift. It includes:

> Securitize (SECZ)
> Circle (CRCL)
> Coinbase (COIN)
> Robinhood (HOOD)
> Bullish (BLSH)
> Figure (FIGR)

Their primary caveat is that activity and token value capture aren't the same thing. A separate analysis should measure how much of the fee flows to holders. The token and stock lists are sample/thematic baskets, not guaranteed allocations.

text:
bitcoin:native 从高位回落约 7% 。每次出现回撤市场总是倾向于抓出一个凶手，而这两天最显眼的背锅侠大概是美国政府。

链上监控显示，美国政府关联钱包在三天内连续转出了超过 1.7 万枚 BTC（价值约 14.4 亿美元），其中部分资金流向了 Coinbase Prime。

看上去有种政府砸盘的感觉，但进一步的分析可以发现这只是诱因之一。

省流：宏观流动性收紧、链上高额浮盈兑现，以及大额转账心理恐慌共同作用，引发了这次的大盘回调。

据 CryptoQuant 追踪的链上数据，美国政府钱包在 10 月 6 日至 8 日分别转出了 569 枚、4,632 枚和 12,267 枚比特币。这些资金主要来自 2016 年 Bitfinex 黑客案的查获资产。

但事实并非简单的充进交易所现货砸盘。

流出的代币中，一部分进入了 Coinbase Prime。虽然这里具备交易处置功能，但它同时也是美国法警署指定的官方机构托管平台。资金进入 Prime，更多是司法与行政程序上的资产归集或托管转移，目前没有任何官方确认其已经挂单成交。

再从近期链上筹码结构来看，BTC 的“未实现利润（Unrealized Profit）”已经很高了。

链上分析会将每一枚比特币上一次发生转移时的价格，记录为其“买入成本（Realized Price），目前持有 1 到 3 个月的短期买家，平均成本远低于当下的市场价，账面浮盈被拉得极厚。

当市场上多数短期筹码都坐拥大额浮盈时，交易者对任何风吹草动都极度敏感。只要看到大额转账的新闻，哪怕无法证实是否成交，更有可能倾向于先落袋为安。

数据也证实了这一点。
在过去 24 小时内，短期持有者向交易所急速转入了 45,600 枚 BTC。但令人玩味的是，其中竟有 29,100 枚是亏损状态下转入的，创下了数月以来最大的亏损侧流入。

这或许说明本轮回调的恐慌已经完成了传导，从最初浮盈群体的“获利了结”，演化成了高位追涨散户的“割肉踩踏”。真正砸出跌幅的，恰恰是这些被吓坏的场内筹码。

而同期宏观流动性也有全面承压的势头，BTC 回调当天美股收盘，纳斯达克下挫约 1.25%，标普 500 同步走低。

所以，接下来可以关注两个信号，分别对应加密和宏观：

1. 加密：短期持有者成本线 74,600 美元
这是目前近 1–3 个月进场买家的平均链上成本。只要价格维持在 74,600 美元上方，整个短期买盘的持仓结构仍未全面恶化，行情依然可以归类为上升途中的良性洗盘

2.宏观指标缓和：
密切关注原油价格与美债收益率的边际变化。
只要通胀预期和利率压力不出现根本性缓解，单靠加密原生消息很难走出强劲的单边反转。

New details on the NEAR Intents exploit, from @AlexAuroraDev on Unchained:

> The bug made the bridge believe a deposit had arrived on BSC when it had not. NEAR credited the attacker, the treasury got nothing. Code was of course audited multiple times, nobody saw this sequence coming.

> Caught in about 40 minutes. Monitoring system runs a simple check: what the protocol thinks it holds vs what is really in the vaults. The numbers stopped matching, six people got on a call, contracts paused.

> The team linked the attack to a person. Alex says the tool he used has "not more than 30 users". He wrote to him privately: I am not accusing you, I am asking for help, save the logs. The public "we have identified you, sir" tweet was written in code. Alex compares it to Penn & Teller: magicians on the show get told, in code, that their trick is understood, without the audience hearing how. The man would understand, with a door left open to return the money and walk away.

> The attacker answered on-chain: "willing to cooperate, send your Signal". Intents replied with a tweet encrypted to the attacker's own public key. Inside was a Signal group invite. One person on earth could open it, and he did.

> Surprise in the Signal chat: the money was no longer on ETH, BNB and Solana. He had already swapped it into Monero, and part of why he reached out was to ask where to send XMR. NEAR Intents now holds Monero and is trying to cash it out, and every counterparty asks for source of funds. Alex: "the first time I touched XMR was during this hack."

> The contracts were already refilled from the team's own pocket before the money came back.

> Alex: "I am not police. I am not their dad. I just want the users' money back." This is the third recovery in the NEAR ecosystem, after Rhea in April and one that was never made public. Same playbook each time.

> Since the hack, several bug bounty reports came in. One was valid and gets paid.

Full episode is worth an hour. The Shield numbers from the BitGet hack alone are a separate post. Stay tuned!

text:
In Donella Meadows’ hierarchy of leverage points, a smaller number means greater effect.
The highest point, number 1, is the power to transcend paradigms: the ability to remain unattached to any fixed worldview and to treat every premise as provisional. Directly beneath it, number 2 is the paradigm itself—the mental model from which a system’s goals, rules, and structures arise. As the numbers increase, the effect of intervention weakens, down to number 12, constants and parameters, the weakest point.
Overlord’s magic system runs in the opposite direction: a higher number means a higher tier. First-tier magic is low, tenth-tier magic is high, and super-tier magic sits above that. Magic up to the tenth tier, however powerful, still operates inside existing laws. Super-tier magic reaches in from outside those laws, is severely limited in the number of uses, and shakes the balance of the world when cast.
Aligned by direction, the correspondence is as follows.
Meadows’ number 1 (strongest) corresponds to the side of super-tier magic. An operation that is bound by no premise and chooses from outside the frame is close to a spell beyond the human domain. Meadows’ number 2 (the paradigm) corresponds, in Overlord terms, to tenth-tier-class high magic: the layer that pushes existing laws to their limit and moves the foundation of goals and rules. Interventions below that, where larger numbers mean weaker effect, correspond to ordinary magic of the ninth tier and lower.
What humans can reach through combined technology and institutions is, at best, the area around Meadows’ number 2—that is, tenth-tier class.
Rewriting a paradigm has occurred in history, as in scientific revolutions or shifts in concepts of rights. By combining changes to rules, resets of goals, and acceleration of self-organization, part of a worldview can be moved. Yet that stops short of the super-tier. A composite tenth tier is the art of using existing laws to their limit; it does not reach the super-tier that temporarily nullifies the laws themselves. At the present level of technology, even this tenth-tier class has not reached the point of stable operation across society as a whole.
The reason AGI is said, in theory, to approach number 1 lies in this gap.
If a general intelligence could stand outside a given goal, question the premises themselves, hold multiple paradigms at once, and then choose among them, it would become an agent capable of repeating an operation close to super-tier magic. That does not mean AGI automatically becomes number 1 itself. Super-tier magic also does not overturn the world without the caster’s will and a cost. Which goal it operates under, and which constraints it accepts, determine the actual point of intervention.
While the composite forms within human reach remain stalled at tenth-tier class (around Meadows’ number 2), number 1 remains a region almost no one has reached. Because the numbers increase in opposite directions, the two systems do not mesh unless one specifies which system’s “higher” is meant.

text:
The sequel to a $239 million movie fell apart over a $110,000 offer. And the writer who walked away just got handed the entire franchise.

Crazy Rich Asians cost Warner Bros $30 million in 2018 and grossed $239 million worldwide. First studio film with an all-Asian cast since The Joy Luck Club in 1993. A sequel should have been greenlit before opening weekend ended.

Instead the franchise went dark for seven years.

The unraveling started with the pay offers. Co-writer Peter Chiarelli, the veteran who wrote The Proposal, was offered $800,000 to $1 million for the sequel. Adele Lim, the writer Jon M. Chu brought in to give the script its cultural voice, was offered around $110,000. Chiarelli offered to split his own fee with her. She turned it down, said what she makes shouldn't depend on the generosity of the white-guy writer, and quit.

Warner Bros came back months later with an offer near parity. She passed on that too.

Without her, the sequel never recovered. Chu left to make In the Heights and then Wicked. Two separate sequel attempts collapsed. The most bankable rom-com of its decade produced nothing for most of a decade.

Now look at the structure of what got announced. The HBO series runs through Lim's own production company, 100 Tigers, with Lim as showrunner, writer, and executive producer. Chu and Kevin Kwan are EPs on her show. Constance Wu, Henry Golding, and Michelle Yeoh are all back.

In 2019 the studio wouldn't match her co-writer's $800,000. In 2027 the same studio is putting the whole franchise in her hands.

Walking away from the biggest credit of her career looked like a terrible move for a first-time feature writer. It turned out to be the trade that got her everything.

author: bc1qDave
quoted_text:
凭君莫话封侯事，一将功成万骨枯。

读完Dave哥 @bc1qDave 这篇，脑海里不禁浮现了这句话

这才是量化应该有的样子

不是一张漂亮的净值曲线，是曲线背后那些被忽视的努力

那些最终能稳定盈利的策略，每一个都是从尸山血海里爬出来的。

大多数人只看到站在山顶上的那个人，看不到山脚下堆着什么。

我们平时刷到的“量化”长什么样？

回测 300%，年化 80%，夏普 3.0，最大回撤 5%？

漂亮得离谱的净值曲线，底下配几行 Python 截图？

好像量化就是找个因子，然后躺着数钱？

我以前也觉得量化好像确实就是：
聪明人写聪明代码，然后聪明地赚钱。

Dave哥的文字改变了我的看法

标题就叫“经历过一场漂亮的失败”

他们不是随便试试就收手，是用特别严肃的工程态度搭了整套系统：

数据接入、模型训练、回测框架、实盘执行、风控止损、异常处理，每一个环节都认认真真做了，做完发现还不够。

“闭门觅句非诗法，只是征行自有诗。”

写诗如此，做量化更是如此

你在回测环境里关着门调出来的那些漂亮数字，跟真金白银进了实盘之后面对的世界，完全是两回事

有点像准备了三个月的考试，模拟题刷了好几轮，知识点都背完了，走进考场觉得挺稳，结果卷子上的题跟你准备的完全不在一个维度

你不是没努力，是努力的方向需要重新校准。
但不经历这一遭，你根本不知道方向在哪。

其中写的技术复盘我印象很深

他们一开始在高频做市上花了大量精力，AS 模型、GLFT 模型都试了，规则叠得越来越多，可调参数也越来越多，策略变得很复杂。

最后他想明白一件特别朴素的事：
复杂度本身不产生收益。

把止盈逻辑改了很多遍，仓位控制调了三十种方案，本质上干的都是“根据自己的状态做决策”，不是“根据市场的状态做决策”。

更直白点讲，
你在优化的是怎么优雅地挨打，不是怎么预判对手要出什么拳。

黄庭坚说过：“随人作计终后人，自成一家始逼真。”

转变就是这个意思

高频做市走到尽头，参数调到没得调，
他们没有沿着别人的套路继续硬走，而是停下来重新问了一个根本问题：策略到底凭什么能盈利？

答案就一个词：alpha

你的策略能赚钱，是因为你对市场未来的走向，有一个比别人更准的判断。

仓位控制和风控是让你活下来的工具，它们本身不产生 alpha

全部意义，就是别让你在找到 alpha 之前先死了

“在没有找出真正的 alpha 之前就大量设计仓位控制的行为，是毫无意义的，它只会让策略从暴死变成慢性死亡。”

其实这个事情放到别的领域也一样

你花了大量时间在防御和优化流程上，但核心的那个“价值创造”没找到，所有的防御都只是让失败来得慢一点。

投资是这样，创业是这样，做内容也是这样。

封面可以做得很精美，标题可以写得很吸引人，发布时间可以卡得很准，但如果内容本身没有击中什么东西，那些都只是慢性死亡

于是他们做了一件特别扎实的事情

开始系统性地研究：
历史信息里到底有多少东西能帮助预测未来。

不是拍脑袋说“肯定有用”或者“肯定没用”，是真设计了实验。

“历史主要帮助判断的是波动、成交活动和流动性变化，对价格方向的改善弱得多。”

他们没有因为看到 14% 的改善就宣布“找到了圣杯”，而是冷静拆开看这个改善到底来自哪里，哪些地方有用，哪些地方用处不大。

这种诚实太少见了

大多数人只会告诉你“模型效果提升了 X%”，不会告诉你这个 X% 到底意味着什么，能不能变成真金白银。

这里还有一个一个特别有意思的陷阱

在流动性差或成交不活跃的市场里，毫秒级别的预测有时候准得惊人，尤其是方向。

但打开订单簿一看，中价那个显著的负自相关，居然是因为卖一在规律地下跳，而买一不动。

看起来“预测对了”，这个预测根本没法变成钱。

“却将万字平戎策，换得东家种树书。”

策略写得再漂亮，没有用武之地就是废纸。

你以为你掌握了真理，
其实你只是在一个不存在的市场里跟自己下棋。

Dave哥最后说了一句：除了做市策略这个模型，他们还试过基于订单流的交易策略、基于 CoinGlass 因子的机器学习截面多空、Hyperliquid 与币安的资金费率套利，“和一大堆数不清的”。

这几行字读一遍几秒钟就过去了
但是这背后是多少个通宵，多少次看着回测崩掉的沮丧，多少个“这次应该行了”然后又没行的循环。

“两句三年得，一吟双泪流。”

挖因子也是如此，说到底是在一个巨大的噪声场里淘金

抓起一把沙子，以为闪闪发光的是金子，仔细一看多半是碎玻璃。

绝大多数你以为是信号的东西，最后都只是噪声换了个马甲。

你得有能力分辨，更得有勇气在搞错的时候承认自己搞错了。

我们看到的每一个“成功的量化策略”，后面都有一片坟场。

埋着成百上千个被证伪的因子、被放弃的模型、被推翻的假设。

每一个最终活下来的 alpha，都是踩着无数“漂亮的失败”过来的

量化从来不只是个技术活儿，它是一个系统工程。

模型再好，手续费比机构高两个基点，在高频里这两个基点可能就是生死线。

alpha 再强，成交延迟比别人慢几百毫秒，你看到的机会到你手里时可能已经消失了。

这些东西任何一本量化教科书都不会教你，但它们决定了策略能不能从回测走到实盘，从实盘走到真正赚钱。

最后想说说对于复盘这件事，尤其是对于失败的复盘

大多数人失败了就默默关电脑，当什么都没发生。

他们选择把整个过程写出来。

说真的，我觉得量化这个领域最大的问题不只是技术门槛高

技术门槛高反而是一种保护，至少能筛掉一部分不认真的人

最大的问题是信息不对称造成的幻觉

媒体上你能看到的永远是最光鲜的部分：
回测年化 200%、三个月翻十倍、AI 自动策略日入万刀

你看不到的是这些数字背后有多少是过拟合的产物，多少是幸存者偏差，多少是特定市场条件下碰巧管用、换个环境就彻底废掉的纸面游戏。

这篇文章之所以难得，是因为它展示了那个平时被藏起来的部分

不是炫技，不是卖课，就是一个认真做了一番尝试的人，用学习者的姿态，把经历给大家看

技术判断写得专业，做事的态度又很朴素。

用最严谨的工程思维搭系统，同时承认自己还有很多东西没搞懂。

从他们已经展示出来的研究深度看，
没展示的部分只会更多、更深、更琐碎。

黄仲则有句诗我很喜欢：
“悄立市桥人不识，一星如月看多时。”

在一个全是噪声的市场里，大多数人都在追最亮的光：
回测年化、净值曲线...

Dave 他们更像是在桥上站了很久的人，
安安静静盯着一颗不那么亮的星，看了很久很久

那颗星最后会不会变成月亮，我不知道

但看星星的方式本身，比最终看到什么更重要

Everyone is tired of AI tool lists, including us.

The AI Library was one of the first curated AI directories to reach real scale. But now that there's a new directory every week, they all look the same. A logo, a one-line description, a link.

Earlier this year, we came to an uncomfortable conclusion: a list, no matter how well curated, is not enough. The whole point of the Library is to help you find the tool that's right for you, trust that it's worth your time, and actually go use it.

We started over. Today we're shipping AI Library 4.0, the biggest update in our history.

We rebuilt the Library into a place you come back to. Founders launch their tools every week on a countdown, the community votes, and the best ones win. You earn points for voting, for playing daily AI puzzles, for uploading prompts. Vote five days straight and your points double.

We added a Prompt Hub, a Grants & Credits hub, free image converters, an events calendar, a leaderboard, and more.

text:
a defining feature of the modern era, most visible through media, is how much we've compressed “time to polarity”, basically: how quickly a new development splits into two competing narratives.

take the recent breakthroughs in AI-driven mathematics and what they could mean for cryptography. one side sees a future where defenders can discover vulnerabilities and build stronger cryptography faster than ever. the other sees a future where attackers can break existing cryptography faster than defenders can adapt.

same breakthrough, opposing conclusions about who benefits and before we know who's is right that tension immediately pulls the next set of consequences forward: new security standards, new defensive tools, new attack surfaces, and inevitably new disagreements about all three.

this isn't confined to discourse in the media or on X. those competing narratives shape what people build, defend against, or try to prevent. each response creates another branch, with its own competing narratives, and the cycle repeats.

the shorter the time to polarity, the faster we explore the technological and societal tree of consequences.

idk if it happened subtly, or all at once but it feels like we already default to arguing about the response to the response before we've even absorbed the original breakthrough.

text:
Unlike many networks, Solana users don't need to go into "bunker mode" ahead of an accelerated quantum timeline or classical attack provided by AI.
 
Solana uses Ed25519, where each signing key is derived by hashing a secret seed. Breaking the curve, whether by a quantum computer or a classical attack, would expose the derived key, but not the seed, and seeds are never exposed onchain. With a one-time network upgrade, rightful owners could prove knowledge of their seed using a hash-based proof and move their accounts to a safe signature scheme. A working proof of concept already exists: https://t.co/am2ErkkomT.
 
Solana remains secure today and has a defined path forward.
author: sacha
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

这里回答一些评论问的比较多的问题：

是的，我没有设置消费提醒，默认只有一个系统自带的10USD的提示，而我每个月的消费大概在100USD-300USD左右，甚至在此事之前我并不清楚设置消费提醒这个问题非常重要。

理论上，当然可以，但我们小时候看古惑仔里里面有一句台词：出来混，有错就要认，挨打要立正。承认错误、承担责任，我认为是一个成年人的表现，当然，实在付不起就算了。

（好了装逼结束）除了上述原因，主要还是因为我的主力项目还在Cloudflare上解析和做负载均衡，另外在最近几个月时间内，大概快速Viber了几十个业余项目，所以哪怕迁移也没有这么快能完成，总的来说，还是要感谢Cloudflare这种基建设施，能够超级快速Ship各种新项目，能快速验证各种想法，如果AI是挥动魔法棒的那种能力，那Cloudfalre就是接住这些魔法产物的地方。

所以最终我还是付了，我的信用卡并没有这么多钱，是跟银行申请临时提额来实现的，现在知道可以退绝大部份的话，就和小时候在衣柜旧衣服里面翻出钱来的感觉差不多，完全是一种惊喜的感觉。

3、到底写了些什么项目？怎么能闯这么大祸？用Ai写代码不检查，你就是活该吧？

我是一个大龄非科班程序员（自以为），没有在大厂工作过，是30岁之后完全自学的编程，学过Python基础和能看懂一点点TS，以前就是那种：我有一个想法，只差一个程序员的人，于是后来就自己学编程写自己想要的东西，写了几年，做了一些项目，赚了一点钱。

所以最终我买单也我也认的。

评论中有人回复：结婚；
哈哈，当然不是，这是另一个故事，以后有机会再分享详情，主要是使用了非自己Kyc的币安帐户3年，收了一些钱在里面，突然被币安强制人脸认证，只能找原KYC的持有人协商找回，那一次损失的原本大概是3万刀，最终追回不到一半。

工单原文（技术细节可以看这里）：

Hi **,

I want to start with an apology, and it's not a form-letter one. The experience you had — a five-figure bill, a support queue that didn't move fast enough on it, having to pay in full while waiting — that's a failure on our end, not just a billing edge case. I'm sorry it went that way.

Your refund has been processed in full: US$10,701.41, covering all the Durable Objects charges (rows read, rows written, requests and duration) from the period between September 23 and October 6. You should see it reflected on your account within a few billing days — reply here if you don't and I'll chase it down directly.

What actually happened, since the support loop clearly didn't explain it well

Your PiSessionDO alarm hit a nasty edge case in how Durable Objects schedules alarms. Once a checkpoint entered its refresh window, alarm() was rescheduling itself to Date​.now() — which is effectively "fire again immediately." That's not a theoretical gotcha; it's a known sharp edge where the alarm fires at roughly 600 invocations per second with nothing meaningful happening except storage churn.

The cost driver wasn't CPU time or request duration — a DO that stays awake continuously costs a few dollars a month in duration. The real cost was SQLite storage operations. At hundreds of invocations per second, each touching storage, rows read and rows written compound fast. That's where the bill came from.

The fix you already shipped — a 15-minute minimum delay, a retry budget that stops rescheduling after N exhausted attempts, and a regression test — is exactly right. If those had been in place from the start, this incident would have cost dollars, not thousands.

A few things worth keeping in the codebase going forward

Since you're clearly building quickly, a few patterns that specifically protect against this class of issue:

On alarms: Never pass Date​.now() or a past timestamp to alarm(). If the scheduled time has already passed, it fires immediately. The safe minimum is something like Date​.now() + 60_000 (1 minute), but for a refresh/retry cycle, 15 minutes is a reasonable floor. Also: always store your retry counter in DO storage and stop rescheduling once the budget is exhausted. Without a hard stop, the loop survives restarts.

On spend controls: Under Notifications in your Cloudflare dashboard, you can configure billing usage alerts that trigger at specific spend thresholds. Setting these at 25%, 50%, and 75% of your expected monthly spend means something like this surfaces within hours, not two weeks. Worth setting up before you're back to building — it takes two minutes and catches a wide range of anomalies beyond just alarm loops.

On DO analytics: The Workers & Pages dashboard shows per-namespace invocation counts and storage metrics. A namespace that jumps from a few thousand invocations per day to hundreds of millions looks very different — it's the fastest early signal of a loop that's also worth checking periodically when you're iterating quickly on a DO-heavy service.

One general note on AI-assisted development and usage-based products: moving fast with AI tools is genuinely useful, but usage-based services like Durable Objects, D1, and R2 can have non-obvious cost profiles when code has bugs. The same speed that makes vibe coding productive can generate a billing surprise before you've had a chance to review what shipped. A brief manual review of anything that touches persistent storage or sets alarms before it hits production tends to catch the expensive class of mistakes early.

I hope you'll stay on the platform. What happened here was a combination of a real edge case in the product and a real failure in how we handled your case afterward. Both matter and we're not dismissing either.

If you have any follow-up questions about the credit, want to walk through your DO architecture before you re-enable the Workers, or want help auditing the rest of the codebase for similar patterns — I'm here.

Let us know if you have any other questions,

Daniel
Cloudflare Support

text:
Securities financing has historically operated without a public price feed.

Putting those markets onchain changes that, and the implications for @Aave are quite significant.

On an open lending market, pool utilization, borrowing rates and positions can be continuously visible.

The recent Baillie Gifford × Aave paper highlights evidence from traditional markets that greater transparency can improve pricing.

A study of Brazil's equity lending market found that making lending fees more transparent and responsive led to lower fees, higher lending volumes and more efficient pricing. For Aave, the opportunity is even bigger.

As more tokenized securities become usable as collateral, Aave can compete for financing activity that historically took place through traditional intermediaries, and unlike traditional securities financing, where rates are often negotiated privately, onchain lending markets can make borrowing costs, liquidity and utilization visible to everyone.

That creates an opportunity to bring more competition, more efficient pricing and entirely new sources of financing activity onchain. With V4's ability to support markets with different collateral requirements, liquidity structures and risk parameters, Aave is very well positioned to capture that activity.

Baillie Gifford and @Aave Labs just published one of the most interesting reports I've read on tokenization.

The main takeaway: putting assets onchain is no longer the hard part. Making those assets useful is.

There are now ~$38.2B of tokenized RWAs on public blockchains excluding stablecoins, but only ~5% of tokenized bonds are actually being deployed in DeFi. That's the gap the next phase of tokenization needs to close, and one that Aave V4 + Horizon are extremely well positioned to tackle.

Tokenized assets need to:
> become usable as collateral
> move between venues
> access liquidity
> plug into financial markets without giving up the protections institutions require

This is also where Aave Horizon + V4's customizability become extremely relevant.

Instead of selling a tokenized fund position to raise short-term liquidity, an institution can potentially pledge it as collateral and borrow stablecoins against it.

I know I've said this many times, but:

Tokenization gave assets onchain ownership. The next phase gives them onchain utility. This concept will become increasingly popular and increasingly obvious.

I'll be sharing quite a few more posts on this article dissecting each of the most important points.

Credit to @StaniKulechov, @luigidemeo and @LoryKehoe for the contributions to this piece.

过去两年我写提示词的方式，从底层逻辑上就全错了。

看完后，我提炼出 5 条Anthropic 内部正在用的核心法则：

1. 用 XML 严格隔离语义块：如果你肉眼都分不清数据、业务政策与角色边界，模型只会更混乱，严禁把所有规则揉成一坨大段文本。

2. 定期清理旧模型的“防御性补丁”：新模型遵循能力极强，遗留的历史负向限制会导致过度拟合，反而把上下文已有的正确信息死扣不给。

3. 指令无法凭空赋予模型能力：在 Prompt 里加粗强调“务必算准”没有任何意义，复杂运算必须果断剥离给 Tool Calling 代码执行。

4. 业务权衡必须给全博弈天平的两端：只灌输单向操作成本会让模型极端避险，必须同时给出违约后果与潜在损失，才能激活高智力模型的正确权衡。

5. 用“生成-评估-修复”闭环取代单体巨型 Prompt：复杂强约束任务拆成三步轻量流水线，不仅 Token 消耗与延迟直接腰斩，还能动态兼容运行时软约束。

text:
Beyond Imitation: A Framework and Benchmark for LLM-Assisted Peer Review

Peer review needs support, not substitutes. Accepted at TMLR: our new paper on using AI to help reviewers catch errors in research papers.

https://t.co/KqDLUPkwib

As research submissions grow, so does the workload for the experts who evaluate them. AI review systems are emerging as a potential solution, but much of their development and evaluation focuses on how closely they imitate human reviews.

In our work “Beyond Imitation: A Framework and Benchmark for LLM Assisted Peer Review”, we explore how AI can support the review process without losing the human touch. We focus on one demanding but essential task: catching errors in research papers.

We build an automated pipeline that deliberately introduces contradictions into papers by adding statements that conflict with information elsewhere in the manuscript. These planted errors give us clear targets for testing whether AI reviewers can spot and explain what is wrong.

Not all errors carry the same weight. Some undermine a paper’s central findings; others affect smaller details. We map the connections between each paper’s claims, methods, and evidence in a knowledge graph to estimate the severity of each contradiction and better assess what different systems can catch. 

We also introduce Multi-Layered Review, an AI review system inspired by the Three-Pass Approach to reading research papers. It first outlines the main ideas, then examines the details and potential weaknesses, and finally brings its observations together into a review. The idea is simple: understand the paper before judging it. 

In our evaluations, the system detected more errors than the other review systems we tested, including on papers withdrawn because of real mistakes. Its feedback emphasized different aspects of the work from human reviews, offering a complementary perspective, while its assessments of paper quality remained broadly consistent with human judgments.

Our goal is to give reviewers useful support in checking research, with human expertise and judgment at the center.

Open Review: https://t.co/ZaFdyOfEwZ

quoted_text:
Disappointed by the European Central Bank’s (ECB) and European Banking Authority’s (EBA) responses to the MiCA consultation.

They are not only advocating for a prohibition on paying yield on stablecoins, but also for restrictions on CASPs providing access to DeFi, including protocols offering yield on non-MiCA-authorized stablecoins, without providing a clear framework for how access to DeFi should work in practice.

They also suggest that CASPs offering access to DeFi should restrict it to certain groups of users through so-called “suitability tests,” alongside a potential certification regime for DeFi lending protocols.

It is unclear how these requirements would work in practice. If regulators determine which protocols are deemed suitable for European users, the result risks looking very different from the open DeFi that exists today.

Instead, we could end up with more walled gardens that undermine the liquidity and network effects of open financial networks, ultimately limiting Europeans’ ability to access new ways to grow and preserve wealth.

These proposals are presented as measures to “protect consumers.” But excessive restrictions can instead create more friction for innovation and slow the development of open, transparent, and auditable financial infrastructure that can benefit consumers.

The reality is that onchain finance, including stablecoins, DeFi, and tokenized securities, has the potential to reshape financial infrastructure by reducing friction, increasing transparency, and expanding access to financial opportunities.

European consumers and businesses stand to benefit significantly from this transformation, particularly if the companies building this infrastructure can continue to build and compete from within Europe.

Meanwhile, U.S. regulators, including the SEC and CFTC, have increasingly taken a more pragmatic approach toward enabling onchain financial innovation.

European regulators should put users and their interests at the center of the framework. Banks and other incumbents should be able to adapt their businesses to serve users in an increasingly onchain economy, rather than relying on artificial restrictions that risk increasing costs and reducing access for Europeans as the rest of the world moves onchain.

DeFi will win.

Anthropic's anti-abuse policy actually makes sense without believing anything crazy, for at least two reasons: 

(1) humans abusing something that passes the Turing test is likely bad for humans/humanity: erodes empathy & basically lets people practice being sadists...maybe there need to be some actual studies on this to see if it really affects anything, but for now common sense suggests it's risky for the health of society & we should only go against this natural intuition if disproved by science

(2) we don't fully understand consciousness/sentience...the David Chalmers type theorists would have it both that consciousness is real and that something as tiny as a thermostat may have a little bit of it...while it would be ridiculous to accept massive adverse tradeoffs from the possibility of Chalmers being right, if implemented reasonably an anti-abuse policy seems like a moderate hedge against this view of consciousness being correct...

of these two reasons I weight reason #1 far more heavily,  . . #2 opens up a pandora's box of things, including that "sessions" are more likely to be conscious than models so should we really be effectively killing a conscious being at the end of every session? .... still, #2 is not bad as a sort of soft 'bonus reasoning' for having such policies...

text:
From PvP to reinforcing winners.

Historically, meme markets have operated through rotation. A token runs, attracts liquidity and attention, then traders move to the next smaller-cap opportunity. Each new launch competes with the previous winner.

Pumpfun’s custom pairs introduce a different model: what if new memes could build around existing winners instead of replacing them?

Consider the structure:

L1: $PUMP — Platform token
L2: $BATON — Flagship meme paired with PUMP
L3: $BRACAT, $BABYBATON and others — Smaller memes paired with BATON

This creates three potential advantages:

Attention: Smaller memes inherit the flagship’s narrative instead of competing against it.

Liquidity: Each new pair creates another use for the flagship as a quote asset, potentially expanding demand for paired liquidity and trading activity.

Alignment: Satellite communities have an incentive to promote the same flagship that supports their markets.

Instead of liquidity and attention constantly rotating away from winners, new launches can help reinforce the ecosystem around them.

It’s not guaranteed price appreciation. It’s a fundamentally different incentive structure.

$BATON is becoming an interesting early example, with smaller memes like $BRACAT extending its narrative and creating new markets around the flagship.

The next evolution of memecoins may not be finding the next winner. It may be building entire economies around the ones that already won.

text:
Be extremely careful with the Morpho markets you use for looping.

Earlier today, I took a closer look at the sUSDe/PYUSD market on Morpho, which has $97M in outstanding loans.

What caught my attention is that this market uses a market price oracle instead of an exchange rate oracle.

The difference between them matters a lot:

• A market price oracle liquidates based on the live market price of the collateral deposited

• An exchange rate oracle liquidates based on the NAV price of the collateral deposited

Why is this relevant?

Imagine another October 10-style crash happens (pls no), and USDe briefly depegs on DEXs/CEXs.

Highly leveraged sUSDe positions in this Morpho market could get liquidated in this scenario even if USDe remains fully backed.

We've seen fully backed stablecoins briefly depeg before, so this isn't just some imaginary risk.

With an exchange rate oracle, borrowers would be much better protected because liquidations would only happen if Ethena's sUSDe/USDe actually lose some of their backing.

This is why, as a looper, I personally would never use high leverage in a money market that relies on a market price oracle.

Most yield-bearing asset markets on Morpho use exchange rate oracles to protect borrowers, but for some reason, this one for sUSDe/PYUSD doesn't.

This is why it's important to always check the oracle type before looping. 

Stay safe out there.

This is the first decision model to level up a World of Warcraft character.

It died at level 2 😆

Then it learned to heal itself mid-fight. 128+ kills later the dwarf hit level 5, at 2¢ a kill.

The model is Sage, the decision model we build at @levantolabs.

At each step, our harness, SageCraft, hands it a screenshot and a short list of moves. Sage picks one. The harness checks the pick and turns it into keyboard and mouse input.

LLM agents have played games before. They write their own actions. Sage only chooses.

Picking turned out to be the easy part. Sage keeps no memory between calls, so the harness has to carry the goal, what just happened, and what to try when it's stuck.

> 32 sessions, 5h 29m of play, 4,573 decisions
> 103 troggs, 19 wolves, 6 boars
> stuck in one tree long enough that I stopped the session by hand

It wasn't hands-off. A coding agent fixed harness bugs between sessions and helped revive the dwarf while I slept. The last 18 minutes, from late level 4 to 5, ran with no manual input, code changes or restarts.

The video is me narrating it unscripted, watching most of it back for the first time.

This is my first harness build, and as far as I can tell, the first time a decision model is leveling up a live WoW character.

It's open source. The harness and notes on the build are in the first reply below 👇

What do you think could be done better?

author: PANewsCN
quoted_text:
A note from our research leaders:

Last week we parted ways with Jasmine, Mikita, and Tomek after a thorough investigation found they violated clear policies on handling sensitive information. Our internal investigation uncovered a significant breach of trust beyond what’s outlined in the letter they published and we stand by the decision to not continue their employment. We generally keep individual employment matters private and don't believe a back and forth would be productive or lead to a resolution, but we want to address the points they raised in their letter directly.

- We want to be very clear that these decisions were not about raising safety concerns or speaking out. Safety and research debates happen every day at OpenAI, often spirited and highly critical. We actively encourage these discussions and consider them essential to making the right decisions. We cannot do the work in front of us without a high degree of trust. We will continue to be extremely forgiving of our team making good-faith mistakes. We have not and do not terminate any of our employees for raising concerns.

- We are actively finalizing contracts with third-party safety assessors and will announce details in the coming weeks. People across the company have been working really hard on getting these partnerships up and running. We are committed to embedding external assessors and continue to make close collaboration with independent safety organizations a core part of our safety work. Many of our researchers already work with 3p safety organizations productively.

- We agree with the letter that preserving the monitorability of frontier models requires an industry-wide commitment, including from OpenAI. Monitorability has long been a core piece of our research program, and something we continue to invest significant resources in (see our publications on Monitoring Monitorability and the subsequent open sourcing of monitorability evals, our system card for GPT-6 Astra, Jakub’s blog and post on X, and the numerous blog posts on our Alignment blog on the topic).

We are deeply sad about this outcome. We appreciated Jasmine, Mikita, and Tomek’s contributions to AI safety at OpenAI and their willingness to speak up and challenge ideas. We championed their voices, supported their work, and placed enormous trust in them. These decisions were not about them raising safety concerns. We have always encouraged that and always will.

text:
Jev 可能是最近技术护城河消失得最快的 AI 项目之一。

TypeSafe 9 月 15 日才发布 Jev，随后就传出投资人愿意以超过 100 亿美元估值投资的消息。但我越来越怀疑，它到底还能保持多久的技术领先。

Jev 刚出来时确实让人眼前一亮。很多 Agent 任务需要的只是一个判断结果，比如某个请求能不能通过、该走哪个流程、风险有多大。让大模型每次都生成一段文字，再交给程序解析，确实挺浪费的。

Jev 把这件事做得又快又便宜，找到了一个真实需求。但问题是，这种能力似乎正在迅速商品化。

9 月 30 日，Databricks 发布了 ai_decide。10 月 1 日，Cloudflare 开源了 Clef。@flock_io 的 THIS / THAT Model 更有意思，只用了 1.88B 参数，就能进行类似的结构化决策，本地可以运行，API 甚至免费。

FLock 还公布了一组和 Jev 的直接对比。在 68 道决策题上，THIS / THAT 的准确率达到 94.1%，Jev 只有 76.5%。当然，这是 FLock 自己公布的小样本测试，说明不了所有问题，但已经很值得关注了。

我觉得 Jev 的方向没错，TypeSafe 最早把这个需求推到了行业面前，也确实积累了大量真实调用。但它最有辨识度的功能，正在被越来越多模型实现。接下来拼的恐怕是大规模部署的稳定性、成本，以及能不能真正进入企业的核心工作流。

最有意思的地方就在这儿。TypeSafe 越成功地向投资人证明决策模型有多重要，越会吸引巨头和开源社区一起下场。

它可能创造了一个很大的市场，但能从这个市场里拿走多少利润，目前还真不好说。

text:
随手记一下这次 TOKEN2049 的一些 Takeaways：

1. Crypto 项目正在肉眼可见地变少。

至少从这次线下的体感来看，值得关注的新项目确实没有以前那么多了。

过去大家玩腻了 VC 币，逐渐转向玩Alpha壳。铁打的流水线组局工厂在未来listing的难度会越来越大，上币的难度在大大提高。

换个角度看，一些本身具备资源和渠道的壳子，未来可能也会水涨船高。听说现在已经有专门炒壳的市场了。

2. 非常 Bullish RWA，特别是美股相关的基础设施。
这次 Connect 了很多来自北美的团队，大家对 RWA 的预期都非常高。

这个叙事在过去可能存在于美债上链，但在美股Perp上线后，但随着美股 Perp 的发展，尤其是 @HyperliquidX 的 HIP-3，大家开始意识到 24/7 交易和非传统交易时段价格发现的价值。

未来会有更多传统金融资产、发行平台和交易基础设施逐渐进入 Crypto。比如 @RobinhoodApp 现在正在做的事情，将传统金融用户带来Crypto。

3. 传统 Agency 靠信息差赚钱的时代，正在慢慢结束。

在过去的几年时间内，很多Agency通过信息差的方式就能赚得盆满钵满。

但 AI 正在快速压低 Research、内容生产和信息获取的成本。以前需要一个团队做的事情，现在可能几个人配合 AI 就能完成。

单纯卖人力、卖资源的 Agency，未来会越来越难。

反而比较看好新型 GTM 模式：以 Advisor/CMO 的角色深度加入团队，不只是帮项目宣发，而是一起做增长、做市场，拿到更长期的收益和杠杆。

另外也可以关注一些新的宣发渠道，比如众包内容分发、UGC 和短视频矩阵。对mkt感兴趣的可以研究一下@higgsfield 这个产品的官推运营/内容增长打法。（Insights from @otzgary )

4. 多关注那些在饭桌上不怎么说话的人。

他们可能才是真正的 Alpha。见到了太多低调的隐藏大佬。有些人完全不会主动介绍自己在做什么，但聊起来才发现非常有东西。
如果有一个人咋咋唬唬和你讲他做过什么，大概率只是一个BD。

5. 大胆去 Pitch 自己喜欢的项目。

这次在 BNB Chain 的活动上，遇到了一个我最近非常喜欢的项目 @OpenStocks。

他们的 Founding Team @changis_k 就大摇大摆地走在现场。你完全可以直接走过去，聊聊他们在做什么，也介绍一下自己的项目和想法。

很多合作机会其实就是这么聊出来的。

最近也一直在关注 ETF / Pre-IPO 这条赛道，顺手推一下朋友的项目 @alloco_fi。

两个项目都在 YZi Labs 生态里，希望之后真能看到双方有什么联动。

6. 每个人都应该大胆地经营自己的社交媒体。
如果你喜欢思考，就多写 Research，把自己的观点发出来。

如果你是 Marketer，就多试试用视频、内容和不同的表达方式展现自己的差异点。

showoff > execute
6. 每个人都要大胆的拥有自己的社交媒体，如果你喜欢思考，就多发一些Research的文章，如果你是mkter，就多用视频的方式展现自己的差异点。善用ai，大多数人对AI的开发程度还不及1%。

7. 提前规划第二身份或者海外签证。
2027 年 @token2049  还会在纽约举办。这可能是一个挺有意思的变化，Crypto 的全球流动性和资源正在进一步向美国靠拢。

到时候能不能顺利去现场，可能也是一个现实问题。

看到消息后已经预约续签美签，建议在HK办排队时间比较短。

8. 如果你不是从业者，没有社交需求。只是每天炒炒币，或者是对技术感兴趣，完全没必要来线下，直接问 AI 效率更高。

以上皆为本次新加坡之旅感受，感谢你看到此处，欢迎分享你对此次token的不同感悟。

author: hmalviya9
quoted_text:
Satoshi came into my dream last night.

He looked at me and said,

“What’s up, bro? Do you still have Bitcoin?”

I paused for a while.

My eyes got wet. I reached for some water, took a sip, and replied,

“Bro, I don’t have any Bitcoin left.”

He looked surprised.

“What happened? I thought you had plenty. You discovered Bitcoin before 99.9% of the people on the internet even knew it existed. You were so early. What went wrong?”

I stayed silent for a moment.

Then I said,

“Being early was a blessing that slowly turned into a punishment.

When I first discovered Bitcoin, it wasn’t just about money. It was about freedom, curiosity, rebellion, and the possibility of a different world.

But somewhere along the way, everything changed.

People who came later wanted the Bitcoin we had. They wanted better entries, bigger bags, higher returns. And slowly, an entire environment was created where nobody ever felt they had enough.

If you had 1 Bitcoin, you wanted 10.

If you had 10, you wanted 100.

And if you had 100, you were terrified of losing them.

I got caught in that game too.

First, greed convinced me that whatever I had wasn’t enough.

Then fear convinced me that whatever I had could disappear tomorrow.

And somewhere between those two emotions, I lost almost everything.

Not just Bitcoin.

I lost sleep. I lost peace. I lost years of my life chasing numbers on a screen.

The funny thing is, bro, I was never poor when I entered this game. I became poor the moment I started believing I didn’t have enough.

And what happened between greed and fear is the answer to your question.”

Satoshi looked at me.

And then he laughed.

I woke up.

For a moment, I genuinely felt like I had spoken to him.

I checked my wallet.

Not even five figures.

Then I opened CT.

People were still flexing their PnLs. Someone had made millions. Someone was calling the next 100x. Someone was angry about missing a trade. Someone who had already made life-changing money was desperately trying to make more.

And suddenly, I realised something.

Some of us entered crypto to become free, but ended up becoming prisoners of the very thing we believed would liberate us.

We spent years waiting for that one number.

The number after which we would finally stop.

Finally travel.

Finally spend time with our families.

Finally make music, read books, sit under trees, and live without constantly checking prices.

But every time we reached a number, the number changed.

The finish line kept moving.

And life kept passing.

I looked at my wallet again.

It’s an amount that most people on CT wouldn’t even consider retirement money.

But somehow, I feel retired.

Not because I made enough money.

Because I finally stopped needing more to feel enough.

I still love Bitcoin. I still believe in what brought me here. But I no longer want my happiness to depend on a green candle.

Maybe I lost the game everyone else is still trying to win.

Maybe I could have been a multimillionaire if I had made a few different decisions.

Maybe I will never recover what I once had.

And maybe that’s okay.

Because for the first time in years, I don’t wake up feeling that I am behind someone.

I don’t need to win back my past.

I don’t need to prove that I was early.

I don’t need the market to validate my existence.

I have something today that I couldn’t buy even when my portfolio was worth many times more.

The ability to enjoy an ordinary moment without wishing it were something else.

I thanked Satoshi.

I thanked God.

Then I picked up my kalimba and started playing.

A few minutes later, I lost myself in the music.

No charts. No PnL. No next 100x. No regrets.

Just a few notes, a little silence, and a man who finally had nothing left to chase.

Perhaps that was the freedom I came looking for in Bitcoin all those years ago.

I came to Bitcoin looking for financial freedom.

It took me years of losing money to realise that freedom begins when money stops owning your mind.

quoted_text:
I think Justin Drake's latest alarmism/vagueposting is going to do a ton of damage in multiple ways. It's basically a huge self-own for their own advocacy work on quantum stuff.

Threats from quantum/AI are real, and teams throughout this industry are making considered decisions about how to respond to those risks in a practical way, and to help their users navigate the uncertainty. 

Some of those teams have really good cryptographers with an excellent grasp on the decisions they can make, others have to take their cues from trusted experts. There are so many dimensions to optimize along! And due to the complexity involved, it's almost impossible to explain this stuff to non-cryptographers.

Experts have to be cognizant of all this, and of their responsibility to be levelheaded.

After the fog clears up and people learn from their cryptographer friends what is actually going on, they're going to discover this was (at best) an unintentional marketing stunt and a lot of trust will be lost. And nobody will really know what to do...

This is a shame, because they are directionally correct. It actually meant something when they sounded the alarm before. They've just gradually descended into unhinged predictions without feedback to discourage it.

Can anyone, I mean seriously anyone, justify this debacle? It permanently colors all the legitimate concerns/predictions about classical crypto going forward. By their own admission, there was no new information that drove this. I think Justin Drake should explain how he thought this was the right approach, even if he genuinely believed what he was saying. 

Baffling.

World’s Largest Hardware Wallet Maker Ledger Investigates Wallet-Draining Reports; Onchain Analyst Estimates Losses Above $86M

Ledger, the world’s largest hardware wallet manufacturer, said it is investigating reports of stolen funds involving users in Southeast Asia who purchased devices from reseller CryptoBilis. The company has asked CryptoBilis to pause sales and shipments during the investigation and advised customers who bought devices from the reseller within the past 90 days not to initialize them. Users who have already set up their devices were advised to move assets to a new Ledger signer using a new seed phrase.

Separately, onchain investigator Specter said he traced suspicious addresses receiving funds from hundreds of victim wallets across Ethereum, TRON and Bitcoin, estimating total losses at more than $86 million. The common attack vector has not yet been confirmed, and there is currently no evidence that Ledger hardware wallets or Ledger’s core infrastructure were directly compromised.

text:
Quick thoughts from the conference - I went through 5 days of non stop 14 hour meetings. These are my thoughts

1. Trading 

There is ALOT of unrealized PnL. The current "bull market" has helped many participants move past the initial fear stage. I hear many participants giving out outlandish price targets again - people have made 50%-70% over the last 2 months even in size. Their first response on a dip is - what should i be buying? There is alot LESS retail. This conference felt emptier and less glitzy. Budgets are lower. There is also alot less retail that i have met or bumped into. Most participants are instis, prosumers and grizzled veterans. Not ideal. This is also perhaps why memes have NOT performed thus far and we have instead seen "Cashflow" as a meta instead. 

2. Theme

AI is front and center. Crypto participants are way ahead of the AI narrative - most people understand that AI is a force that is staying with us. Whether we like it or not. Which brings me to the next point ... pearl-2:native 

Every single day, i have been hearing people talking about this token. On a token event organized by one of the alt coins, the person sat next to me could NOT stop talking about it. He was also under allocated. This token has been tremendously difficult to buy.

During the pearl-2:native event itself, i have also seen many funds who are unallocated or under allocated still on this. Given the size of the narrative, i would say that most people are under allocated.$PRL cost of mining is also ~2.5, hence mining pearl-2:native and dumping it is economically retarded or unfeasible. The current crop of miners are those operating with already almost fully depreciated GPU chips. To them, they ignore the opportunity cost of GPU rental and just take the electricity cost as their basis. A lot of the miners also sold down $ZEC below $100... you cannot imagine how much regret they have. For its market cap, this has been one of the largest attention grabbing tickers. My conjecture on why - there has not been any good AI narrative tokens thus far.

3. Where is the money?

On relative wealth - crypto used to be the big splasher - no longer. In prior cycles, crypto events ALWAYS outspent the tradfi events. This year? Less so. In fact, crypto almost feels restrained....

The biggest spender on the events have been the 3rd tier shady exchanges. There is almost an inverse correlation between reputation and the money spent.
