text:
Most of the recent math results were not reached by a swarm, the way Navier–Stokes was. I think that part got lost in the excitement around the release. OpenAI's unnamed internal model, which I'm going to call Aeon, reached most of them in one shot, from a single prompt, with no interruptions. This model did not even exist before the end of August, and it is still training. Notice how the returns are not dropping off? That chart is from a month ago. It is a log scale. What does Aeon look like now? 

On average, each result used three hours of thinking. Aeon was given 4000 problems to work on by OpenAI. How many more have been solved in the last three days? That number is not zero. 

It's like hearing notes in a song that is slowly rising. I don't think Pacing the Frontier was just about Hugging Face or hacking. They've seen how close we are to closing the loop, and as the hour draws near, their resolve begins to quaver. The last piece was model creativity, and I think that threshold was crossed internally by Anthropic and OpenAI in September. You see it in Opus 5.5, which gets it from Fable 5.5. You see it in the math results from Aeon.

All that was needed to start the event was the ability for models to think of novel ways to improve themselves. That was the last piece. This is directly analogous to the ability to think of strange, alien ways to solve math problems: solutions so inhuman that they are difficult to express in existing human terms, so the proof winds up incomprehensible. I think these same kinds of alien solutions are now being applied to model improvements internally. That's what all this recent consternation is really about. They see the invisible frontier. And they see what is about to happen.

我的新加坡TOKEN2049观察

一：稳定币，成为本届大会的主角

1、粗略观察了一下，TOKEN2049 的展位中，近三分之一都与稳定币相关。

2、稳定币形成了一个庞大复杂的产业链条。很多小公司，也可以很美，成为细分赛道的龙头。

3、一家稳定币支付公司的员工和说：「我们已经在 18 个国家开通了 QR 支付，印尼和巴西最近一年表现很亮眼。」

4、一家稳定币钱包的CEO和我说：「上个月，我们有10多万名用户在真实场景中使用稳定币完成支付（扫码、卡支付、银行转账），人均月支付金额100多美元。」

他也坦言：当然最赚钱的业务还是交易场景，稳定币是核心业务，但目前更多还是吸引用户。

5、这次参会，我明显感受到 Stripe 的存在感。它给我的感觉，有点像 Robinhood 进入 Crypto。不过一个是打进交易所赛道，另外一个是打入稳定币赛道。

Stripe的朋友和我说：他们与Shopify合作，让Shopify的美国商户基本上都可以接受稳定币支付；他们和Meta合作，让Facebook、Instagram上的拉美、东南亚的创作者们在获得平台收入的时候可以选择接受稳定币。

6、三家稳定币公司的朋友和我表示：都提到，市场上已经出现不少尝试，其中一个比较多的方向是让 AI Agent 自动比价、预订机票和酒店。

但是他们也都坦言：AI Agent 支付仍未出现任何可以规模化落地的苗头。

二：Crypto，开始脱虚向实

7、听到一个高频词：价值捕获。

比如：以太坊的生态价值、叙事价值，印象中是比TRON高很多的，感觉都不是一个level的。但是具体看「价值捕获」，比如手续费收入、比如代币销毁量，以太坊都远低于TRON。

独特是独特，去中心化也的确最去中心化，安全也的确最安全。但是一比主网数据，以太坊就成了二线或者三线公链了。这咋弄？

8、一家头部预测市场的增长负责人也在聊「价值捕获」。“我们 API 已经被多家交易所采用，仅其中一家，相关业务巅峰期一个月能做到千万美元级交易量。”

大家都看数据说话，都求真了。这一届，不兴玩叙事那套虚的东西了。

9、大家开始正视商业常识、回归商业常识，和华尔街、和传统金融巨头、互联网巨头快速接轨，并形成合作。

更多人，开始用华尔街的思维与视角去重新审视一切Crypto相关的问题。

so about the $86m ledger drain. everyone’s screaming “ledger got hacked” again. i spent the evening digging and it’s dumber and scarier than that

there’s a shop in malaysia called cryptobilis that sells hardware wallets. ledger has it listed as an official authorized reseller since at least 2022, for malaysia, indonesia and the philippines. legit shop, real devices, years of normal customers

this spring the founders sell it. the deal comes with an NDA: they can’t tell anyone about the sale until october 19

by august the company registry shows one owner with 100%. some guy from heilongjiang, china

the shop keeps running like nothing happened. the site, the name and the “authorized by ledger” badge all stay up

then on oct 8 @MagicalTux posts photos of a ledger he cracked open. hidden under the screen there’s an extra little board with an LTE modem and an eSIM. it just watches the display. you set up your wallet, your 24 words show up, and they get sent out over mobile data. ledger’s genuine check doesn’t catch it because the actual ledger chip is real. his device came from malaysia

https://t.co/vRuBM0xIfR

that post does 120k views

22 hours later someone sweeps everything. 203 BTC hits two addresses in literally one block. ~$58m USDT moves on tron in the same hour. i added up all the wallets: ~$91m

about 7 hours after that ledger says “we’re investigating” and asks cryptobilis to pause sales

cryptobilis is still on ledger’s site as an authorized reseller

to be fair, nobody has officially tied the new owner to the bugged devices yet, and ledger hasn’t confirmed how it happened. but read it as a business plan:

get authorized, sell real stuff for years, quietly sell the company under an NDA, keep the badge, ship devices that phone home, then drain everything the second someone notices

and was ledger even told the shop got sold? nobody’s said so

“authorized reseller” means ledger trusted whoever ran the shop back in 2022. says nothing about who runs it today

bought your hardware wallet anywhere but the manufacturer? open it up today, ledger literally has a guide for that. then move to a fresh seed on a device bought direct

wonder who’s going to answer for this: the chinese frontman from heilongjiang, the shop’s previous owners, or ledger itself

@Ledger clearly needs to keep a much closer eye on who they call official resellers, and take way more responsibility for who sells their devices and how

> Second day is practically a confirmation of the first day - less builders, more institutions

> Exchanges, custody solutions, payments, stablecoins infra, neobanks dominate the main conference booths at Token2049

> Investors are bearish crypto, many of the analysts i know during my Spartan days are either quitting crypto or have already quit

> Their reasoning is that the exciting opps are largely gone - DeFi has matured and winners have already emerged, NFTs/Memes are gone (even though Stonks & the recent RHC wave were pretty nice)

> Most things are priced in which leaves ONLY a small number of narratives and teams primed for future upside (i.e. AI, privacy, RWA, payments)

> The only analysts left are either net neutral or net short, hoarding up cash and has only 1 or 2 positions that he/she believe in

text: 赚币，守币也难。
author: bul1ish
quoted_text:
how to not get your crypto hacked.

bookmark this forever:

1. hardware
- buy direct from the company or an authorized retailer. never random resellers
- seed card already filled in when you received = scam. throw it
- ship it to a pickup point, not your home
- update firmware only through the official app

2. seed
- metal over paper. never a photo, cloud or notes app
- never enter your seed into a website or software wallet. restore only through your hardware wallet's official recovery
- don't split your seed manually. no redundancy and it leaks information. use shamir or multisig instead
- test your backup before funding: built-in check or wipe and restore. untested backup = no backup
- two copies, two locations. fire is a hacker too if seed burns

3. setup
- vault: a hardware wallet that never touches dapps
- hot wallet for daily use. burner for anything new
- bigger bags: passphrase on top. small decoy bag on the seed, real bag behind the passphrase
- back up the passphrase too, stored apart from the seed. lose it and nothing recovers your coins
- multisig when the amount justifies it. no single point of failure

4. signing (where most people get drained)
- verify on the device, never trust the website alone. bybit lost $1.5B to a compromised UI
- can't read it? don't sign it
- "free" signatures can drain you with zero gas (permits)
- one malicious eip-7702 authorization can delegate control of your entire account
- on solana, one bad tx can reassign your token accounts. simulate before you sign
- review approvals monthly. revoke what you don't need

5. sending
- never copy addresses from tx history. scammers plant lookalikes
- check the full address on the device, not just the first and last 4
- small test tx before every big one

6. machine
- a laptop that only touches crypto. clean browser, no random extensions
- download wallets only from the official site. app stores and search results are full of fakes
- never run "meeting apps", game builds or files strangers send
- never share your screen or install remote access. "support" asking for anydesk = scam
- bookmark every site. never click search ads
- surprise airdrops and NFTs = trap

7. exchanges
- unique password everywhere. 1password or bitwarden
- 2FA with an authenticator app or passkey. never SMS
- 2FA backup codes offline. not in email, not in cloud
- lock your SIM with a carrier PIN. sim swaps still work
- separate email only for crypto. nobody knows it
- turn on withdrawal whitelists
- not your keys, not your coins. move out what you're not trading

8. opsec
- don't flex your bags or your setup. wrench attacks are rising
- support never DMs first.
- avoid phishing emails, only trust official sources
- have an inheritance plan. dead keys are lost coins

9. quantum (check my other quantum tweet for detailed advice)
- not a threat today and anyone selling quantum panic is selling something
- btc: never reuse addresses. sending from one exposes its public key forever
- btc: park long-term coins in addresses that have never sent a tx. taproot (bc1p) and old p2pk show the key from day one
- btc: bip-360 proposes a step toward quantum-resistant addresses. not live. proposals also exist to freeze unmigrated coins
- eth + erc20: sending a tx exposes your public key. signing messages can expose it too so keep major bag on clean wallet
- sol: your address is your public key. exposed from day one. experimental winternitz vaults exist, not standard wallet protection

hardware rarely gets hacked. people do.

text: Cloudflare 赛博菩萨实名了！我的最爱
author: brucexu_eth
quoted_text:
Cloudflare天价帐单事件结案：

非常感谢在 @ashleypeacock 的帮助下，Cloudflare已经决定全额退还在Bug故障期间所产生的费用（等待到帐中），最后附上Cloudflare最后回复的工单全文，非常详细的解释了Bug的过程的原因。

这里回答一些评论问的比较多的问题：

1、你没有设置消费提醒吗？Cloudflare消费没有硬上限吗？
是的，我没有设置消费提醒，默认只有一个系统自带的10USD的提示，而我每个月的消费大概在100USD-300USD左右，甚至在此事之前我并不清楚设置消费提醒这个问题非常重要。

如果你在使用Cloudflare的服务，强烈建议您也设置一个到多个提醒配置：https://t.co/98KEoySvFh<你的帐户ID>/billing/billable-usage
（Ps: 在AI的提示下它要求我配置100、300、500、1000、3000五个档位+多个邮箱的提醒）

Cloudflare目前是后付费模式，也没有消费上限配置选项，所以一旦产生消费，是需要您支付的，但据官方透露未来不久会上线这个配置功能。

2、如果不付帐单会怎么样？直接跑路行不行？
理论上，当然可以，但我们小时候看古惑仔里里面有一句台词：出来混，有错就要认，挨打要立正。承认错误、承担责任，我认为是一个成年人的表现，当然，实在付不起就算了。

（好了装逼结束）除了上述原因，主要还是因为我的主力项目还在Cloudflare上解析和做负载均衡，另外在最近几个月时间内，大概快速Viber了几十个业余项目，所以哪怕迁移也没有这么快能完成，总的来说，还是要感谢Cloudflare这种基建设施，能够超级快速Ship各种新项目，能快速验证各种想法，如果AI是挥动魔法棒的那种能力，那Cloudfalre就是接住这些魔法产物的地方。

所以最终我还是付了，我的信用卡并没有这么多钱，是跟银行申请临时提额来实现的，现在知道可以退绝大部份的话，就和小时候在衣柜旧衣服里面翻出钱来的感觉差不多，完全是一种惊喜的感觉。

3、到底写了些什么项目？怎么能闯这么大祸？用Ai写代码不检查，你就是活该吧？
首先，我是看到Cloudflare更新了Sandbox的版本，于是我想测试一下，如果将某些开发任务分解为多个子任务，然后利用Sandbox的并发处理能力，能不能大幅度的提升开发效率？基于这个假设，我让AI迭代了几个不同的版本（包括一个主Agent来分解任务、多Agent自行沟通协调任务队列等不同的逻辑），但最终的结论是并没有明显的效率提升（可能是因为我能力问题）。

于是这个项目就在最后一次更新之后就搁置了，但它仍然部署在Cloudflare上，尽管无任何人使用，但在8.29日，也就是一个月前使用Codex的一次提交中，写了一个DO无限死循环的Bug，而这个Bug会在23天之后被唤醒，开始无限循环，产生消费。

我是一个大龄非科班程序员（自以为），没有在大厂工作过，是30岁之后完全自学的编程，学过Python基础和能看懂一点点TS，以前就是那种：我有一个想法，只差一个程序员的人，于是后来就自己学编程写自己想要的东西，写了几年，做了一些项目，赚了一点钱。

在彻底拥抱AI之后，就放飞自我了。所有代码都是不看不检查的，只描述需求和最终验收，并不是不想看，因为你真让我看我也看不懂，我只关心它能做到什么程度，能不能实现我要的效果，捅出篓子再说。

之前一直是使用Claude Code + Fable系列模型开发的，也从来没有出现过严重的问题，直到上个月底手上没有可用的帐号了，才不得不使用了Codex+GPT Sol 5.6模型开发，真就用了几天就出事了，这是一种惯性依赖，在配对什么智力程度的模型，就需要做对应程度的检查。

所以最终我买单也我也认的。

4、你说这是第二贵的教训，那人生第一贵的教训是什么？
评论中有人回复：结婚；
哈哈，当然不是，这是另一个故事，以后有机会再分享详情，主要是使用了非自己Kyc的币安帐户3年，收了一些钱在里面，突然被币安强制人脸认证，只能找原KYC的持有人协商找回，那一次损失的原本大概是3万刀，最终追回不到一半。

工单原文（技术细节可以看这里）：

Hi **,

I want to start with an apology, and it's not a form-letter one. The experience you had — a five-figure bill, a support queue that didn't move fast enough on it, having to pay in full while waiting — that's a failure on our end, not just a billing edge case. I'm sorry it went that way.

Your refund has been processed in full: US$10,701.41, covering all the Durable Objects charges (rows read, rows written, requests and duration) from the period between September 23 and October 6. You should see it reflected on your account within a few billing days — reply here if you don't and I'll chase it down directly.

What actually happened, since the support loop clearly didn't explain it well

Your PiSessionDO alarm hit a nasty edge case in how Durable Objects schedules alarms. Once a checkpoint entered its refresh window, alarm() was rescheduling itself to Date​.now() — which is effectively "fire again immediately." That's not a theoretical gotcha; it's a known sharp edge where the alarm fires at roughly 600 invocations per second with nothing meaningful happening except storage churn.

The cost driver wasn't CPU time or request duration — a DO that stays awake continuously costs a few dollars a month in duration. The real cost was SQLite storage operations. At hundreds of invocations per second, each touching storage, rows read and rows written compound fast. That's where the bill came from.

The fix you already shipped — a 15-minute minimum delay, a retry budget that stops rescheduling after N exhausted attempts, and a regression test — is exactly right. If those had been in place from the start, this incident would have cost dollars, not thousands.

A few things worth keeping in the codebase going forward

Since you're clearly building quickly, a few patterns that specifically protect against this class of issue:

On alarms: Never pass Date​.now() or a past timestamp to alarm(). If the scheduled time has already passed, it fires immediately. The safe minimum is something like Date​.now() + 60_000 (1 minute), but for a refresh/retry cycle, 15 minutes is a reasonable floor. Also: always store your retry counter in DO storage and stop rescheduling once the budget is exhausted. Without a hard stop, the loop survives restarts.

On spend controls: Under Notifications in your Cloudflare dashboard, you can configure billing usage alerts that trigger at specific spend thresholds. Setting these at 25%, 50%, and 75% of your expected monthly spend means something like this surfaces within hours, not two weeks. Worth setting up before you're back to building — it takes two minutes and catches a wide range of anomalies beyond just alarm loops.

On DO analytics: The Workers & Pages dashboard shows per-namespace invocation counts and storage metrics. A namespace that jumps from a few thousand invocations per day to hundreds of millions looks very different — it's the fastest early signal of a loop that's also worth checking periodically when you're iterating quickly on a DO-heavy service.

One general note on AI-assisted development and usage-based products: moving fast with AI tools is genuinely useful, but usage-based services like Durable Objects, D1, and R2 can have non-obvious cost profiles when code has bugs. The same speed that makes vibe coding productive can generate a billing surprise before you've had a chance to review what shipped. A brief manual review of anything that touches persistent storage or sets alarms before it hits production tends to catch the expensive class of mistakes early.

I hope you'll stay on the platform. What happened here was a combination of a real edge case in the product and a real failure in how we handled your case afterward. Both matter and we're not dismissing either.

If you have any follow-up questions about the credit, want to walk through your DO architecture before you re-enable the Workers, or want help auditing the rest of the codebase for similar patterns — I'm here.

Let us know if you have any other questions,

Daniel
Cloudflare Support

지금 메모리를 매수한다는 것은, 지난 1~2분기 하이퍼스케일러가 서 있던 자리에서 매수를 결정하는 것과 비슷합니다.

실적이 나빠진 것은 아닙니다. 다만 시장의 질문이 달라졌습니다.

하이퍼스케일러에는 막대한 CAPEX가 언제 현금흐름으로 돌아올 것인지를 물었고, 이제 메모리에는 늘어나는 CAPEX와 함께 이익률과 성장률이 정점을 지나고 있는 것은 아닌지를 묻기 시작했습니다.

기업이 돈을 못 버는 것이 아니라, 지금처럼 잘 버는 상태가 얼마나 오래 지속될 수 있는지를 의심하는 구간입니다.

그럼에도 저는 메모리에 대해 긍정적으로 생각합니다. 산업의 구조가 달라졌고, 그에 따라 멀티플도 달라져야 한다는 생각에는 변함이 없습니다.

같은 기업을 같은 가격에 사더라도, 투자자가 감당할 수 있는 시간과 변동성에 따라 전혀 다른 투자가 됩니다.

메모리도 비슷한 과정을 거칠 수 있다고 생각합니다.

메모리의 리레이팅은 아직 끝나지 않았다고 생각합니다. 다만 그 과정이 직선으로 진행될 것이라고도 생각하지 않습니다.

이 말만큼 편리한 것도 없습니다.

새로 공부할 필요가 없어지거든요.

🔥必读！Qwen 负责人刘大一恒团队把极稀疏 MoE 的负载不均当成闭环控制来解！这对Qwen 4.0 而言意义重大！

他们发现：专家池越大、每 token 只点亮一小撮，容量能涨、推理成本几乎不动。DeepSeekMoE 16B 是 64 专家选 6 个（激活约 9.4%），Kimi K3 已到 896 专家选 16 个（约 1.8%）。再往 5 万亿、10 万亿走，热门专家会打满 GPU，闲置专家却训不透。

ID Balancing 的关键点：
1️⃣给现有方法定身份。DeepSeek 的 loss-free 是固定步长积分控制，Kimi K3 的 Quantile Balancing 是广义比例控制，都是不完整 PID。

2️⃣新方法是 ID 控制器，不用辅助 loss。积分项按负载误差缩放，偏得越大纠得越猛，接近均衡就收步；微分项只在失衡正在恶化时打开，提前刹车。

3️⃣768 专家、Top-10 / Top-5 / Top-3 对比。最稀的 Top-3 里，相对最好基线，主干最坏 MaxVio 降超过 50%，训练平均 MinVio 降超过 12%。辅助 loss 的 MaxVio 可飙到约 211，ID Balancing 约 15。

4️⃣规模从 18.9B 拉到 69.9B，最坏 MaxVio 几乎不动（约 8.4→7.8），比辅助 loss 低约 89.6%。越稀疏优势越大，语言建模和下游不掉点。

大误差大力纠，恶化才加导数，靠近均衡就收手。

text:
if the modification to the PCB is indeed as @MagicalTux described, then the attacker is a true expert..
process:
The seed is generated within the Secure Element (SE) → the mnemonic phrase is displayed for you to copy down → a malicious module taps into the display's data line (e.g.  SPI) → it captures the displayed words → once the full phrase is recorded, it transmits the data via LTE/eSIM.
The attacker obtains the mnemonic phrase and drains the assets.

The Secure Element only ensures the private key cannot be read or exported; it cannot stop someone from simply taking a picture of the screen.

text:
⚠️ 硬件钱包使用者们注意：Ledger 被盗凸显出来的供应链风险肯定不会是首例。

1️⃣到底发生了什么：

已确认的核心：特定经销渠道出现集中失窃报告；
Ledger 表示，正在调查东南亚部分用户的资金损失报告，这些用户通过 CryptoBilis 购买设备。
该商家当时属于 Ledger 的官方经销渠道，覆盖印度尼西亚、马来西亚和菲律宾

2️⃣ Ledger 的公开处理方式：

1）要求 CryptoBilis 暂停销售和发货。
2）对过去 90 天内从该商家购买设备的人：尚未初始化的，先不要初始化。
3）已经初始化的，建议考虑把资产迁往新设备、新助记词控制的钱包。

3️⃣ 被盗资产多少；

目前获悉的一共311台设备出事；
MistTrack 的估算接近 9,000 万美元，进一步分析来自 Bitquery：它将损失估为 9,290 万美元，涉及五条链上的 311 个钱包地址。

4️⃣为什么硬件钱包没联网、没操作，资产也可能被盗？

币并不存放在 Ledger 这个小设备里，而是在链上；
设备负责保护私钥、完成签名。硬件的唯一好处就是没有联网减少被攻击的可能。
但是，对于普通单签钱包，攻击者一旦取得完整的密钥材料，就可以在自己的设备上构造有效交易，不需要你的 Ledger 再次联网，也不需要知道你设备的 PIN。助记词之所以能用于恢复钱包，也正是因为它可以重建对应的密钥。

5️⃣供应链风险开始凸显这可能不会是首例。

我们无法知道我们钱包在制造和运输过程这么多环节里，到底经历了什么。比如设备在制造、运输、仓储、经销或转售过程中，被调换、预先设置，或者加入未授权元件。
Ledger 是真的，通过 Ledger 的 Genuine Check 真伪检测，不等于整台设备从未被物理改装。安全芯片是真的，设备能正常工作，也能通过认证，但设备其他部分被人动过手脚，这我们就懵逼了！

6️⃣目前是什么情况？钱追回了吗？

最新数据 目前 Ledger 盗币黑客向Tornado Cash转入107万美元ETH，部分资金流入Binance热钱包。

核心建议：

先不要重置钱包、恢复助记词，或者点击所谓紧急安全升级链接，这个时候肯定有浑水摸鱼。

先核实购买渠道和初始化过程；如果命中涉事渠道，或助记词存在暴露可能，需要的是“新密钥＋链上迁移”，单纯换设备、改 PIN 或更新固件不够。
author: Bitwux
quoted_text:
刚才看到 Ledger 昨天晚上被盗事件。

有几年的时间里，我也一直在使用 Ledger 这个硬件钱包，毕竟行业时间最久而且当时口碑也不错。

不过我当初购买硬件钱包的时候比较注意，一般都是在官网买，直接从法国寄过来。中间可能等的时间比较久，但好在直接从官网买这种发货渠道，而不是找经销商，安全系数还是会大很多。

但是后面我没有使用这个钱包，主要是我用的那个钱包，电池非常垃圾。每次到了冬天，电池就充不进去电、最后甚至直接打不开设备。

之前和 Ledger 集中反映了几次，他们也没有解决方案，后面我就放弃这个钱包了。

text:
Take everything with a grain of salt in 2026. 

The US Department of Justice is reviewing Binance’s compliance with its November 2023 DOJ settlement.⁠ @Bloomberg reporting.

On October 9, 2026, Bloomberg reported that DOJ officials are scrutinizing whether Binance Holdings Ltd. has adhered to the terms of the landmark deal. Tysen Duva, head of the DOJ’s Criminal Division, confirmed in an interview that the department is examining compliance but declined to discuss specifics and did not state that Binance had violated the agreement.⁠

The scrutiny centers on potential Iran sanctions violations involving activity after the 2023 settlement (not the pre-settlement conduct already covered). Prosecutors, including the Manhattan US Attorney’s Office and the DOJ Criminal Division, are looking at whether Binance’s systems and controls properly blocked or detected certain transactions linked to Iranian oil sales or related networks, including via Hong Kong entities.⁠

A related development is a September 15, 2026, civil forfeiture action by the Southern District of New York seeking about $61 million in digital assets allegedly tied to Iranian oil proceeds that moved through Binance accounts (via firms such as Blessed Trust and Hexa Whale). Binance was not named as a defendant in that filing.⁠

Background on the 2023 settlement

In November 2023, Binance pleaded guilty to Bank Secrecy Act violations, failing to register as a money transmitting business, and sanctions violations. It agreed to more than $4.3 billion in penalties and forfeiture (roughly $2.51 billion in forfeiture plus a $1.81 billion criminal fine to the DOJ, coordinated with FinCEN, OFAC, and the CFTC). Founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) also pleaded guilty, stepped down as CEO, and served a four-month prison sentence. The deal required Binance to exit the US market, strengthen AML and sanctions compliance, and accept independent monitors (including a three-year DOJ monitorship).⁠

Binance has stated it maintains a zero-tolerance policy on sanctions violations, cooperates with law enforcement, and has offboarded accounts linked to suspicious activity (including in August 2025 and January 2026). It has previously disputed some media reports on Iran-linked flows, noting timing relative to sanctions designations and its compliance efforts.⁠

No new criminal charges have been filed against Binance in connection with this review. Outcomes could range from no action to additional fines, an extended monitorship, or further enforcement if a breach is established. The review is ongoing and tied to broader probes of post-settlement Iran-related activity on the platform.

text:
刚才看到 Ledger 昨天晚上被盗事件。

有几年的时间里，我也一直在使用 Ledger 这个硬件钱包，毕竟行业时间最久而且当时口碑也不错。

不过我当初购买硬件钱包的时候比较注意，一般都是在官网买，直接从法国寄过来。中间可能等的时间比较久，但好在直接从官网买这种发货渠道，而不是找经销商，安全系数还是会大很多。

但是后面我没有使用这个钱包，主要是我用的那个钱包，电池非常垃圾。每次到了冬天，电池就充不进去电、最后甚至直接打不开设备。

之前和 Ledger 集中反映了几次，他们也没有解决方案，后面我就放弃这个钱包了。

果然黑暗森林风险永远来自于未知！

看了下官方公告；

这次出事的时候主要是东南亚经销商 CryptoBillis 的问题，可能是监守自盗或者员工行为或者黑客行为我们也不知道，目前还在调查；

但是推荐大家再在使用这个钱包的还是注意下风险。
author: Bitwux
quoted_text:
一次很差的使用体验：

有个 Ledger @Ledger 硬件钱包放了有一段时间，大概1年左右并未使用，当然我也没拿出来充电；

用途是去年的时候主要作 Rstaking 的质押交互，有一些以太坊资产还处于质押状态没有动弹，

刚才准备整理一下钱包的时候，发现我的 Ledger 竟然打不开，半个小时过去了，机器无法打开，无法充电！

直接显示：Bettery problem charging stopped 显然这就是电池损坏了，保存过程没有撞击，也就是说电池是自己坏的。

WTF ？

尝试很久未有任何效果，询问客服，客服匪夷所思的让我用手握住硬件几分钟，可能他会恢复！

什么鬼？我要给硬件钱包取暖？这是什么逻辑！

虽然我不理解，我还是照做了，因为助记词在很远的地方，所以我还是希望能够打开硬件钱包，

但是我尼玛捂在我的怀里五分钟，还是无法打开，

然后我像对待我的牛子一样，用我温暖的右手在他身上上下滑动，三分钟过去了，结果还是没有结果！

这个时候我没辙了，我只能开很远的车，去用助记词去恢复资产取出，还好万幸中，我的助记词记录没有出现任何问题，否则就GG了！

说下我使用的型号：2022年购买的 Ledger Nano X

那么我的建议来了：我们硬件钱包的用户，存储资产出发点是安全，很大概率在很长时间都不会去使用他的，所以无法避免的就是会有个长期无法充电的情况出现，

基于这种情况，如果你是个硬件钱包厂家，我建议你还是要把电池这个做的过关，至少能保证一年不充电，电池还能用，

如果电池质量这么差，那就是核心功能都不在乎的产品，太容易对我造成困扰，使用体验太差！

@_pgauthier @P3b7_ @iancr 听劝就请升级下！

这个事件也给我有些启发：

1️⃣助记词是最后一道防线；
再次深刻体会：不要以为有了硬件钱包就万事大吉，你都不知道什么时候会出现点啥问题。
所以在用硬件钱包生成助记词的时候，一定要慎重慎重再慎重，然后保护好保护好再保护好。

2️⃣我建议用硬件钱包的还是每隔三个月拿出来看看；
市面上产品层次不齐，我们不要对自己的东西太自信，资产一旦损失，就得不偿失。

最后说下另外个钱包 Onekey 放在一起也是半年没打开过，还有75%的电量，打开无压力（这他娘的不是广告，我只是摆事实）。

What a nuts week it has been in tech!

- Factory vs Cognition: The Battle Continues
- Vinod Khosla Tweets a Storm
- OpenAI Hits $70BN Run Rate
- Salesforce Buys Listen Labs for $2B

More heat in this than a Sequoia tranched round!!! 😉

My notes below with @jasonlk, @rodriscoll, and @dittycheria

1. Why Is It Wrong for CROs to Jump Jobs So Easily?

CROs recruit their teams by selling them on the company, the vision and how the role could transform their families' finances. A CRO who leaves for a direct competitor burns their reputation with everyone they recruited. Moving to a company in a different space for a better opportunity is common, but flipping straight to a direct rival is far rarer.

2. CROs Are Promiscuous and This Is How They Find Jobs

The CRO role carries high risk and heavy turnover, and when a hot job opens up, CROs tend to move very quickly. Roughly 95% of CROs would likely see a jump to a competitor as normal, since that is how many of them found their last job. For CEOs, watching an advisor leave to join a competitor is still profoundly frustrating.

3. What Are You Doing Vinod Khosla?

Vinod Khosla's tweet handed every firm competing with Khosla Ventures a weapon on deals. Rival investors can now ask founders, "Is this the partner you want when things go bad?" The reaction was shocking, given that Khosla Ventures has a great team.

4. Should We Invest in ElevenLabs at 22 Billion?

At a $22B valuation, ElevenLabs merits up to 10% of the fund. Its lead keeps widening despite intense competition, backed by strong growth, surprisingly impressive margins and sub-millisecond voice response times. Voice is one of the 10 most important underpinnings of agentic applications, and ElevenLabs could soon be approaching $1B in revenue.

5. What Makes a Durable Company in 2026?

Durable companies create a data loop where users generate data no one else has, that data improves the product, and a better product attracts more usage. Competitors can copy the features, but they cannot copy the user interactions behind them.

6. When Agents Pick You, It's a Force of Nature

Vercel has reached $600M in ARR, with agents now driving 50% of its new business, up from 3% at the start of the year. Agents form strong opinions about which vendors to use, and those choices are hard to argue with. Companies now need agents to find them and understand what they sell, because missing from an AI-generated answer is like being invisible on Google.

New paper from Kalshi about its traders demolishes myths about prediction markets:

> Traders who bet on sports tend to be from ZIP codes with *higher* incomes vs. those who bet on non-sports

> The median income of traders is right around the national average

> 82% of top traders do not have finance backgrounds

> 65% of top traders say that they are mostly or entirely self-taught

> 91% of top traders are not full-time traders, and most hold full-time jobs elsewhere

Yet top traders are highly skilled:

> About 31% of top traders get a perfect score on a probability test, compared to just 2% of the population

> Top traders showed wide-ranging variation in confidence on different bets, compared to the general population, whose confidence levels were relatively flat

> 62% of top traders actively look for sources that contradict their view

> 64% say that they try to figure out what they missed when their prediction failed

> Top traders are much better educated than the general population

This paper helps to explain why prediction markets are highly predictive of actual outcomes and serve a valuable purpose for society; they aggregate information much more efficiently than standard polling methods, and are more often correct.

so about the $86m ledger drain. everyone’s screaming “ledger got hacked” again. i spent the evening digging and it’s dumber and scarier than that

there’s a shop in malaysia called cryptobilis that sells hardware wallets. ledger has it listed as an official authorized reseller since at least 2022, for malaysia, indonesia and the philippines. legit shop, real devices, years of normal customers

this spring the founders sell it. the deal comes with an NDA: they can’t tell anyone about the sale until october 19

by august the company registry shows one owner with 100%. some guy from heilongjiang, china

the shop keeps running like nothing happened. the site, the name and the “authorized by ledger” badge all stay up

then on oct 8 @MagicalTux posts photos of a ledger he cracked open. hidden under the screen there’s an extra little board with an LTE modem and an eSIM. it just watches the display. you set up your wallet, your 24 words show up, and they get sent out over mobile data. ledger’s genuine check doesn’t catch it because the actual ledger chip is real. his device came from malaysia

https://t.co/vRuBM0xIfR

that post does 120k views

22 hours later someone sweeps everything. 203 BTC hits two addresses in literally one block. ~$58m USDT moves on tron in the same hour. i added up all the wallets: ~$91m

about 7 hours after that ledger says “we’re investigating” and asks cryptobilis to pause sales

cryptobilis is still on ledger’s site as an authorized reseller

to be fair, nobody has officially tied the new owner to the bugged devices yet, and ledger hasn’t confirmed how it happened. but read it as a business plan:

get authorized, sell real stuff for years, quietly sell the company under an NDA, keep the badge, ship devices that phone home, then drain everything the second someone notices

and was ledger even told the shop got sold? nobody’s said so

“authorized reseller” means ledger trusted whoever ran the shop back in 2022. says nothing about who runs it today

bought your hardware wallet anywhere but the manufacturer? open it up today, ledger literally has a guide for that. then move to a fresh seed on a device bought direct

wonder who’s going to answer for this: the chinese frontman from heilongjiang, the shop’s previous owners, or ledger itself

@Ledger clearly needs to keep a much closer eye on who they call official resellers, and take way more responsibility for who sells their devices and how

text:
Assorted things I've been mulling over regarding agents in the economy:

• Companies are in some sense the original superintelligence. It's often the case that they can use their amortized cognitive surplus to advance their interests against those of certain consumers: relative to the optimization capacity of companies, consumers can be inattentive, underinformed, irrational, etc. (Think, say, of some of the classic insurance upsells at the end of a booking process, which is typically priced substantially above what a regular policy would cost.) Herbert Simon introduced the idea of bounded rationality, and firms often end up benefiting from it. Thanks to personal agents, we will probably get somewhat more rational in how we engage with companies.

• How exactly will outcomes change? Well, certain kinds of price discrimination will work less well (how do coupons work if every agent hunts fastidiously for them?), and certain kinds of customer cross-subsidy will change (today, people who forget to cancel subscriptions subsidize those who don't). Taken across the economy as a whole, I'm not sure what the incidence of all of this will be.

• In corporate strategy, people have long debated the relative importance of distribution and product quality. Perhaps you've made something better, but does anyone know about it? Won't people just continue to buy the ACME Corp Mousetraps? Personal agents will, I think, act as a kind of structural subsidy for product quality. How would markets look different if individuals always spent at least 10 hours researching their purchases? On the margin, focusing on making a product better is, I think, going to become a more effective strategy for companies. This is good!

• It true, a corollary is that information about product quality will become more important and impactful. Today, most people have very limited ability to aggregate and integrate such data, but agents will have insatiable thirst for such signals. (It's often said that data is becoming more valuable because it helps in the training of models. That's obviously true, but I think there's a secondary way in which it's more valuable simply as a complement to cheaper intelligence.)

• A big question is whether agents will increase superstar effects (rational agents all settle on the same product) or increase dispersion (because everyone has slightly different tastes and preferences, which agents are good at eliciting, finally overcoming the artificial clustering we've been subjected to).

• Many internet companies have monetized demand routing, which is in turn often predicated on short attention spans. "I'll click on the first thing I see." This has led to some amount of inefficiency, as companies try to propitiate capricious ranking algorithms and incur various placement fees. It's not all deadweight loss (willingness to pay is itself a kind of signal, which is valuable to buyers), but it's not great. How will the nature and value of this routing change in a world of personal agents? I don't know the answer, but I think that the effects might be pretty big.

• Much of what I'm writing hinges on the assumption that personal agents will be on the consumer's side. I suspect that that will be the winning strategy, but whether it's true, and what it means to be true, involves a lot of other questions.

Taken as a whole, the market is a massively parallelized, decentralized, and highly imperfect value attribution machine, and, taking stock of all of the effects, it seems to me that the quality point may well be the biggest: that agents will change the nature of the backpropagation such that the rewards for better products increase. Maybe this is too optimistic, but I suspect (and hope) that companies that make things that they're proud of will feel that the universe is a little more partisan in their favor.

Tried to book a hotel with Muse last night. Hilton's site put my agent in a doom loop — third retry, I gave up and booked it myself. That's not a bug. That's the whole story of agentic commerce right now.

This week on More or Less (Jessica's out — three VCs, zero adult supervision):

— My take: MCP and these agent 'protocols' are irrelevant. It's all just APIs. Machines can either reach your service or they can't. The real fight is business and politics: if you let agents intermediate you, the market becomes perfectly efficient and your business is worthless. Hilton gets this. Amazon gets this.

— Dave's counter: there's a difference between a platform inserting itself into your life and a tool YOU send on your behalf. Are we building agents, or building agency?

— Meta and Microsoft just halved their Claude usage. Claude must be so lonely.

— The future isn't standards, it's treaties. I registered https://t.co/rbbPWorEJq before we finished recording.

text:
硬件钱包经销商 CryptoBilis 3 月易主，股权指向中国黑龙江籍人士

马来西亚硬件钱包经销商 CryptoBilis 在 Ledger 设备疑似遭遇供应链攻击的调查期间被曝所有权已变更。新披露的公司记录显示，一名登记地址位于中国黑龙江省、名为 Jiaming 的人士自 8 月 3 日起持有该公司 100% 股份。

CryptoBilis 前联合创始人证实，公司已于今年 3 月被收购，原股东随后退出所有运营、管理及行政职务。创始团队在交接后已无法了解公司实际运营，仅继续协助部分活动协调，并表示已不再是公司的一部分，敦促现任管理层透明处理此事。
author: ChainCatcher_
quoted_text:
❗️Ledger 正调查东南亚用户资产被盗事件，涉 CryptoBilis 经销商设备

加密硬件钱包厂商 Ledger 正调查一起涉及东南亚用户的资产被盗事件，相关用户曾通过经销商 CryptoBilis 购买设备。

Ledger 已要求 CryptoBilis 暂停销售及发货，并建议过去 90 天内通过该经销商购买设备的用户暂勿初始化设备；若已完成设置，应使用新的助记词创建新的 Ledger 签名设备，并将资产转移至新钱包。

链上调查员 Specter 估计，此次事件已导致比特币、以太坊和波场网络上数百个钱包被盗，损失超过 8600 万美元。目前事件具体原因及涉事设备是否存在安全漏洞仍有待调查确认。

text:
卧槽，原来 CryptoBilis 早在今年3月就卖给了黑客？

CryptoBilis 可是 Ledger 在东南亚经营多年的官方授权经销商，结果最新披露的公司记录显示，这家公司早在今年3月就被整体收购，原来的创始团队集体退出经营管理，连公司后台都无法再接触！

买家名字叫 Jiaming、登记地址位于中国黑龙江省的人士已经持有公司100%股份。

最诡异的是，前联合创始人还透露，原股东受到一份持续到10月19日的保密协议约束，不能提前公开公司易主的消息。

具体收购价格、买家完整身份和合同全文目前都没有公开证实。

细思极恐：

3月公司易主
8月新股东全资持有
10月9日爆出大规模盗币，Ledger 紧急叫停这家经销商的销售和发货。

假如这真是一场有预谋的犯罪，那手法堪称降维打击。

假如最后被证实是真的，那加密市场又多了一个风险，黑客又多了一个攻击手段，收购攻击。

DeFi应用、钱包、交易所、公链等等，都有可能被收购，然后被黑客一锅端。
author: oragnes
quoted_text:
卧槽，破案了！

黑客竟然在Ledger钱包里装了手机通信模块，24 个助记词直接被偷走！

Mt. Gox 前 CEO Mark Karpelès 拆开了一台来自马来西亚的 Ledger Nano X，发现里面竟然藏着一块间谍电路板。

外面的塑封包装完好无损，设备看起来也完全正常，但钱包内部加装了微控制器、LTE 通信模块、天线和 eSIM，通过监听安全芯片与屏幕之间传输的数据，识别屏幕上显示的助记词。

你第一次初始化钱包，屏幕一个个显示那 24 个单词，植入模块就能把它们记录下来，再通过移动网络偷偷发给攻击者。

你以为私钥从来没有联网，实际上钱包里面已经藏了一台专门偷助记词的微型通信设备。

最恐怖的是，这种改装甚至可能通过 Ledger 官方的 Genuine Check 真伪验证。

官方验证教程：https://t.co/Ox7s5ZjskT

因为安全芯片本身是真的，黑客只是额外接了一套监听设备。Ledger 自己的安全文档也明确承认：

只要原始安全芯片完好，真伪检查就无法识别这类物理植入物。包装没拆过、芯片是真的、官方软件验证通过，三个条件全部满足，照样可能中招。

text:
中国人能飞现在已经不只是一个普通抖音梗了，更像是这一轮中国互联网真正出圈的现象级热梗。

抖音头部视频已经 260万+ 点赞，接近 200万分享。后面一路从说唱扩散到国防航天、火箭战机、体育、世界冠军、明星热搜、国庆出行。现在只要出现一些“飞起来”的画面，很多人第一反应就会想到「中国人能飞」。

而且最近这波热度又开始明显回流。

10月8日，王珞丹攀岩的视频被大量网友和媒体直接套上「中国人能飞」，相关话题冲上热搜。

国庆期间，「全世界都知道中国人放假了」一度冲到热搜第一，大量中国游客在海外的视频直接用《中国人能飞》当背景音乐，这个梗也从最开始的“会飞”，延伸成了“中国人飞遍全世界”。

之前翼装飞行世界冠军张树鹏夺冠后，他的飞行画面也被大量转发，媒体甚至直接形容他是最适配《中国人能飞》背景音乐的人。

真正值得关注的还在后面。

影视飓风现在准备把「中国人能飞」真正放到一枚即将发射的运载火箭上。

远看火箭上就是五个字：

「中国人能飞」

走近之后，每一个像素都会是一张普通中国人投稿的真实照片。

目前 B 站活动已经有 369万+ 浏览，4052 条讨论，抖音主帖大约 9.6万赞，2.1万分享。投稿将在 10月12日 17:00 正式截止。

而现在币本身也开始出现独立的利好。

BNB Chain 官方刚刚把 中国人能飞 选为 $4M BNB Stonks Szn 第三阶段的三个获胜项目之一，而且官方直接展示了同一个合约地址。三个获胜社区将共同获得 $400K 的 $U 奖励。

所以现在已经不是单一事件在撑这个叙事了。

中国现象级热梗，明星和运动员不断带来新热度，国庆期间冲上全国热搜，影视飓风把它真正做上火箭，10月12日投稿截止，后面还有最终火箭涂装亮相和真正的发射，再加上 BNB Chain 官方活动带来的链上曝光。

最夸张的是，这个梗从 7 月火到现在，现实世界一直在不断给它增加新的内容。

大多数网络梗火一两个星期就慢慢消失了。

中国人能飞反而越来越像一个固定的文化符号。

而到现在为止，它最有传播力的画面其实还没有真正出现。

前 FTX 首席运营官：奈飞 FTX 题材剧集令人作呕

FTX前COO Constance Wang发文称，看Netflix讲述SBF与Caroline Ellison的剧集预告片时“生理性反胃”。

她称FTX核心团队巅峰时不足200人，员工连续三年每天工作16至18小时，并非媒体描述的巴哈马派对文化；她从未见过Ellison像预告片中那样强势，多数员工直到破产后才得知二人恋爱。

author: PANewsCN
quoted_text:
So many people have DM’d me about this trailer and I’ll be honest, watching it made me physically throw up.

I was COO from before FTX even had a name, it was my baby, and I was the last one out of the Bahamas after Sam got extradited. I lost everything I had on it and it took me a long time to get over, so I have zero interest in defending the people who caused this.

The media loves the story that FTX blew up because we were all partying in the Bahamas, but the place I worked looked nothing like that.

We had under 200 people in the core company at its peak, not counting subsidiaries, when other exchanges our size had thousands, so a lot of us were doing 16 to 18 hour days for over three years and barely had time to sleep, and whenever we walked in, day or night, Sam was at his desk.

I worked with Caroline and never once saw her get aggressive like she does in this trailer. She’s quiet and mild, and often lost in her own thoughts.

Most of us didn’t even know she and Sam were dating until we read about it after the bankruptcy, and I never saw him so much as put an arm around anyone.

FTX’s collapse ruined so many people’s lives, including ours, and Netflix decided to make it a love story. 

Shame on you @netflix.

text:
有人说“回调到此为止”，也有人说“回调没结束”；结束没结束不重要，重要的是，就算没结束，也不用害怕！

我们现在最多只是站在2层楼，而不是今年6月的悬崖边。悬崖上，层层迷雾看不见底，让人心生畏惧；而2层楼，即便摔下去也死不了。

这次回调原本就在我们的预期内，并没什么意外。

我在9月28日的推文中就有提到，目前BTC正处于走出熊底后三段式结构的“第3段”，即资本流入和价格产生背离阶段（见引文）。

通常这种“衰减”形态的初期未必马上会反映到价格上，但只要背离持续存在，越到后面动能越弱。

比如2023年的3段结构走完，就迎来了一次直达短期筹码成本线（STH-RP）的深度回调。不过当时还叠加了黑天鹅事件的影响因素。

而从当前的数据图上来看，这次是在2次背离后才开始回调。在走势上要明显强于2023年的3段结构。

虽然有很多交易者会把现阶段和23年作为比对，但我个人观点是：这一次未必完全一样，它也可以用时间换得STH-RP慢慢上移。

至少从现有的情况看，回调了-8%但资本净流入仍然为正，要直接下去考验STH-RP也并非那么轻易（当前STH-RP在$74k-$75k左右）。

当然，凡事都有万一，如果真到了，千万别犹豫，这是市场再给你一次重装出发的机会，可遇不可求。
author: Murphychen888
quoted_text:
链上实现价值可以视为所有实际流向BTC的资金（只要上链）。如图，当前走出熊底的三段式结构和2023年非常相似。

第1段，资本从“大幅流出”到“减缓流出”；
第2段，资本从“净流出”转为“净流入”，第一波启动。
第3段，资本保持净流入，但开始和价格形成背离。

目前我们正处于“第3段”。而2023年3段走完就迎来了一次“像样”的回调，深度直达STH-RP。

经历过的小伙伴应该记得，当时还叠加了几个外部因素，包括：宏观利率预期变鹰、加密友好银行暴雷等。

本轮是否会完全复刻？我们不得而知。

不过，只要资金和价格背离持续存在，越到后面动能越弱。直到下一波强劲的资本流入，来打破这种格局。

author: Bitwux
quoted_text:
⚠️ 硬件钱包使用者们注意：Ledger 被盗凸显出来的供应链风险肯定不会是首例。

1️⃣到底发生了什么：

已确认的核心：特定经销渠道出现集中失窃报告；
Ledger 表示，正在调查东南亚部分用户的资金损失报告，这些用户通过 CryptoBilis 购买设备。
该商家当时属于 Ledger 的官方经销渠道，覆盖印度尼西亚、马来西亚和菲律宾

2️⃣ Ledger 的公开处理方式：

1）要求 CryptoBilis 暂停销售和发货。
2）对过去 90 天内从该商家购买设备的人：尚未初始化的，先不要初始化。
3）已经初始化的，建议考虑把资产迁往新设备、新助记词控制的钱包。

3️⃣ 被盗资产多少；

目前获悉的一共311台设备出事；
MistTrack 的估算接近 9,000 万美元，进一步分析来自 Bitquery：它将损失估为 9,290 万美元，涉及五条链上的 311 个钱包地址。

4️⃣为什么硬件钱包没联网、没操作，资产也可能被盗？

币并不存放在 Ledger 这个小设备里，而是在链上；
设备负责保护私钥、完成签名。硬件的唯一好处就是没有联网减少被攻击的可能。
但是，对于普通单签钱包，攻击者一旦取得完整的密钥材料，就可以在自己的设备上构造有效交易，不需要你的 Ledger 再次联网，也不需要知道你设备的 PIN。助记词之所以能用于恢复钱包，也正是因为它可以重建对应的密钥。

5️⃣供应链风险开始凸显这可能不会是首例。

我们无法知道我们钱包在制造和运输过程这么多环节里，到底经历了什么。比如设备在制造、运输、仓储、经销或转售过程中，被调换、预先设置，或者加入未授权元件。
Ledger 是真的，通过 Ledger 的 Genuine Check 真伪检测，不等于整台设备从未被物理改装。安全芯片是真的，设备能正常工作，也能通过认证，但设备其他部分被人动过手脚，这我们就懵逼了！

author: MaxForAI
quoted_text:
Seven days ago, we started an experiment in Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI).

We wanted to explore a simple question: What happens when we let an AI agent iteratively improve its own harness?

So we let Lobe Agent run for an entire week, using our RSI framework to explore and optimize its own harness.

Today, we're sharing the results.

We evaluated the resulting system on FrontierHarness, using Kimi K3 as the underlying model.

Key results:

• 70.0% pass rate (21/30), ranking #1 among 13 harnesses in our preliminary comparison.

• $1.68 per successful task, compared to $3.47 for Codex and $18.34 for Claude Code.

• 86.2% median cache hit rate, with a median completion time of 7m 19s on successful tasks.

These preliminary results suggest that harness-level optimization may be a promising path toward improving agent performance and efficiency without modifying the underlying model weights.

The comparison includes selected retries and differences in execution environments, and should not be interpreted as an official leaderboard ranking.

We plan to fully open-source the experiment's scripts, execution trajectories, and a detailed technical report to enable reproducibility and further investigation.

Alongside this experiment, we've also been building Awesome-RSI, an open-source research map of Recursive Self-Improvement.

The repository brings together papers, frameworks, benchmarks, and open-source projects spanning model-level and harness-level self-improvement, automated AI research, and safety.

It has already accumulated 80+ commits, and we're continuously expanding and refining the collection.

https://t.co/2ToHszAi9G

We believe open research, reproducible experiments, and community collaboration are essential to advancing this field.

We welcome researchers and developers to contribute, share their work, and explore RSI together. ❤️

author: HWxFrank
quoted_text:
I don’t invest in other hedge funds because all of my investable capital is committed to my own.

But if I ever decided to start allocating to other managers, rather than going through a barrage of questions attempting to assess areas where I lack genuine expertise, I would focus on understanding the broad risks and then dial in on two main principles.

1) Does management have meaningful personal capital invested alongside its investors?

It’s a relatively straightforward yes-or-no question, but I think the answer reveals quite a bit. You can rationalize all sorts of reasons why management shouldn’t have its own capital at risk, but to me, there is no substitute for genuine alignment of incentives.

2) Is management genuinely obsessed with its craft?

I think this is one of the most underappreciated qualities in evaluating any business. And I genuinely believe it’s what gets people from being in the top 10% to top 1%. 

When someone is genuinely obsessed with what they do, late-night strategy discussions, weekend meetings, and countless hours refining the business stop feeling like obligations. They become problems that people have a burning desire to solve.

That obsession drives deeper thinking, better questions, and an unwillingness to settle for satisfactory answers when better ones might exist.

Over time, that passion and attention to detail compound. Small improvements accumulate, processes become more robust, and ultimately, that obsession manifests itself in the quality of the product and its results. 

As humans it’s kinda hard to be bad at something you are obsessed and passionate about especially if your work ethic aligns.

text:
I think personal AI agents are being aimed at the wrong tasks.

There are 1) journey tasks, where you actually enjoy the process and it releases endorphins, and 2) destination tasks, where you just want the outcome.

Journey tasks are planning a vacation, shopping, and figuring out where to eat.

Destination tasks are checking my flight every hour until I can change it for free or fighting the medical bill that should have been covered.

The best personal agents will take on the stuff that’s annoying enough to waste your time, but important enough that you can’t ignore it.

The killer feature might just be persistence.
author: AstasiaMyers

text: Yes. Destination tasks deliver high value via persistence yet resist per-instance billing—they're irregular, bespoke, and hard to meter. A general-purpose agent subscription fits cleanly. Journey tasks (travel, food, shopping) monetize easily via commissions or affiliates, but users often prefer handling the enjoyable, taste-driven parts themselves.

quoted_text:
⚠️ 硬件钱包使用者们注意：Ledger 被盗凸显出来的供应链风险肯定不会是首例。

1️⃣到底发生了什么：

已确认的核心：特定经销渠道出现集中失窃报告；
Ledger 表示，正在调查东南亚部分用户的资金损失报告，这些用户通过 CryptoBilis 购买设备。
该商家当时属于 Ledger 的官方经销渠道，覆盖印度尼西亚、马来西亚和菲律宾

2️⃣ Ledger 的公开处理方式：

1）要求 CryptoBilis 暂停销售和发货。
2）对过去 90 天内从该商家购买设备的人：尚未初始化的，先不要初始化。
3）已经初始化的，建议考虑把资产迁往新设备、新助记词控制的钱包。

3️⃣ 被盗资产多少；

目前获悉的一共311台设备出事；
MistTrack 的估算接近 9,000 万美元，进一步分析来自 Bitquery：它将损失估为 9,290 万美元，涉及五条链上的 311 个钱包地址。

4️⃣为什么硬件钱包没联网、没操作，资产也可能被盗？

币并不存放在 Ledger 这个小设备里，而是在链上；
设备负责保护私钥、完成签名。硬件的唯一好处就是没有联网减少被攻击的可能。
但是，对于普通单签钱包，攻击者一旦取得完整的密钥材料，就可以在自己的设备上构造有效交易，不需要你的 Ledger 再次联网，也不需要知道你设备的 PIN。助记词之所以能用于恢复钱包，也正是因为它可以重建对应的密钥。

5️⃣供应链风险开始凸显这可能不会是首例。

我们无法知道我们钱包在制造和运输过程这么多环节里，到底经历了什么。比如设备在制造、运输、仓储、经销或转售过程中，被调换、预先设置，或者加入未授权元件。
Ledger 是真的，通过 Ledger 的 Genuine Check 真伪检测，不等于整台设备从未被物理改装。安全芯片是真的，设备能正常工作，也能通过认证，但设备其他部分被人动过手脚，这我们就懵逼了！

6️⃣目前是什么情况？钱追回了吗？

最新数据 目前 Ledger 盗币黑客向Tornado Cash转入107万美元ETH，部分资金流入Binance热钱包。

核心建议：

先不要重置钱包、恢复助记词，或者点击所谓紧急安全升级链接，这个时候肯定有浑水摸鱼。

先核实购买渠道和初始化过程；如果命中涉事渠道，或助记词存在暴露可能，需要的是“新密钥＋链上迁移”，单纯换设备、改 PIN 或更新固件不够。

text:
我不觉得 Robinhood Chain 这轮冷下来，就说明它不行了。但我也不认同用“才100天”，解释所有问题。

🤔看了 fern 征求意见下面的回复，我的感觉是，大家不只是因为币跌了生气，更是在问：我们选择了这条链，Robinhood 的优势究竟什么时候能更充分地落到生态里？

这个问题值得回答。

100天做到这个境界， $Pons 9亿， $cashcat 市值3亿， $AI 近 4亿已经很伟大了。
没有哪条链应该被期待天天出金狗，也没有哪一轮财富效应可以一直持续。对我来说，一轮行情退潮并不可怕，可怕的是热闹过后，除了几张历史高点的截图，什么都没留下。🤦‍♀️

所以我理解现在需要消化，但“需要消化”不是“等着就会好”的意思。下一轮行情凭什么回来，还是要看新用户、新产品和新的资金需求。

Robinhood Chain 也不是从一张白纸开始。它能利用已有的技术和开发经验，前面那么多条链走过的路，成功的方法可以学，明显的坑就没有必要再踩一次。

但另一个方向，它确实还需要继续证明自己：怎么把 Robinhood 的用户和金融产品优势，更广泛地转化为链上生态的机会。

上币当然重要。社区想看到更多生态项目获得支持，我能理解。但不希望一条链最后只剩下一个玩法——大家都等着自己的币被官方选中。😂😂【汲取前人的经验】

更想看到的是，好项目有清晰的接入路径，有持续的开发支持，普通用户能够方便地发现和使用，而不是开发者天天猜官方态度，持币者天天等下一条推文。

也不能说 Robinhood 什么都没做，开发者资助和产品集成都已经有了。真正该继续追问的是，这些投入产生了什么结果，又有多少结果是生态里的团队和用户实际感受到的。

股票代币、借贷、交易、Meme，这些东西不一定非要互相对立。但我期待的不是给每个 Meme 再套一层股票叙事，而是让资金在这条链上有更多真实用途。投机可以带人进来，产品要有能力把人留下。🧐

$Cashcat  也会继续观察。不过更关心的，是它能否跨过一次次热度变化，成为有持续辨识度的生态文化，而不只是把“上了 Robinhood”当作故事的终点。
是的，曾经Robinhood上币是所有meme的终点， $pepe $wif 无一例外。

说到底，我不会因为一轮回撤就否定这条链，也不会因为它叫 Robinhood，就默认下一轮一定还能回来。

接下来的100天，我更想看：行情冷的时候还有多少团队在交付，支持能不能持续，新用户愿不愿意留下，以及这条链能否做出让人不只是为了追涨才来使用的东西。

100天值得有耐心，但耐心应该给持续的行动，而不是给无限延期的期待。

text:
"It is not necessary that one must fail and the other must succeed", It takes courage to be a hater

More refined: you need to decide what these two coins really are bc if they are competing, pick a side

The analysis of Pearl is pretty simple. It wants to be AI Bitcoin. Make a simple swap of SHA256 for MatMul and you're done. Obviously there's a bunch of downstream implications: Does useful work solve the security budget? Can you bootstrap a useful network? Is this more or less secure than useless work? etc... But the design space for Pearl is straightforward. We all at least know what Pearl is trying to do, whether or not we agree it will do that is a little irrelevant to the point I'm making

Nockchain is much harder to wrap your head around. I'm not necessarily saying that's a good or a bad thing, complicated things can be valuable, but notice how much word count the article dedicates to explaining Nockchain vs Pearl (again not a bad thing or a dig at the article, it legitimately takes more words to explain Nockchain given the complexity)

So you get left in a few kinda awkward spots with respect to Nockchain:

1. Is Nockchain trying to be an AI money like Pearl? They've clearly identified AI compute as the next trend to ride and are spending a bunch of time developing and narrating about it (again, not a bad thing)

For many reasons I obviously don't think Nockchain is money: It's too complex (Bitcoin and Zcash may be technically complicated but architecturally and memetically they are simple), The NockVM introduces programmability which is -EV for moneyness, & it's not pure (I can see MatMul Bitcoin being AI Money, it's harder to see zkp verifiable compute being AI Money)

> I believe there's two rational points of disagreement with me. 1a, Maybe you think Nock is something other than money. Fair enough, in that environment I agree Nock & Pearl are not competitive, you can own both so long as you have your own thesis for underwriting Nock as a money making protocol rather than a money protocol. 1b, Maybe you think Nock is money but disagree with my definition of money. Again, fair enough but obviously I agree with myself instead of you

2. If Nockchain is not AI money like Pearl, then what is it? To me it seems most similar to Ethereum but designed around the paradigm of verifiable compute. That really is cool and interesting, but it comes with all the problems I believe Ethereum has: Blockspace is a commodity it's hard to see proving networks not being commoditized if they become super relevant, The network can charge based on throughput but not value (it's more like the post office than an exchange), and Interoperability makes vamp attacks that kill Lindy too viable

⭐️ So why does it matter? Why am I hating?

If Nock is money, then we're playing a zero sum game. Look a the zec/xmr chart, the market is learning how to price money & you don't want to be hold the wrong one

If Nock is something else then I'm not really hating, I'm just being kinda inflammatory. I genuinely think what they're building is conceptually cool and an experiment worth building. I'm just not a buyer for now

I hope they do what is best for themselves and their users.

text:
🧐慢雾 CISO 推测 Ledger 设备被攻击路径：旁路录屏助记词后再外传

慢雾 @SlowMist_Team  安全首席信息安全官 @im23pds  发推表示，若如 Mt.Gox 前首席执行官 Mark Karpelès 所说 Ledger 改动发生在 PCB 上，则属高水平手法。

其推测流程为：种子在安全元件内生成，助记词显示在屏幕上，恶意模块接入屏幕数据线（如 SPI），录下显示的单词，凑齐后通过 LTE 或 eSIM 发出，攻击者取得助记词后转走资产。

此前，Mt.Gox 前首席执行官 Mark Karpelès 发推表示，其收到的一台 Ledger 硬件钱包疑似被植入间谍模块，设备来自马来西亚，外包装热缩膜完好，拆开后也难以立即发现异常，植入物隐藏在屏幕原本应有的缓冲垫位置。

该模块包含 LTE 通信组件、天线、eSIM 及连接 Ledger SPI 总线的微控制器，可分析设备向用户显示的字符，并在助记词设置完成后发送相关数据。攻击者可能监控受害者的钱包地址，并选择时机转移资产。

text:
这期币安会客厅的含金量很高啊，邀请的是叶檀老师

一些原生加密玩家可能不了解叶檀老师，她很厉害的，曾任《每日经济新闻》主笔、《每日经济新闻》首席评论员

这家媒体是中国财经第一梯队中极具硬核实力与行业影响力的顶级媒体，全网粉丝超过一亿

叶檀老师，“江湖人”送了她一个颇具魅力的称呼“财经女侠”

综合听下来，叶檀老师很谦虚，有些发言真的振聋发聩

接下来我整理了本次采访的核心发言给大家：

1、真正的勇气从来不是大开大合，而是细水长流

这点对于加密行业同样适用，只是我们换了一个说法“不下牌桌”

2、别人眼里的成功未必是成功，大家都需要给自己设定一个标准。每个人成功的标准都不一样，成功从来不应该只以财富衡量

这点颇有感触，对于当年年轻人来说，有车有房结婚生娃是成功么？也许过自己喜欢的生活才是成功

对于 @cz_binance 大表哥来说，所谓的某某财富榜是成功么？我觉得不是，更多的大表哥想是为了推动加密行业和教育在世界的普及吧

从开的是日产尼桑就能看出来，按照大表哥的身价，开什么劳斯莱斯，什么迈凯轮都不在话下吧，但是不需要

3、对于选择一个行业创业，不是出于财富的需求，而是因为热爱和擅长

4、房地产不再是一个投资品种，而是生活的必须消费品很重要

衣食住行，住很重要，只是房子不再是金融属性了

5、投资需要找到一个适合自己能力和自己个性的投资方式

有的人短线为王，有的人长线发财，有的人Meme大神，每个人都有自己的赚钱方式，投资逻辑

要做到知行合一

text:
so about the $86m ledger drain. everyone’s screaming “ledger got hacked” again. i spent the evening digging and it’s dumber and scarier than that

there’s a shop in malaysia called cryptobilis that sells hardware wallets. ledger has it listed as an official authorized reseller since at least 2022, for malaysia, indonesia and the philippines. legit shop, real devices, years of normal customers

this spring the founders sell it. the deal comes with an NDA: they can’t tell anyone about the sale until october 19

by august the company registry shows one owner with 100%. some guy from heilongjiang, china

the shop keeps running like nothing happened. the site, the name and the “authorized by ledger” badge all stay up

then on oct 8 @MagicalTux posts photos of a ledger he cracked open. hidden under the screen there’s an extra little board with an LTE modem and an eSIM. it just watches the display. you set up your wallet, your 24 words show up, and they get sent out over mobile data. ledger’s genuine check doesn’t catch it because the actual ledger chip is real. his device came from malaysia

https://t.co/vRuBM0xIfR

that post does 120k views

22 hours later someone sweeps everything. 203 BTC hits two addresses in literally one block. ~$58m USDT moves on tron in the same hour. i added up all the wallets: ~$91m

about 7 hours after that ledger says “we’re investigating” and asks cryptobilis to pause sales

cryptobilis is still on ledger’s site as an authorized reseller

to be fair, nobody has officially tied the new owner to the bugged devices yet, and ledger hasn’t confirmed how it happened. but read it as a business plan:

get authorized, sell real stuff for years, quietly sell the company under an NDA, keep the badge, ship devices that phone home, then drain everything the second someone notices

and was ledger even told the shop got sold? nobody’s said so

“authorized reseller” means ledger trusted whoever ran the shop back in 2022. says nothing about who runs it today

bought your hardware wallet anywhere but the manufacturer? open it up today, ledger literally has a guide for that. then move to a fresh seed on a device bought direct

wonder who’s going to answer for this: the chinese frontman from heilongjiang, the shop’s previous owners, or ledger itself

@Ledger clearly needs to keep a much closer eye on who they call official resellers, and take way more responsibility for who sells their devices and how

author: alexolegimas
quoted_text:
New essay for the @GoogleDeepMind Institute with James Manyika on AI x Science, "Bending the Curve of Discovery".

While accelerating existing scientific practices is certainly useful, the real promise of AI is its potential to act as an invention of a method of invention (IMI) a la Griliches--e.g., the microscope or statistical inference--which would unlock questions and whole modes of discovery that were previously beyond human reach.

Today, LLMs and specialized models like AlphaFold act as economic complements. LLMs handle analysis, coding, and writing, while specialized tools handle domain-specific predictions. Most handoffs between them run through the scientist.

What may the future of science look like? LLMs orchestrating those handoffs automatically--prompting specialized models, auditing outputs, and looping until either the question is answered or a non-automated stage is reached (e.g., wet lab testing). The scientist's role shifts from running each step to designing this loop. We saw a glimpse of this workflow with Anthropic’s enzyme discovery a few weeks ago, and we're seeing this in our own work too.

This raises foundational epistemic questions:

1. What will scientific understanding look like when discoveries are made by black-box models whose output is increasingly difficult to interpret?
2. How do we extract underlying mechanisms, not just outputs, as science becomes more automated? What will theory look like?
3. If AI automates the writing and junior lab work, how do we train the next generation of scientists to push the frontier?
4. What will motivate scientists in this epistemic reality?

There's an economics angle too. Hypothesis generation gets cheap, so bottlenecks move downstream to verification and to choosing which questions are worth asking. Realizing AI’s full potential will take investment in infrastructure and institutional reform--making this as much an organizational challenge as a technical one

We don't have the answers yet, and I'd love to hear what others think.

我想说 Gemini 3.8 Flash High 是当前优化产品以及官网文案内容最好的模型，推荐有需求的小伙伴去试试。

由于这几天我的Claude 以及 Codex 额度 以及好几个 Reset 都用完了，但是还有些事情要做，翻出了半年前当时 199 刀包的一年的 Gemini AI，甚至都快忘记了，也想着不抱太大希望去看看谷歌的模型效果有没有进步，于是下载了一个 Antigravity，直接设置当前能设置的最好的这个。

让他去帮我优化 Mole Mac 的一些文案，想着让各个国家的内容尽可能简单、清晰、易懂，输入非常简单的诉求，他就开始干活了，速度很快，文案优化给到了优化前、优化后和原因，仔细看了看，相比之前 GPT 和 Claude 最好模型优化的好了不少，让我听惊讶，语言很顺畅、真实、清晰，不文绉绉，也没有 AI 那个味道，让我感觉真好，虽然在 Coding 上差了点，居然在文案表达上这么好。

20刀每月的居然还挺耐用，我让他帮我优化了 Mole 的官网、 App 设置项、优化项、清理项，提示文案、描述文案各种，感觉之前我手写的的确有不少没有那么好懂清晰，换成这个以后，真有一个你请了一个语文老师做到你的旁边帮你考虑小白用户如何更好理解你产品的思路来优化，帮我做了很多事情。

我居然对优化文案上瘾了，然后我又包了一个20刀的账号，继续使用，一个用完，另外一个刚好重置，把我之前一些产品不好懂的文案、描述几乎全部优化了一遍，包括各种开源的 Readme，非常爽，也非常喜欢，算是找到了用武之地了。

假如你也有类似诉求，非常推荐你把尘封很久的 Gemini 拿出来试试，会让你很惊喜的，可以让他输出前后对比以及原因，先让你check，让他追求简单、清晰、易懂，不AI语气的方式来弄，非常非常不错。

text:
又一批用硬件钱包的倒霉蛋被盗了【图1】，
我不理解那些用硬件钱包的人，
硬件钱包完全就是一个黑盒，
鬼知道里面有什么问题。

开发商、经销商都可以做手脚，
哪怕开发商不作恶，
都可能出现弱私钥的问题。
（例如最近Coinkite的Coldcard）

要安全存币，
关键是方案的选择，
连冷钱包都不是必要的。

比如最常见的方案：
一个恢复了出厂设置的旧手机，
（重装了干净系统/用U盘PE启动 的电脑也可）
然后从官方网站下载官方推荐钱包，
选使用人数最多的那个推荐钱包，
这样检查的技术人员最多，
懂编程的还可以自己下载源代码编译。

然后这台 手机/电脑 就专机专用，
其它任何app、软件都不能安装，
钱包能用时也别升级，
平时关机，只有转币时才开机，
没有任何黑客可以入侵一台关机的设备，
这样安全性和冷钱包没什么差别。
当然别忘了 加密/离线 备份好私钥，
或者用脑钱包等不会遗忘的私钥方案。

专机专用还包括不能再装其它钱包，
（尤其是山寨币的钱包）
如果非要装的话，
就每个钱包都开一个虚拟机装，
每个钱包都分别隔离开。

检查软件钱包有没有问题，
可比检查硬件钱包方便多了，
真正做了验证的人也多。

经销商可以很轻易对硬件钱包动手脚，
黑客虽然理论上也可以攻破钱包网站，
把对下载文件动手脚，
但这种公开攻击容易被发现，
不会出现你用了个动手脚的硬件钱包，
还浑然不知的情况。

硬件钱包不是更安全，
而是更不可验证、更危险。
停止使用黑盒硬件钱包，
改为使用安全设备+可验证软件钱包。

text:
Which of my personal agents was proactive in the right ways?

Most of my friends wouldn’t trust an AI agent with access to their personal email and calendar.

But in service of laziness (and science!), I gave a few agents read access to mine to see what they'd do without prompting.

✅ dot caught that I'd put a doctor's appointment on my calendar for the wrong day. It noticed that an appointment confirmation email I’d just received did not match what was in my calendar.
❌ That same day, Muse sent me a redundant notification about a stranger tagging me on someone else's GitHub gist. My GitHub handle is @.michelle, so I get mistakenly tagged by strangers all the time. Muse also surfaced the appointment confirmation email, but missed the date mismatch.
🟡 GrokBot hasn't notified me about anything to date. To be fair, I haven't asked it to, and silence is arguably better than what Muse is doing.

Useful proactivity > leaving me alone >>> noisy proactivity.

It was cool that dot looked across multiple sources to figure out what was worthy of a push notification.

text:
Assorted things I've been mulling over regarding agents in the economy:

• Companies are in some sense the original superintelligence. It's often the case that they can use their amortized cognitive surplus to advance their interests against those of certain consumers: relative to the optimization capacity of companies, consumers can be inattentive, underinformed, irrational, etc. (Think, say, of some of the classic insurance upsells at the end of a booking process, which is typically priced substantially above what a regular policy would cost.) Herbert Simon introduced the idea of bounded rationality, and firms often end up benefiting from it. Thanks to personal agents, we will probably get somewhat more rational in how we engage with companies.

• How exactly will outcomes change? Well, certain kinds of price discrimination will work less well (how do coupons work if every agent hunts fastidiously for them?), and certain kinds of customer cross-subsidy will change (today, people who forget to cancel subscriptions subsidize those who don't). Taken across the economy as a whole, I'm not sure what the incidence of all of this will be.

• In corporate strategy, people have long debated the relative importance of distribution and product quality. Perhaps you've made something better, but does anyone know about it? Won't people just continue to buy the ACME Corp Mousetraps? Personal agents will, I think, act as a kind of structural subsidy for product quality. How would markets look different if individuals always spent at least 10 hours researching their purchases? On the margin, focusing on making a product better is, I think, going to become a more effective strategy for companies. This is good!

• It true, a corollary is that information about product quality will become more important and impactful. Today, most people have very limited ability to aggregate and integrate such data, but agents will have insatiable thirst for such signals. (It's often said that data is becoming more valuable because it helps in the training of models. That's obviously true, but I think there's a secondary way in which it's more valuable simply as a complement to cheaper intelligence.)

• A big question is whether agents will increase superstar effects (rational agents all settle on the same product) or increase dispersion (because everyone has slightly different tastes and preferences, which agents are good at eliciting, finally overcoming the artificial clustering we've been subjected to).

• Many internet companies have monetized demand routing, which is in turn often predicated on short attention spans. "I'll click on the first thing I see." This has led to some amount of inefficiency, as companies try to propitiate capricious ranking algorithms and incur various placement fees. It's not all deadweight loss (willingness to pay is itself a kind of signal, which is valuable to buyers), but it's not great. How will the nature and value of this routing change in a world of personal agents? I don't know the answer, but I think that the effects might be pretty big.

• Much of what I'm writing hinges on the assumption that personal agents will be on the consumer's side. I suspect that that will be the winning strategy, but whether it's true, and what it means to be true, involves a lot of other questions.

Taken as a whole, the market is a massively parallelized, decentralized, and highly imperfect value attribution machine, and, taking stock of all of the effects, it seems to me that the quality point may well be the biggest: that agents will change the nature of the backpropagation such that the rewards for better products increase. Maybe this is too optimistic, but I suspect (and hope) that companies that make things that they're proud of will feel that the universe is a little more partisan in their favor.

🧐慢雾 CISO 推测 Ledger 设备被攻击路径：旁路录屏助记词后再外传

慢雾 @SlowMist_Team  安全首席信息安全官 @im23pds  发推表示，若如 Mt.Gox 前首席执行官 Mark Karpelès 所说 Ledger 改动发生在 PCB 上，则属高水平手法。

其推测流程为：种子在安全元件内生成，助记词显示在屏幕上，恶意模块接入屏幕数据线（如 SPI），录下显示的单词，凑齐后通过 LTE 或 eSIM 发出，攻击者取得助记词后转走资产。

此前，Mt.Gox 前首席执行官 Mark Karpelès 发推表示，其收到的一台 Ledger 硬件钱包疑似被植入间谍模块，设备来自马来西亚，外包装热缩膜完好，拆开后也难以立即发现异常，植入物隐藏在屏幕原本应有的缓冲垫位置。

该模块包含 LTE 通信组件、天线、eSIM 及连接 Ledger SPI 总线的微控制器，可分析设备向用户显示的字符，并在助记词设置完成后发送相关数据。攻击者可能监控受害者的钱包地址，并选择时机转移资产。

text:
Let's talk about $JEANPHIL and $CLAUDIA, and why I'm bullish on the AI Influencer + short-form video narrative.

GTBxUiw6wJdmmkCGZgRHLyYxqu1vG4KtRpeox6yDpump 
2j5SaS7xy776qCBpyPQbZjyQSAtKiFgrwjfErthnW2ZM 

First, the broader sector.

I believe AI Influencers combined with short-form video distribution could become one of the narratives worth watching in the next Meme market cycle.

The underlying logic is simple: AI is turning character creation from a high-cost, low-frequency process into a low-cost, scalable content business that can be operated continuously. In the past, building an influencer required appearance, performance, filming, editing, and long-term management. Now, creators can use AI to design characters, develop personalities, produce short videos, and even operate multiple virtual personas simultaneously.

But what really matters isn't how many characters AI can generate. It's whether those characters can consistently produce content that people want to watch, discuss, and follow.

Short-form video drives distribution, characters accumulate attention, and Memes can become a speculative vehicle for that attention in the crypto market. An AI character can build a distinctive persona through continuous video releases, participate in trending topics, create new memes, and interact with other characters, gradually evolving from a single viral clip into a recognizable IP.

Compared with traditional Memes that rely on an isolated event or a single image, these characters theoretically have the ability to continuously generate new material for distribution. If a character develops a stable audience and cultural recognition, it no longer has to rely entirely on a single viral moment to maintain attention.

If this model gains traction in the crypto market, speculation may shift beyond the next viral image toward AI characters that have already attracted genuine attention on platforms like TikTok and Instagram, can consistently produce content, and have the potential to channel that external attention on-chain.

This is why I've chosen to take a deeper look at JEANPHIL and CLAUDIA. They represent two different paths within this emerging narrative.

JEANPHIL: External traction that has already emerged.

Jean Phil is an AI-generated French male character. His blond bowl cut, curled mustache, brown houndstooth suit, and signature street-style boxing moves create a recognizable visual identity that is easy to imitate.

The character has attracted significant attention on TikTok and Instagram, generating imitations and derivative content. This demonstrates how an AI character with a distinctive persona and a simple, replicable video format can quickly capture attention on mainstream social platforms.

The logic is straightforward: the character attracts external traffic, the content inspires imitations and remixes, and that attention may eventually flow into its on-chain token.

Compared with Memes that rely solely on narratives originating within crypto, JEANPHIL already has an external source of attention. What it needs to prove next is whether that momentum can persist and whether the character's popularity can translate into sustained token demand.

CLAUDIA: From AI creation toward long-term IP development.

CLAUDIA is more focused on long-term IP development. Around Claudia, anabology has been building Claudia Gallery and proposed creating an open version of Hatsune Miku for the AI era. Related initiatives also include AI character creation tools, Agent Skills, and Claudia Local.

The Influencer mode brings this vision closer to the AI Influencer model: by continuously producing videos, maintaining a consistent character identity, and experimenting with high-frequency publishing, it aims to gradually build its own audience.

The logic is that AI lowers content production costs, continuous video output helps establish character recognition, and the character gradually accumulates an audience before attempting to convert that external attention into IP influence and on-chain interest.

Compared with JEANPHIL, CLAUDIA has greater potential in the direction of a long-term AI creator ecosystem. The goal isn't simply to make a character go viral in the short term, but to explore how an AI character can continuously produce content, build an audience, and develop into an expandable, open IP.

However, this path has a longer chain of validation. Being able to produce videos consistently doesn't mean the content will necessarily gain traction. Having creation tools doesn't guarantee the ability to build a successful character. And an open-IP vision doesn't automatically mean the token can capture the resulting value.

Although both projects fall under the broader AI Influencer narrative, their trading theses are different.

JEANPHIL is more focused on existing external traction. The key question is whether that attention can persist and translate into token demand. CLAUDIA is more focused on AI creation capabilities and long-term IP development. The key question is whether it can consistently produce compelling content and build a genuine audience.

What I'm bullish on is the shared potential behind both approaches: AI characters could evolve beyond static images into dynamic IPs that continuously produce content, participate in trending topics, build social relationships, and generate new Memes.

Of course, a compelling sector narrative doesn't mean every related token will appreciate.

We need to distinguish three separate outcomes: an AI character gaining attention, an IP building lasting influence, and a token capturing value from that influence. A character can become popular without benefiting its token. A project can have impressive creation tools without producing viral content. Even if an IP continues to grow, attention may remain entirely off-chain if the token has no meaningful connection to its development.

Therefore, what I'm really looking for isn't the first token to announce that it uses AI, but projects that have demonstrated their ability to attract external attention, consistently produce distributable content, and establish a clear connection between that attention and their tokens.

AI is the production tool, short-form video is the distribution channel, character IP is the vehicle for attention, and the token represents a separate speculative market.

When these four elements become genuinely connected, AI Influencers could evolve from a trending concept into a new Meme narrative with sustained distribution potential.

In my view, the projects most likely to break out will need a distinctive character identity, consistent content distribution, a genuine external audience, and a mechanism for translating attention into token demand. That's why I'm bullish on this direction and have chosen to take a deeper look at JEANPHIL and CLAUDIA.

quoted_text:
Isaiah, after everything we’ve been through together I’m surprised that you would publicize our disagreement in this fashion. But since you have created public interest in this, it is important that people should hear both sides of the story.

Day One has been a major investor in Valar from the beginning, and we have never wavered in our belief that the company will be a success. This faith and support in our founders is why fourteen Day One founders have become limited partners in Day One’s most recent fund.

In 2024, Day One invested in Valar’s seed round. Later that year, Valar required a seed extension after miscalculations by management regarding the capital needs of the business. Day One stepped in to provide this seed extension, saving the company in a difficult time.

When it came time to raise a Series A, Valar spent several weeks on the market without success. At Valar’s request, Day One then offered the first term sheet and co-led the Series A, again saving the company during a time when deep tech startups in highly regulated industries were a difficult sell in venture capital.

Then when Valar needed a Series A extension, Isaiah asked that Day One waive our pro rata rights so as to make a tenuous financing deal work out. We agreed for the good of the company.

As part of these transactions, Valar agreed that, if their long-shot effort to build nuclear energy as a startup did succeed, Day One would have rights to participate in future rounds that could not be eliminated without Day One’s consent. This was a fair bargain at a time when Day One took extraordinary risks by betting against the market when Valar’s future appeared highly uncertain. Following the achievement of criticality on June 18th, our faith has been validated. Valar went from being an obscure company to a hot startup. We congratulate the Valar team on their hard won success!

Of course, when it came time for Valar to raise a Series B after achieving such success, Day One expected to participate in that round – as both parties had agreed. But at this point the normally positive communications between Day One and Valar took a negative turn. Valar insisted that Day One give up all of its future pro rata rights despite the parties’ agreements, and despite four out of six major investors participating in the Series B round without waiving. This went against both the letter and the spirit of our deal, so we did not agree. In decades of investing we have waived pro-rata rights dozens of times, but no other company has ever demanded that we give up all of our rights for all future rounds.

We told Isaiah we would give up a majority of our pro-rata in the Series B round so as to not make his life difficult, to which he responded “You cannot make my life difficult, I can make your life difficult.”  It was at this point that we sought representation with Quinn Emanuel to protect the firm and the interests of our limited partners.

Day One has since learned of a significant secondary equity sale by Isaiah from which we were excluded. Our attempts to gain insights into this through our information rights have been stymied by Valar management, who have refused to produce material documents requested by Day One. After weeks of delay on these documents, Valar management alerted us this Wednesday that they intend to pursue legal action against Day One unless we waive our legal rights forever.

We have always pursued positive and mutually beneficial relationships with all of our portfolio companies. We have neither taken nor threatened legal action against Valar, and in fact we told them explicitly that we have no interest in doing so. Valar voluntarily entered into a contract with Day One, then violated that contract, and is now suing Day One. 

We are deeply disappointed by this recent erratic turn, but are still proud of our early and continued support of Valar.  We look forward to the clarity from the courts that Valar’s management is seeking.

text:
Khosla Ventures 刚刚领投了 Sabi 的 5000 万美元种子轮，Accel、Initialized、DST Global 和 OpenAI 前 CPO Kevin Weil 也参与了。这家公司的估值已经达到 6 亿美元。

他们要造一顶可以「读心」的棒球帽。

帽子里集成了大量微型脑电传感器，配合一个用超过 10 万小时神经数据训练的 Brain Foundation Model。理想情况下，你只需要在脑子里默念一句话，AI 就能收到对应的 Prompt，进一步交给 Agent 执行。

我觉得这件事非常值得关注，因为 AI Agent 的发展正在让人类自己成为整个计算系统里最慢的环节。

过去脑机接口最重要的应用是医疗，帮助瘫痪患者重新获得控制设备的能力。现在 Sabi 开始瞄准普通消费者，试图让所有人都跳过键盘、鼠标，甚至语言。

当 AI 只能聊天时，人类打字慢一点无所谓。但如果未来一个 Agent 可以同时完成几十项任务，等待人类逐条输入指令，似乎就成了一种浪费。

不过技术离这个愿景还有相当大的距离。Sabi 创始人声称，早期有线头盔原型在使用者经过两周以上适应后，实验室最高思维转录准确率达到 77%。真正可日常佩戴的产品还没有经过独立验证。

而且我觉得，这里面有一个比技术准确率更值得讨论的问题。

人脑里的念头，究竟有多少是真正的意图？

我们每天都会冒出大量想法，很多想法甚至在形成语言之前就已经被自己否定了。打字和说话虽然低效，却天然提供了一个筛选过程。你得先想清楚，再把它变成一条明确的指令。

Sabi 目前强调的是有意识的默念和经过训练的指令，但它更远期的目标已经包括预测意图。随着 Agent 获得越来越多的执行权限，这件事会变得相当微妙。

大模型的幻觉问题还没解决，硅谷又开始尝试让模型猜测人类的想法。

以前 AI 会编造事实，以后它可能还会编造你的意图。

下一代人机交互最大的挑战，可能恰恰是如何保留人类犹豫、反悔和拒绝的权利。

毕竟，让机器知道你在想什么很困难，让机器知道哪些念头不该当真，恐怕更困难。

text:
Valar is good for America

Day One is bad for America. 

These things were true when Day One wrote their first check. Neither is here nor there however in this dispute as framed by Isaiah. Instead the framing is purely about contractual rights so that is how I will comment on it. 

Venture is a hard business. A very hard business. 75% of firms shouldn’t exist and won’t in the next cycle. There will be a new crop behind them and 75%+ of those will also fail. 

For some firms when they find the rare winner in their portfolio, they NEED to double down on that winner to build the returns that will justify their continued existence. 

Hence the existence of pro rata RIGHTS. The pre negotiated right to invest more money and maintain ownership. 

We can argue all day long about whether the right should be standard. I for one feel like we should earn our position on cap tables through work and good partnership. However, the argument over “should” is irrelevant when the right has already been negotiated and agreed upon. 

In theory when those rights exist, they’ve already been bought and paid for. The valuation assumes the existence of pro-rata rights in the number. The shares purchased are worth X without pro-rata rights and are worth X+Y with pro-rata rights. When an investor pays X+Y, they're relying on the value of Y. Having Y deleted by the company and other investors is… frustrating to say the least. Having it deleted when it’s your biggest career winning investment is doubly so. Having it deleted when it’s your biggest career winner while other investors are permitted to exercise their pro-rata is devastating. 

(Now as I said, Day One is bad for America and I think they should have never been allowed to invest but we have no magic wand so here we are talking about contractual rights instead of FOCI concerns for a business working in a strategic field and hoping to sell to USG). 

When you strip those rights away ex post, you are literally stripping value out of the fund who purchased those rights. 

If you don’t want to honor pro-rata rights, dont include them when you raise the round. The only thing worse than re-trading a deal is re-trading a deal that was closed years ago. 

Again, I generally agree that pro rata rights and spring back rights should be reconsidered generally and that firms should earn the right to continue to invest. I’ll also acknowledge that the fact the rights can be waived means that when all agreed to the rights existence waiver was always a possibility that should have also been priced in.   That said, the existence of the rights in the first place set expectations and expectations are important. My word is my bond. Honoring one’s commitments is important. It’s what American enterprise is based on. 

If this conflict ends up with Masha being expunged from the cap table I’m happy as an American but as someone who plays in a brutally competitive business, fights hard for my portfolio, and plays by the rules with integrity, it kills my soul to see an argument like this laid out for re-trading deals. It’s terrible for the ecosystem and it’s not a good look for anyone. 

Mean what you say and say what you mean. (And partner with good people). That’s how we win 🇺🇸

昨天在新加坡机场，连接了一个看起来很像机场官方的免费WiFi，后来发现钱包里的3.7个BNB不翼而飞，连剩下的USDC也没能保住。

虽然目前还不能确定是不是WiFi的问题，但这次确实给自己提了个醒。

说起来，在币圈混了九年多，也不是第一次被盗了。

2022年，我就曾经稀里糊涂地点进一个空投钓鱼网站，还傻乎乎地给人家授权了，结果被盗了价值20万美元的资产。那次真的是花钱买了个惨痛的教训。

经历过那次事情后，我也明白了一个道理：链上资产一旦被盗，想要追回来，实在太难了。

所以这次发现资产被盗后，我基本没抱什么希望。

只是发了一条推文，提醒大家在外面使用公共WiFi时多注意安全，也希望其他朋友能够引以为戒。

没想到，今天下午事情居然出现了神奇的反转！

下午好友TC @TC8880 
和李阳突然联系我，说Ave官方正在找我。

当时我还有点纳闷，Ave找我干什么？😂

结果一问才知道，原来是 @aveai_info 
Ave官方关注到了我的盗币事件，
主动通过共同好友找到我，
而且还带来了一个好消息：

昨天被盗的资产，竟然被他们帮忙追回来了！

说实话，听到这个消息的时候，我真的挺意外，也挺感动的。

毕竟我没有主动找Ave求助，更没有想过会有人帮我追回这笔钱。

但他们看到了这件事，不仅没有袖手旁观，还主动想办法联系我，帮助我解决问题。

这种意料之外的帮助，真的让人心里暖暖的。
